a_rows_sample.anchor: The seven-context strategic model is the authoritative architecture model ... ADR-AIP-01's frozen six-context table is hereby amended
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB formally accepts the seven-context strategic model (Landscape v2, Context Map v2, Capability Map v2), which amends ADR-AIP-01's previously frozen six-context table, recognizing BC-7 as a Supporting Subdomain with CAP-14.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Why ADR-AIP-04 stays frozen during this work ... BC-7 discovery may itself produce role-ownership evidence ... Starting ADR-AIP-04 before this landscape lands would mean designing roles before understanding their ownership.
b_rows_sample.statement: A principled reason is given for freezing ADR-AIP-04 (role-model ownership) during BC-7's strategic discovery: the discovery itself may surface evidence about whether Role/Assignment/Actor/Authority belong partly to BC-7, so deciding roles first would risk designing them before their ownership is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation · code changes · component movement · workflow_engine changes · ADR-AIP-04 decision · role-model ownership decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: The commission's forbidden-classes list mechanically excludes implementation, the workflow_engine itself, and any ADR-AIP-04/role-model decision from this tactical discovery work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Python Stage-2 verification → portfolio quiet → ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery → role/capability consequences → Implementation Architecture → Implementation.
b_rows_sample.statement: The ARB's registered sequencing determination orders remaining platform work: finish Python Stage-2 verification, quiet the portfolio, then run ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery before any implementation architecture, with the architectural reason recorded that beginning implementation first risks encoding an incomplete role model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-AIP-04 must NOT be framed as 'let's add a Knowledge Engineer and a Communication Engineer.' ... What capabilities does a sustainable AI Engineering Platform require?
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability-first guard is registered before ADR-AIP-04 discovery is even commissioned: the governing question must stay 'what capabilities does a sustainable AI engineering platform require', evaluated strictly in the order capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, never role-first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the governing question is "what capabilities does a sustainable AI Engineering Platform require?", evaluated capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, with people and agents last.
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability-first discovery guard is registered before the ADR-AIP-04 commission exists: the discovery must proceed strictly in order capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, placing people and agents last.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation: commission ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery first -- it is the first-named purpose, its guard is already registered, and the BC-7 role-model question has been formally deferred to it since 2026-08-17.
b_rows_sample.statement: ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery is recommended as Track 2's first commissioned work item, because BC-7's role-model ownership question (Stage-2 OQ-5) was already formally deferred to it on 2026-08-17.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine the capabilities required for a sustainable session-based AI Engineering Operating System *before* formalizing or extending the role model.
b_rows_sample.statement: The purpose of the ADR-AIP-04 commission is to determine required capabilities before formalizing or extending any role model; it is a discovery/architecture item and does not authorize implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every important statement classified OBSERVED - INFERRED - PROPOSED - DECIDED - OPEN. Do not turn a proposal into a decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: A five-value classification discipline (OBSERVED, INFERRED, PROPOSED, DECIDED, OPEN) is mandated for every important statement in the ADR-AIP-04 deliverable, with an explicit prohibition against silently promoting a proposal to a decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-AIP-04 -- Capability Discovery Proposal, seventeen sections: Context ... Capability Inventory ... Ownership Analysis ... Invariants ... Role/Stewardship Analysis ... Candidate Contexts or Stewardships ... Open Questions ... PO/ARB Decisions Required.
b_rows_sample.statement: A fixed seventeen-section deliverable structure is mandated for the ADR-AIP-04 discovery proposal, spanning context through to PO/ARB decisions required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RETURNED FOR MATERIAL CORRECTION ... The verification question was: is this sufficiently justified to be placed before PO/ARB for decision? On E and I -- not yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery proposal is returned for material correction on two evidence claims (six-role hypothesis, C-14 status) while its DDD discipline, mechanism evidence, and refusal to promote C-19 to a bounded context are found to survive independent falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Whether the discovery independently converged or reconstructed an unread source CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED. ... Classification: OPEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Because the discovery's Section 13 stewardship reading materially matches the untracked document's 'Option B', but I-did-not-read-it is a self-declared and unattestable claim, the question of independent convergence vs reconstruction from an unread source is classified OPEN, and the convergence must not be counted as corroboration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Amendment 1 declares NO producing process. ... Its authorship is recoverable only by inference
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding W-4: Amendment 1 violates its own lane's requirement to disclose a producing process; its authorship is only inferable, and no correction assignment was ever registered for its production -- a governance/provenance defect distinct from the content defects.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION SUCCEEDED. THE DECISION SURFACE IS NOT YET CLEAN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict on Amendment 1: the corrective discipline succeeded in substance (no finding strengthened, no capability invented, nothing outside the proposal touched) but two defects (W-1's own recurrence of the truncated-search error; W-2's misplaced pointer) must land before the decision surface is clean for PO/ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: capability -> ownership -> bounded context / stewardship -> human role -> agent -> platform service -> technology
b_rows_sample.statement: The capability-first ordering is restated as the binding method for the entire discovery: capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> platform service -> technology, with the explicit prohibition on beginning from role creation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
b_rows_sample.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search AND an explicit statement of what was searched. ... a search that can be truncated is not a survey.
b_rows_sample.statement: Amendment 1's root-cause finding (A1.0): both verified defects (V-1, V-2) share one mechanism -- an absence claim resting on a truncated search or an ungeneralised narrow claim -- proposing a durable discipline that an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search plus an explicit statement of what was searched.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the evidence package has now been materially wrong three times about the same thing, and the honest summary is that this discovery has been better at DDD reasoning than at surveying its own estate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2's self-assessment: across the discovery, Amendment 1 and Correction #2, the same evidence-survey error class recurred three times, while the DDD reasoning method itself (capability-before-agent, parsimony, refusing role-inferred-capability) held; no finding is strengthened by Correction #2 and two (C-14, SB-3) end weaker than before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION ... Three material evidence errors in one work item is a real record. But the correction that matters most -- F-3'' -- replaced its basis rather than defending it
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery/Amendment 1/Correction 2 package is READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION -- ungoverned material is properly routed to OQ-I, inferred ownership is refused at every convenient point, and eleven actual architectural decisions remain, none pre-empted; two low-severity residuals (missing supersession markers) do not block.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-1 ... As of this decision that thesis is FALSE -- the model IS governed. What remains live in W-1 is the evidence-quality question
b_rows_sample.statement: The adoption decision retroactively supersedes the narrow thesis Verification #2's finding W-1 was testing ('the six-role model is not currently established as governed architecture'), because that thesis is now false by decision; the verdict-G re-scoping requires the still-pending Verification #3 lane to be redirected to the evidence-quality question rather than the adoption question itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
a_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
a_rows_sample.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_i: X ⇉ Y because one input can legitimately lead to multiple candidates. ... Determination=HighRisk may lead to: Decision1=Mitigate or Decision2=AcceptRisk depending on governance context. ... P(K|E)>0.95 might be sufficient in one domain. But another domain may require: P(K|E)>0.999. ... the threshold is a domain/governance rule, not a universal mathematical truth. ... It should not dictate: Probability>0.95 ⇒ Truth. That would be inappropriate architectural overreach.
b_rows_sample.statement: Models transitions T_i as relations (X ⇉ Y) rather than deterministic functions where multiple valid outcomes exist (e.g. Determination=HighRisk can lead to Decision=Mitigate or Decision=AcceptRisk depending on governance context); warns that any evidence-to-knowledge probability threshold (e.g. P(K|E)>0.95) is a domain/governance-set decision rule, not a universal mathematical truth, and that KnowledgeOS itself must not dictate a universal threshold (Probability>0.95=>Truth) -- 'inappropriate architectural overreach' -- but should only provide the machinery Evidence->Inference->DecisionRule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_i = <Source, Input, Predicate, Method, Evidence, Authority, Time, Output, Verdict>. ... Broken evidence chain: K ↚ E. Broken determination chain: D_t ↚ K. ... Broken feedback chain: O' ↛ E'. Each is independently diagnosable. ... CompleteChain(c) ... Assured(c) ⇒ CompleteChain(c) ... CompleteChain ⇏ CorrectModel. We need both: StructuralCompleteness and SemanticValidity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a per-transition assurance tuple A_i=<Source,Input,Predicate,Method,Evidence,Authority,Time,Output,Verdict> forming an assurance trail richer than an audit log, and an independently-diagnosable taxonomy of seven broken-chain conditions (broken evidence/determination/decision/authority/execution/outcome/feedback chains). Defines CompleteChain(c) (every required transition has known input, defined rule, required evidence, applicable authority, recorded result) with Assured(c)=>CompleteChain(c) for claims whose policy requires end-to-end traceability, but explicitly states CompleteChain does not imply CorrectModel (a perfectly complete chain can still encode a wrong conclusion), requiring both StructuralCompleteness and SemanticValidity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance = Structural + Epistemic + Governance. ... TemporalConsistency must be added ... A decision may have been valid then, even if the knowledge is no longer valid now. ... OperationalAssurance. ... Assurance = Structural + Epistemic + Temporal + Governance + Operational. ... we have constructed a multi-dimensional assurance system around a lifecycle.
b_rows_sample.statement: Builds up a five-dimensional model of architecture assurance incrementally -- Structural (are required relationships present), Epistemic (does evidence justify the claim, Evidence |- Claim), Governance (was the action legitimately authorized, Authority |- Action), Temporal (a decision valid THEN even if the knowledge is invalid NOW), Operational (did the authorized action actually happen as intended) -- yielding Assurance = Structural + Epistemic + Temporal + Governance + Operational (a conceptual composition, not arithmetic); concludes KnowledgeOS is 'a multi-dimensional assurance system around a lifecycle', with the workflow (O->E->K->D_t->D_c->A->X->R->O') and the assurance dimensions {S,E,T,G,O} kept distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
b_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

b_notations: Assurance = Structural + Epistemic + Temporal + Governance + Operational
T_i: X ⇉ Y (relations, not functions, for Evidence→Knowledge and Determination→Decision)

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: MATCH VERDICT: 6 of 8 agenda items delivered; 2 named and NOT delivered
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (a): Step 207's tail agenda for Step 208 lists eight items (contract composition, information preservation, semantic loss, version compatibility, monotonicity, contradiction, uncertainty propagation, provenance preservation) under the question 'can a chain of individually valid transformations produce an invalid or misleading conclusion?'. Step 208 delivers 6 of 8: version compatibility is NOT delivered (Version appears only as a tuple field; no compatibility relation between contract versions is defined) and uncertainty propagation is NOT delivered (Section 208.14 shows uncertainty being lost, but no composition rule for uncertainty through C_2 o C_1 is given, and the word 'propagation' never occurs in Step 208). Additionally the headline question is restated, not quoted: 207 asks about an 'invalid or misleading conclusion'; 208 asks only whether the chain is 'necessarily valid' -- 'misleading' is dropped entirely and never addressed as distinct from invalidity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 208 neither cites nor consumes Step 82 (Uncertainty Propagation)
b_rows_sample.statement: The corpus already contains a dedicated prior step, '# Step 82 — Uncertainty Propagation', whose own Section 1 states 'we now test whether our mathematical model remains correct when uncertainty passes through multiple layers' -- exactly the agenda item Step 207 assigned to Step 208. Step 208 both omits the item (uncertainty propagation) and omits the prior work that already addressed it, with zero citation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Answered from scratch: zero citations to Steps 048/050/058
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (b): machine grep of Step 208 (and all 8 in-scope files) for the prior corpus's answers to the same headline question -- Step 048's boxed 'LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness', Step 058's boxed 'CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition', and Step 050's Attack 5 ('semantic collision', PASS) -- finds zero matches anywhere in the band. Step 208 Section 208.13 re-derives the same proposition in new notation ('locally valid but globally invalid'), so the same proposition is now boxed four times in the corpus in four notations with zero cross-reference; under LATER != SUPERSEDING, Step 208 does not supersede 048 or 058, it duplicates them without knowing they exist. Step 208's Section 208.22 (contradiction propagation) and Section 208.15 (RichEvidence -> SimpleBoolean) likewise re-derive the ground of Step 050's Attack 2 and Attack 5 respectively, also uncited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: C_chain=C_3∘C_2∘C_1; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)); L(C)=I_required-I_preserved; SI(C,B)=True; Booleanization; KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 ('Semantic Contract Algebra') treats a DDD context contract as an information-preserving projection and defines: semantic sufficiency S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) relative to a receiving context's task; minimal sufficient contract; semantic projection pi; semantic loss L(C) = I_required - I_preserved; semantic integrity SI(C,B); the anti-pattern 'Booleanization' (collapsing rich epistemic state into a Boolean); contract temporal validity C(t); provenance composition P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple (Content, Meaning, Provenance, Validity, Version, EpistemicStatus); the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim ladder; Proposition as a first-class object; and a four-layer architecture split (Epistemic/Normative/Decisional/Operational).

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). 1 — We continue from Step 207.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 cites exactly one prior step by number (Step 207, 'we continue from...') and nothing else -- not Steps 048, 058, 050, or 082. Later response in scope: Step 208's SI non-compositionality (Section 208.12) is restated in Step 211 Section 211.5 as 'Component correctness ⇏ System correctness'; Step 208's L(C) (Section 208.10) reappears in Step 212 Section 212.19 as L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without Step 208's own caveat; Step 208's Section 208.14 example reappears in substance, uncredited, in Step 212 Section 212.20.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_RESOLVES / REVIVES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 resolves 6 of 8 of Step 207's agenda items and, unknowingly, revives already-boxed results from Steps 048 and 058. Definitionally: Booleanization, Suff(C,B,Task), semantic projection, and the four-layer split are CLEAR. The information measure I(.) is NOT DEFINED -- Section 208.3 writes an ordinal comparison I(A)<I(E) and Section 208.10 writes a difference L(C)=I_required-I_preserved while itself stating 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure' -- the measure is never defined and the operations are performed anyway. S_B ('the information necessary to perform its legitimate responsibility') is AMBIGUOUS because 'legitimate' is never defined, so S_B cannot be constructed for any concrete B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 208.3 (compounded at 208.10); SECOND DEFECT: Section 208.25's provenance equation
b_rows_sample.statement: DERIVATION VERDICT PARTIALLY_VALID. I(A)<I(E) presupposes a total order on information content; I_required-I_preserved presupposes an interval scale; neither is established (Section 208.10 explicitly declines to establish one, then uses the operations anyway) -- every downstream claim quantifying loss is conditional on repairing this. Second defect: P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation,' is either vacuous (if closure holds, P(A)∪P(E)=P(A)) or self-refuting (if it does not, provenance is not closed); it also excludes any provenance contributed by the governance act itself, directly conflicting with Step 209 Section 209.4's Final(D) ⇒ DecisionBasis(D) ∧ Authority(D) (see Contradiction #2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing in Step 208 reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: Computability ladder for Step 208's objects: Booleanization is DEFINED; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)) is DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (both S_B and I uninstantiated); L(C) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from COMPUTABLE by its own Section 208.10; the Contract Safety theorem (Section 208.37) is DEFINED but not DERIVED. Nothing in the file reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED (0 tests specified, 0 run); the nine review questions in Section 208.38 are a checklist, not tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG on framing, WEAK on inference; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: FAILS on the information measure
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistically, Section 208.6's sufficient-statistic analogy is immediately and correctly fenced ('this is an analogy, not a claim that DDD contracts are literally sufficient statistics') but left un-cashed (no Fisher-Neyman factorization or formal criterion transposed), and Section 208.23's handling of conflicting estimates is sound but uncited against prior statistical steps (025N, 082). Measurement-wise: I(.) has no declared scale type yet is compared (<) and subtracted (-) -- arithmetic NOT justified; result=0.91 in one block silently becomes confidence=0.91 in the very next (unjustified type conversion between a point estimate and a degree of belief); uncertainty=0.08 is silently converted into a symmetric +/-0.08 interval half-width in Step 210 Section 210.12, presupposing an unstated symmetric error distribution and coverage level; epistemic strength S(x) is compared with > (Section 208.9 forward) while Step 209 Section 209.21 later explicitly retracts any universal total ordering on the same kind of quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG — the best DDD content in the band; UBIQUITOUS-LANGUAGE: Evidence != Claim boxed, then violated two files later
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208's sufficiency-relative-to-responsibility (Section 208.4) is a correct, non-obvious Published-Language/conformist-boundary formulation; S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) ≪ I(A) (Section 208.5) is precisely the anti-Shared-Kernel constraint; Booleanization (Section 208.16) is a genuinely useful named anti-pattern; the four-layer split (Section 208.36) is a defensible strategic decomposition -- but none of it is mapped to Step 206's bounded contexts or Step 207's actual context contracts. Section 208.28 rules 'we should not collapse [Data/Information/Evidence/Assessment/KnowledgeClaim] into one generic object called Knowledge' -- a ruling violated two files later (Contradiction #1). Section 208.30 promotes Proposition to a first-class term; Section 208.29 boxes Evidence != Claim but gives it no owning context ('term without an owner').

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; UNDEFINED SYMBOLS in Step 208
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: a contract is total and deterministic; information is set-like so subset applies; S_B is knowable a priori. Hidden assumptions: that an information measure exists at all (Section 208.10 defers it and nothing in the band supplies one); that provenance sets are finite and mergeable (required by P(A)∪P(E), never stated); that Valid(C) (Section 208.2) and SI(C,B) (Section 208.12) are different predicates, though the text slides between them; that 'legitimate responsibility' (Section 208.4) is externally given, smuggling the governance model into the definition of sufficiency. Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 208
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement). Does not survive: L(C) as any quantity; I(A)<I(E) as a comparison; P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the Section 208.37 'provisional architectural theorem' (Sufficiency+Provenance+Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety), which is a definition dressed as an implication since Contract Safety is not independently defined -- not a theorem in any sense, a naming convention.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
b_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 208 load-bearing boxed claims: Semantic Sufficiency, the provisional Contract-Safety theorem, and the survivor 'zero loss of relevant meaning'
b_rows_sample.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 208, adjudicated: (1) 'Semantic Sufficiency: S_B⊆I(C(A))' -- the file's central definition, resting on the undefined I(.) and the undefined 'legitimate responsibility' in S_B. (2) 'Semantic Sufficiency + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety' -- self-labelled 'a provisional architectural theorem, not a mathematically proven theorem'; verifier judges it a stipulative definition of Contract Safety rather than an implication, since the consequent is not independently defined. (3) 'The objective is not zero information loss. The objective is zero loss of relevant meaning.' -- survives; the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement.

a_rows_sample.statement: Verification #2 (the phase-a-v1.1-correction-verification report) is found to have run under no recorded lane, grant, or START at all; its content is not disputed, but its independence cannot be attested from the record, which INV-ATTR-2 already predicts as a limitation.

a_rows_sample.statement: For a work item whose subject is evidence integrity, its own evidence chain is observed to be split unresolved across two documentation roots (docs/publicdigit/reviews and docs/knowledgeos/reviews), with the placement resolver returning no matching rule for this case; recorded as an observation only, with no files moved.

a_rows_sample.statement: Verification #3 confirms the N-1/N-2 correction did exactly what was authorized and nothing else, closing the entire Phase-A correction chain (Verification #1 -> v1.1 -> Verification #2 -> N-1/N-2 correction -> this report) with no outstanding verified defect.

a_rows_sample.statement: F-5 (whether KOS_MECHANISM_PATH may redirect the 'sole writer', and why AST-017/AST-018 use hard constants while AST-019 does not) is explicitly held outside REPAIR-001 pending a separate Architecture decision -- must not be fixed, mitigated, or documented away inside the repair, since a correctness slice silently settling an architecture question is a category slippage the estate forbids; ASD-001 is preserved as a recorded sequencing defect (not reopened/remedied/erased), found to be the same defect class as F-1 from opposite directions (O-3); verification history (seq 1-4) stays untouched; the adopted parent layers L1+L2+L3's byte-integrity is stated as an acceptance criterion of REPAIR-001, not an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence requirements differ by role -- kept separate deliberately
a_rows_sample.statement: Independence bars differ by role and are kept separate deliberately: the REPAIR-001 implementer is barred only from being the verifier (must not repair what it verified, R-34/EP-02) or the governance process that scoped the slice, while the original AST-019 producer is explicitly NOT categorically barred from implementing (repairing one's own code is ordinary engineering); re-verification afterwards bars the first verifier, the producer, the scoping governance process, AND whoever implements REPAIR-001, since independence from the work under check is what makes the check worth anything -- collapsing verification-role bars onto implementation-role bars would shrink the eligible pool for no governed reason.

a_rows_sample.anchor: declaration-only prompt. This is NOT the repair commission.
a_rows_sample.statement: A two-phase actor-onboarding pattern is used: Phase 1 is a declaration-only prompt in which a candidate determines its own process identity from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and discloses independence before reading any subject material; Phase 2 (the actual repair commission) issues only after appointment, human START, and an approved EP-01 plan -- explicitly designed so a declaration arriving with a plan attached is judged to have already broken the boundary the prompt exists to protect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the actual test is PARTICIPATION, not identity
a_rows_sample.statement: A different runtime session UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence, since a restarted process can report a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining the same working context (observation O-5); the actual eligibility test is participation ('have I authored, scoped, reviewed, verified, analysed, or advised on this work item or subject in this conversation or any context I carry'), to be disclosed in full even if it makes the candidate ineligible, with the identifier list treated only as a non-exhaustive aid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two statements, both true
a_rows_sample.statement: The original AST-019 producer is kept distinct on two levels: the general rule is that it is NOT categorically barred from implementing its own repair (ordinary engineering, no rule bars it), while the PO/ARB has separately excluded it for this specific slice as 'not the cleanest separation for this defect'; a candidate matching that identity must report NOT ELIGIBLE citing the PO/ARB decision, not a rule, and is also barred from the later re-verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 84c0f6f6 was handed the full commission at first start and, following it in order, read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
a_rows_sample.statement: The declaration-only prompt design (step 0 'declare before you orient' placed first) is a direct correction of an earlier failure mode: a prior candidate (84c0f6f6), handed the full commission at first start, read approximately 120 lines of the subject before declaring, traced to prompt selection (structuring) rather than process error; the AMENDMENT-001 changelog also records bars becoming participation-first (UUIDs demoted to a non-exhaustive aid), a new barred id (e40f3fd0) added after the scoping process itself restarted under a new runtime id, and the return format extended with REQUESTED ROLE/REPAIR GRANT/NON-ACTIONS/explicit STOP fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the implementation STOP is unrecorded
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance determination that the actual next governed act precedes any re-verifier: the repair (commit d8a5ee93, +22/-5 plus a 293-line contract test) exists in git but the authoritative workflow record never recorded the implementation lane's STOP (lane 84e5c1f7 still ACTIVE); consequence if skipped: appoint would still mechanically work but the implementer's IMPLEMENTED report and evidence would never enter the record, existing only as a git commit -- exactly the fact/record separation the estate protects. Canonical chain: implementation STOP (reports IMPLEMENTED, never VERIFIED) -> item becomes STOPPED -> human CONTINUATION -> AST-018 appoint the re-verifier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is independent re-verification binding? YES
a_rows_sample.statement: Determination that independent re-verification of the repaired code is binding, grounded primarily in a quoted PO/ARB authorization clause ('keep AST-019/AMENDMENT-001 not adopted and not authorized pending independent verification') that has never been lifted; reasoning that a verification of superseded (pre-repair) code cannot be the verification of the code that replaced it, so a prior FAIL verdict does not discharge the condition -- the repair is what makes the condition answerable. Substantive reason: defect F-1 was invisible to the entire prior 25-test contract suite, and the new tests certifying the fix (GO-26..GO-30) were written by the same process that wrote the fix, so the only present evidence of a cure comes from the party being certified -- explicitly NOT generalized into a rule that every implementation requires fresh verification, resting on this one named condition attached to this one named asset plus a blocking FAIL whose defect the existing suite could not see.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fresh runtime UUID ≠ absence of prior participation
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and applies the accumulated independence-detection findings (a subagent reports its parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so collision with a barred identity disqualifies; CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 is non-discriminating per O-5, disclosed but neither disqualifying nor certifying; prior participation established from primary evidence searches, not UUID novelty) to bar four named identities (the REPAIR-001 implementer, the first verifier, the AST-019 producer, and the scoping governance process) from re-verification, each for a stated reason rather than by reflex.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A previous candidate was handed the full commission at first start ... and read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
a_rows_sample.statement: A second declaration-only Phase-1 prompt (for the re-verifier role) reapplies the 'declare before you orient' pattern established for the implementer (S0413), explicitly citing the same prior ordering-deviation incident as its rationale; requires the candidate to search for its own id via git grep/log and directory scans before reading any authoritative state, and to report identity/independence/prior-participation/eligibility/work-item-state/authorization in a fixed six-field format before stopping.

a_rows_sample.anchor: recordedBy: governance, deliberately not implementation
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance closes the implementation lane's STOP itself, but by TRANSCRIBING the lane's own already-existing completion report (commit d8a5ee93, its message, the EP-01 plan, developer guide, session log) rather than speaking in the lane's voice, per INV-ATTR-1/2; explicitly asserts only that the completion report exists and is cited, not that the repair is correct (auditing correctness would be Governance performing the verification it is commissioning); status recorded as IMPLEMENTED -- explicitly NOT VERIFIED, NOT ADOPTED, NOT AUTHORIZED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The human speaks BUSINESS LANGUAGE. The system handles TECHNICAL WORKFLOW MECHANICS.
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-018's core business principle: the human speaks business language and never operates workflow mechanics (UUIDs, REGISTER, HANDOFF, START, predecessor, mutation owner, transition JSON); Governance/Communication capabilities perform the mechanical consequences of business decisions through the canonical workflow mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Responsibility ≠ Authority; Eligibility ≠ Authorization; Recommendation ≠ Appointment; Appointment ≠ Activation; Activation ≠ Work completion; Workflow state ≠ Business decision; Evidence ≠ Authority; Identity ≠ Authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight critical non-equivalences the capability must preserve, most centrally: the system may recommend a next actor, but only an explicit human decision constitutes an appointment, and appointment itself is not yet activation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: inferring 'Yes' because the user asked for a reviewer prompt; treating an AI message as humanAct without an explicit human act; auto-appointing because one candidate exists; auto-starting a session merely because it was selected
b_rows_sample.statement: Four named invalid inferences of human authority are explicitly forbidden: inferring consent from an unrelated request, treating an AI message as the human act, auto-appointing a sole candidate, and auto-starting a selected session; the human decision remains the sole authority act, and the orchestrator only automates mechanics after it exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0 candidates: NO_ELIGIBLE_CANDIDATE; 1 candidate: candidate can be proposed; >1 candidates: AMBIGUOUS. Never silently choose.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate discovery for appointment must be deterministic and fail-closed across exactly three cardinality cases (0/1/>1 candidates), with candidate identity always sourced from the runtime mechanism / authoritative record, never manufactured.

b_rows_sample.anchor: no spawning of an implementation actor by the recorder (a subagent of this session would inherit this session's identity and would not be a fresh actor)
b_rows_sample.statement: The process recording a commission for a fresh implementation session is explicitly barred from spawning a subagent to fill that role, because a subagent inherits the parent session's identity and therefore cannot satisfy the freshness/independence requirement for appointment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Empirical probe 2026-08-22: a subagent spawned from this session reports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID = b51dba91-6fc4-4110-b2f2-ac76ad0f3808 (parent's identity inherited; distinct OS PID only)
b_rows_sample.statement: An empirical probe finds that a subagent spawned from a Claude Code session reports the parent session's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID rather than a distinct one (only the OS PID differs), establishing that a subagent can never serve as a 'fresh, independent' actor for appointment purposes; the fresh actor exists only when the PO/ARB starts a genuinely new session.

b_rows_sample.anchor: it correctly determines: 'A fresh process is required.' but then tells the human: 'You start a fresh session.' and leaves the human to figure out what to tell that new session. That is the remaining usability gap.
b_rows_sample.statement: The original AST-018 design correctly identifies when a fresh session is required but stops one step short of usefulness, leaving the human to manually reconstruct what to tell the new session; this gap motivates adding a third use case, PrepareNextActorSession, that generates a complete copy-pasteable kickoff prompt from governed facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Important DDD boundary — NOT a 'session creator' ... Human: starts the new process. Governance Architecture: prepares the handoff instructions. New session: declares its identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: PrepareNextActorSession must remain strictly a prompt-preparation responsibility, not a process-creation one: the human still starts the new OS process, the new session still self-discovers and declares its own identity, and the capability never attempts to manufacture a process identity — consistent with the empirical subagent-inheritance probe.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FU-1 · The authoritative workflow store is not durable ... .claude/runtime/workflow/*.json is the authoritative record ... A lost or reset working tree loses every governed lane, every recorded human START act, and therefore every attribution the system relies on.
b_rows_sample.statement: The entire governance chain's trust anchor — the transition log every REGISTER/HANDOFF/START in this batch is written into — lives only in a git-ignored working-tree file with no durability mechanism outside it; a lost or reset working tree would lose every governed lane and every recorded human act, sharpening a previously weaker concern about evidence durability into a concern about the durability of the registration mechanism itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The human START act recorded at seq 3 declares its own sequence verbatim ... The STOP that the governed sequence places before 'fresh independent verifier' has not been recorded. The work item is therefore not yet at the point in its own declared sequence where a verifier is due
b_rows_sample.statement: Beyond the missing verification lane, a second and independent gate failure is identified: the predecessor implementation lane was never explicitly STOPPED per its own recorded declared sequence, so appointing a verifier while that lane still holds mutationOwner would leave the record internally inconsistent — two separately-necessary facts are missing, not one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NEXT-ACTOR-ORCHESTRATION-001 / AST-018 (SEPARATE, EXISTING, UNCHANGED) ... KOS-OPERATING-MODEL-001 (NEW — this recording) ... The new slice CONSUMES AST-018 as the existing canonical mechanism for next-actor orchestration. It does not modify, re-implement, re-open, or await the adoption of AST-018.
b_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB's Option-B decision explicitly creates a separate governed slice (the operating model) that consumes, rather than modifies or waits on, the existing AST-018 slice; AST-018's own STOP→verification→adoption path continues unaffected in parallel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the capability layer is minimal. The operating model is the primary deliverable; it consumes the existing AST-018 commands and does not re-implement, enlarge, or re-open them. Any new software produced under this commission is minimal support for the operating model — never a second workflow engine
b_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB authorizes all three delivery layers (operating model document, minimal supporting capability, verification/acceptance) but clarifies 'minimal supporting capability' to mean the new software must consume AST-018's existing commands rather than re-implement or enlarge them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The work item is STOPPED (seq 4) — an explicit CONTINUATION (recordedBy governance/human) must precede any REGISTER(verification); this prompt creates no activation.
b_rows_sample.statement: The candidate-declaration prompt for a fresh verifier explicitly states that STOPPED is sticky and that an explicit, human-recorded CONTINUATION must occur before any REGISTER(verification) can be written, listing nine barred prior participants including the implementing session itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-018 prepare-next-session → NO_FRESH_ACTOR_REQUIRED — 'Preparing a kickoff prompt now would invite you to start a new process for work that is already assigned.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Live behavior confirms AST-018 itself correctly refuses to prepare a fresh-session kickoff prompt while the work item is STOPPED, reasoning that doing so would wrongly invite a new process to start work that is already assigned to an existing (stopped) lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: next-actor.result NEXT_ACTOR_REQUIRED → role field = the authoritative next role; require --requested-role === role, else MISMATCH → STOP (GO-08) ... HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED + empty session set → first-binding case ... WORK_ITEM_STOPPED → exit 65, honest Inv-E blocker; the capability NEVER writes CONTINUATION
b_rows_sample.statement: The commission-resolution table maps every AST-018 next-actor result to a specific AST-019 behaviour: an authoritative next role must match the requested role exactly; an empty-session-set HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED is treated as the first-binding case, requiring the role to be named in the recorded human act; a STOPPED work item always fails closed since the capability never writes CONTINUATION.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No transition was hand-composed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independence verified from primary evidence (git grep/log, filesystem search, no registered lane referencing the candidate in 23 workflow records) rather than candidate testimony alone; appointment executed canonically through next-actor-orchestration.php appoint (role-specific bars passed as --exclude arguments, so eligibility is recorded by mechanism, not by an author's judgement -- the property whose absence produced ASD-001); AST-018 wrote all three transitions (REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, seq 6-8) deriving predecessor/from from the fold's current owner rather than being hand-composed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I was wrong about START, and it changes what the human must do next
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction C-1: the prior claim (stated in the REPAIR-001 authorization record, CONTEXT, the session log, and to the PO/ARB) that AST-018 appoint 'deliberately does not write START; G-3 stays human' was FALSE -- appointReviewer() writes three transitions (REGISTER, HANDOFF, and START at lines 430-447, recordedBy human, using the supplied --human-act) and then verifies ACTIVE from the fold; the prior reading stopped one block short of the START. Consequence: the implementation lane is already ACTIVE and authorized; the PO/ARB does not need to record a separate START.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-018 appoint collapses appointment and activation
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding O-6: one human act produces REGISTER+HANDOFF+START with no appoint-without-activate path through AST-018 appoint, and the same --human-act string serves as both the appointment authority and the START authority; judged not a defect but documented business intent (the tool's purpose is to remove UUID/REGISTER/HANDOFF/START mechanics from the human), yet worth recording because a person authorizing an appointment thereby also authorizes the start, and the estate's own vocabulary/prompts had treated these as two separate gates -- 'the vocabulary and the mechanisms disagree.' Contrast: AST-019 activate also fuses REGISTER->HANDOFF->START. Status: RECORDED - NOT PROMOTED - NOT DECIDED (ES-006.1, first clean occurrence, methodology frozen), explicitly not a proposal to change AST-018 and not in REPAIR-001's scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: That advice is misleading in this state
b_rows_sample.statement: Observation O-4 (reporting imprecision, not a defect claim): after the CONTINUATION, AST-018 next-actor reports 'LANE ACTIVE ... no new actor is needed', which is misleading in this state since the lane is ACTIVE only as a mechanical consequence of the continuation, not because the verifier has further work; the fold itself is correct, only the advisory interpretation is wrong; verified harmless to the plan since appointReviewer() has no active-lane refusal (unlike AST-019's GO-13 gate). Status: RECORDED, NOT PROMOTED (ES-006.1, single occurrence).
