b_rows_sample.anchor:
The central distinction is: Supported 
eq Accepted 
eq Committed 
eq True. This distinction should become one of the core laws of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing distinction of Step 8 as a candidate core law of KnowledgeOS: Supported ≠ Accepted ≠ Committed ≠ True.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The problem ... Strong supporting evidence, No known contradiction, Current, High provenance quality ... Can KnowledgeOS now put P into the Knowledge State as accepted knowledge? Not necessarily. There is a missing concept: AcceptancePolicy. The evidence tells us what the evidence supports. The acce
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues even strong, uncontradicted, current, high-provenance evidence does not automatically warrant acceptance, introducing AcceptancePolicy as the missing concept determining what may be admitted as accepted knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four epistemic statuses ... Candidate \rightarrow Supported \rightarrow Accepted \rightarrow Committed ... Supported \rightarrow Contested ... Supported \rightarrow Rejected ... Candidate \rightarrow Unresolved ... These are not simply levels of "confidence." They represent different domain states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Candidate/Supported/Accepted/Committed as a branching progression (not a confidence scale), with additional branches to Contested, Rejected, and Unresolved, insisting these are distinct domain states.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate ... A proposition becomes a candidate when KnowledgeOS has reason to represent it but does not yet have sufficient basis to accept it. ... LLM extracted from document ... Candidate(P)=True but Accepted(P)=False. This is particularly important for AI-generated knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Candidate(P) status (proposition represented but not yet accepted), illustrated by an LLM-extracted proposition, flagged as particularly important for AI-generated knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supported ... Supported_\rho(P) = Assessment_\rho(P)\models SupportCondition_\rho ... The evidence provides a defensible basis for the proposition under the selected assessment policy. But Supported(P)\not\Rightarrow Accepted(P).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Supported_ρ(P) as Assessment_ρ(P) satisfying a policy-specific SupportCondition_ρ, explicitly not implying Accepted(P).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Accepted ... Accept_\rho(P,EA) \rightarrow AcceptedAssertion subject to the acceptance policy. ... One authoritative current source is sufficient ... Two independent observations ... Accepted_{\rho_1}(P)=True while Accepted_{\rho_2}(P)=False. This is not a mathematical contradiction. It is policy de
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Accept_ρ(P,EA)→AcceptedAssertion as policy-relative, showing the same evidence can be Accepted under one policy (single authoritative source) and not under another (requiring two independent observations) — policy dependence, not contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Commitment ... an organization may accept ... but still not be committed to using that assertion as a basis for an operational decision. "We accept that Nexus is 3.69, but migration approval requires an additional infrastructure verification." Accepted(P)\not\Rightarrow Committed(P). Commitment mean
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Commitment as distinct from Acceptance: Accepted(P) ⇏ Committed(P), illustrated by an organization accepting a fact but still requiring additional verification before migration approval; commitment means willingness to rely on the proposition for a defined purpose/action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Commitment is purpose-dependent ... Commit_\rho(P,Purpose,Authority) ... Commit(P,migration,ArchitectureBoard) may require more than Commit(P,internal research,Engineer). Commit(P,P_1)\neq Commit(P,P_2). This fits our earlier Ideal State principle: I_t(P_1)\neq I_t(P_2).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Commit_ρ(P,Purpose,Authority) as purpose-dependent, e.g. migration commitment requiring Architecture Board authority versus lighter requirements for internal research, echoing the earlier purpose-dependence of the Ideal State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth remains outside the state machine ... Accepted(P)\neq True(P) and Committed(P)\neq True(P). KnowledgeOS does not have an oracle for reality. It records what is currently supported, accepted, and/or committed under a defined epistemic and governance regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that neither Accepted(P) nor Committed(P) equals True(P): KnowledgeOS has no oracle for reality, only records what is supported/accepted/committed under a defined regime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formal acceptance function ... \alpha_\rho: EA\times P\times C \rightarrow \mathcal S_A ... \mathcal S_A=\{Candidate,Supported,Accepted,Rejected,Contested,Unresolved\} ... an assertion can be Supported + Contested. So again, we should be careful about a single enum.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines α_ρ:EA×P×C→S_A over six statuses, warning against treating S_A as a single mutually-exclusive enum since e.g. Supported+Contested can co-occur.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Better: acceptance as a multidimensional status ... \Omega_A=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus) ... Support: Strong, Acceptance: Accepted, Commitment: Committed, Contest: Active. This looks strange initially, but it accurately represents real organizational knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines acceptance status as a four-dimensional vector Ω_A=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus), with a worked example showing Accepted+Committed+Contest:Active as coherent, accurately reflecting real organizational knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Why "Accepted + Contested" is possible ... an architecture board has formally accepted ... another architect disputes ... Accepted(P)=True while Contested(P)=True. This is not logically impossible. ... The proposition is institutionally accepted while still being epistemically contested. This is exa
b_rows_sample.statement: Justifies Accepted+Contested coexisting via an architecture-board example (formally accepted decision still disputed by an architect), establishing that epistemic status and governance status must not be collapsed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Acceptance policy ... \rho_A = AcceptancePolicy ... Evidence requirements N_{independent}\geq2 ... Source requirements Authority(Source)\geq A_{min} ... Temporal requirements Age(e)\leq T_{max} ... Conflict requirements ActiveConflict(P)=False ... Human approval ... Statistical threshold Pr(P\mid E)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines AcceptancePolicy ρ_A as specifying six example condition types (independent-evidence count, source authority minimum, evidence-age maximum, no active conflict, human approval, statistical threshold) — explicitly examples of policy, not universal law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us a clean separation ... Mathematics defines what the evidence assessment means. Policy defines when an assessment is sufficient for acceptance. Governance defines who has authority to commit to that knowledge. Assessment \rightarrow AcceptancePolicy \rightarrow Acceptance \rightarrow Go
b_rows_sample.statement: Draws a three-way separation — mathematics (what assessment means), policy (when acceptance is sufficient), governance (who may commit) — formalized as Assessment→AcceptancePolicy→Acceptance→Governance→Commitment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD interpretation ... a bounded context around Knowledge Commitment. Assertion ... EvidenceAssessment ... AcceptancePolicy ... AcceptanceDecision ... Commitment ... Authority ... These should not be hidden inside the Assertion entity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a Knowledge Commitment bounded context with six concepts (Assertion, EvidenceAssessment, AcceptancePolicy, AcceptanceDecision, Commitment, Authority) that must not be hidden inside the Assertion entity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Acceptance is a domain event ... AssertionAccepted should be emitted. AssertionId, AssessmentId, PolicyId, PolicyVersion, Authority, Context, EffectiveFrom, DecisionBasis, Timestamp. This creates an auditable transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an AssertionAccepted domain event carrying AssertionId, AssessmentId, PolicyId/Version, Authority, Context, EffectiveFrom, DecisionBasis, Timestamp for auditability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rejection is different from absence of acceptance ... NotAccepted\neq Rejected ... Evidence: insufficient ... The correct state may be Unresolved. It does not mean P=False. Unresolved\neq Rejected. This is critical for incomplete real-world knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: States NotAccepted≠Rejected and Unresolved≠Rejected: insufficient evidence should yield Unresolved, not a claim that P is false — critical for incomplete real-world knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Example ... Production Nexus is backed up. ... Infrastructure engineer says yes ... Backup configuration not inspected ... No restore test ... Support: Moderate, Uncertainty: High, Verification: Insufficient ... KnowledgeOS should not conclude \neg P. Nor Accepted(P). The correct result may be Unres
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a backup-verification example where weak/unverified evidence (engineer's verbal yes, uninspected config, no restore test) correctly yields Unresolved(P) with a Lord recommendation to verify configuration and run a restore test, rather than either Accepted(P) or ¬P.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Acceptance and Ideal State ... MustBeVerified(BackupStatus) ... Supported(P) may still fail the ideal requirement: \Sigma_K(P)\not\models I^K(P). Accepted(P) \not\Rightarrow IdealSatisfied(P). A proposition can be accepted while the knowledge objective remains incomplete.
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects Acceptance to the Ideal State: Accepted(P) ⇏ IdealSatisfied(P) — a proposition can be accepted while the underlying knowledge objective (e.g. independent verification) remains incomplete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Example ... Nexus = 3.69 Accepted. But the Ideal State requires MustBeKnown, MustBeCurrent, MustBeIndependentlyVerified ... Independent verification = no ... Accepted(P)=True but \Delta_t\neq\emptyset. Acceptance does not mean completion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: an accepted Nexus-version assertion still leaves a nonempty discrepancy Δ_t because independent verification is missing — 'Acceptance does not mean completion.'

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'A1..A10'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may have many pieces of evidence supporting incompatible propositions. How does it determine what may be accepted, what remains uncertain, what is rejected, and what must be escalated? The answer should not be "choose the most trustworthy source." We need to separate authority, evidentia
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 19's central problem: choosing among conflicting evidence must not reduce to 'pick the most trustworthy source' — authority, evidential support, reliability, applicability, independence, and epistemic commitment must be kept separate.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
The fundamental distinction ... Evidence 
eq Truth and Source 
eq Evidence ... Authority 
eq Reliability and Reliability 
eq Evidential Support and Evidential Support 
eq Knowledge Commitment. These are different properties.
a_rows_sample.statement: States five separated properties: Evidence≠Truth, Source≠Evidence, Authority≠Reliability, Reliability≠EvidentialSupport, EvidentialSupport≠KnowledgeCommitment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Why this matters ... Source A An official constitution ... Source B An engineer says ... Source C An LLM says ... KnowledgeOS cannot simply calculate (1+1+1)/3. This is not a democracy. Knowledge commitment is governed epistemic synthesis, not source voting.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates with a constitution/engineer/LLM three-source example that KnowledgeOS cannot average opinions — 'Knowledge commitment is governed epistemic synthesis, not source voting.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source ... S=(SourceID,Type,Origin,Owner,Context,AuthorityProfile,ReliabilityProfile,TemporalScope,Provenance). A source is a producer/container of information. It is not itself evidence for every proposition it contains. ... Source versus evidence ... Source \supset Evidence conceptually. A source
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Source=(SourceID,Type,Origin,Owner,Context,AuthorityProfile,ReliabilityProfile,TemporalScope,Provenance) as distinct from Evidence — a source is not itself evidence for every proposition it contains (Source ⊃ Evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence support ... Support(e,A) = (Direction,Strength,Specificity,Directness,Completeness) ... Direction = supports / contradicts / neutral; Strength = how strongly; Specificity = how directly it addresses A; Directness = direct observation versus inference; Completeness = whether relevant informa
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a structured five-dimension Support(e,A)=(Direction,Strength,Specificity,Directness,Completeness) instead of a scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority ... Who or what has the legitimate right to establish a proposition or rule in this context? ... Constitution Very high for governance rules ... LLM No intrinsic organizational authority ... Authority(S,A,Ctx) must be contextual. ... Authority is not universal ... an architecture board doe
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines contextual Authority(S,A,Ctx) (worked with a seven-source authority table), establishing Authority is scoped — high authority in one domain does not transfer to another.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reliability ... How consistently does this source produce information that turns out to correspond to the relevant domain state? Rel(S,A,Ctx,t) can be estimated from historical performance. ... Reliability is empirical ... \hat p=990/1000=0.99. But we should not immediately declare Reliability=0.99.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines empirically-estimated Reliability Rel(S,A,Ctx,t), warning a raw hit-rate must account for sampling/independence/bias/measurement-error/confidence-intervals — Reliability is an estimate, not an intrinsic metaphysical property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical reliability ... \hat p=k/n ... p\sim Beta(\alpha,\beta) and after k successes in n observations p\mid data \sim Beta(\alpha+k,\beta+n-k). This gives KnowledgeOS a principled way to represent source reliability uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a Bayesian Beta-Binomial estimator for source reliability p|data~Beta(α+k,β+n-k), representing reliability uncertainty as a distribution rather than a point estimate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But source reliability is not proposition reliability ... Rel(S,Infrastructure)=High but Rel(S,LegalInterpretation)=Low. Reliability(S)\neq Reliability(S,A). This is an important correction to simplistic trust scores.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects simplistic single-value trust scores: Reliability(S) ≠ Reliability(S,A) — a source can be reliable in one domain and unreliable in another.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Applicability ... Applicable(S,A,Ctx,t) ... A 2024 architecture decision may be authoritative, but no longer applicable after a 2026 superseding decision. Authority \land Reliability does not imply Applicability. ... Temporal validity ... T_v(S,A) must be considered. Commitment = f(Authority,Support
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Applicable(S,A,Ctx,t) as a third dimension distinct from Authority and Reliability — Authority∧Reliability does not imply Applicability, especially once superseded — feeding Commitment=f(Authority,Support,Reliability,Applicability,Time,...).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence ... five websites repeat ... suppose all five copied the same original article. n=5 does not mean five independent observations. Independence(e_i,e_j) or at least an estimate of dependence. ... Evidence correlation ... EffectiveEvidence(e_1,e_2,e_3)<3. This prevents evidence inflation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms that apparent multi-source agreement (five websites) can collapse to one effective observation if all derive from a common original, requiring an explicit evidence-dependency graph — Corroboration depends on independence, not merely source count.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contradictory evidence ... e_1\Rightarrow A and e_2\Rightarrow \neg A. We should not immediately calculate A=0.5. Instead create EvidenceConflict(A,\neg A). Then evaluate authority; reliability; applicability; time; independence; specificity; directness.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires contradictory evidence produce an explicit EvidenceConflict(A,¬A) object evaluated across seven dimensions, rather than collapsing to a naive average like A=0.5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence comparison ... W(e,A,C)=(Authority,Reliability,Directness,Specificity,Freshness,Independence,Completeness). This is a profile, not necessarily a single number. ... Why not simply create one evidence score? Because dimensions can conflict. Old Constitution: Very high authority, Low directnes
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the seven-dimension evidence comparison profile W(e,A,C), warning against collapsing to one score since dimensions can conflict (e.g. an old authoritative constitution vs a fresh but lower-authority database state) — Evidence comparison is purpose and proposition dependent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence ordering ... e_1\succeq e_2 if w_i(e_1)\geq w_i(e_2) for all relevant i. This gives us a Pareto-style evidence ordering. ... Evidence need not be totally ordered ... e_1\nsucceq e_2 and e_2\nsucceq e_1. They are incomparable under the current ordering. EvidenceComparison=Incomparable rather
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a Pareto-style partial order over evidence (e1⪰e2), explicitly allowing evidence to be mutually Incomparable rather than forcing a winner.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source authority hierarchy ... Constitution > Policy > Procedure > Guideline > Recommendation. But this hierarchy must itself be a governed rule. It is not a universal law of KnowledgeOS. AuthorityHierarchy is domain policy. ... Proposition-specific authority ... Authority(ArchitectureBoard,Architec
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires any source-authority hierarchy (e.g. Constitution>Policy>Procedure>Guideline>Recommendation) itself be a governed policy, not a universal law, since a single global trust ranking would be absurd across unrelated proposition types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source reliability matrix ... R_{S,A,C} ... CMDB High infrastructure, Low architecture, None business policy ... LLM Candidate only across all. This is far more useful than Trust(LLM)=0.6.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a source×assertion-type×context reliability matrix (worked with a five-source example) as far more useful than a single scalar trust score.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLMs require special treatment ... LLMOutput be modeled as a generated informational artifact, not as a trusted source of organizational truth. Authority(LLM,GovernanceRule)=0 unless the organization explicitly assigns authority. Its outputs become CandidateEvidence or CandidateAssertion or Candidat
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires LLM output be modeled as a generated informational artifact with Authority(LLM,GovernanceRule)=0 by default, entering only as Candidate — LLM→Candidate→EvidenceAssessment→GovernedKnowledge, never LLM→Truth, a defining KnowledgeOS architectural property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge commitment ... Candidate \rightarrow Supported \rightarrow Corroborated \rightarrow Accepted \rightarrow Committed. But this is not necessarily a universal linear lifecycle. Candidate\rightarrow Rejected. Candidate\rightarrow Undetermined. Supported\rightarrow Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-stage Knowledge Commitment lifecycle (Candidate→Supported→Corroborated→Accepted→Committed) with explicit non-linear branches (to Rejected, Undetermined, Superseded).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What does "committed" mean? ... A proposition is knowledge-committed when the system is authorized to use it as an accepted premise within a specified context and purpose. Committed_\rho(A,K,Ctx,t) means: Under governance policy \rho, assertion A is admitted into the committed knowledge state for co
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Committed_ρ(A,K,Ctx,t) as policy-relative admission into the committed knowledge state, purpose- and context-sensitive rather than universal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge state partition ... K=K_C\cup K_S\cup K_U\cup K_X where K_C committed knowledge; K_S supported but not committed; K_U unresolved/uncertain; K_X rejected/superseded historical knowledge. This prevents the database from collapsing everything into one truth bucket. ... Committed knowledge is
a_rows_sample.statement: Partitions K into K_committed∪K_supported∪K_uncertain∪K_historical, and states Committed(A) ⇏ universally true — only that KnowledgeOS is permitted to treat A as accepted knowledge given its epistemic and governance state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A=\{Human,LLM,System,Sensor,Database,Agent,ExternalAuthority\} ... What should KnowledgeOS do when credible sources disagree? ... not pick the source with the highest confidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the model to a seven-type set of independent epistemic producers, framing the central question of what to do when credible sources disagree, explicitly rejecting 'pick the source with the highest confidence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent\neq Evidence ... The scanner itself is not the observation. The observation is E ... ProducedBy(E)=Agent
b_rows_sample.statement: States Agent ≠ Evidence: an agent produces evidence, provenance recorded as ProducedBy(E)=Agent, worked with an InfrastructureScanner example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentID and AgentType\in\{Human,AI,System,Sensor,Organization,Authority\} ... without treating them as equivalent sources
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires every epistemic actor to have stable AgentID and AgentType (six-value enum), preventing treatment of dissimilar sources as equivalent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Trust(Agent)=0.9 ... too simplistic ... Trust(a,d,c,t) ... Trust(AI,CodeAnalysis,RepositoryX) may be high ... Trust(AI,LegalApproval) may be irrelevant
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a bare scalar Trust(Agent)=0.9, requiring contextual Trust(a,d,c,t) parameterized by domain/context/time, worked with a code-analysis-vs-legal-approval contrast.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Expertise=High but AuthorityToApproveArchitecture=False ... Expertise\neq Authority ... Trust\neq Authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Expertise from Authority (a highly expert engineer may lack architecture-approval authority; an authoritative Board may not be the best source for a low-level measurement) — Expertise ≠ Authority, Trust ≠ Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reliability(Source) from Trust(Agent) ... an architect's recollection of an IP address ... highly trustworthy [but] low reliability for exact network facts
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Reliability(Source) from Trust(Agent): a generally trustworthy source can still be unreliable for a specific measurement type.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent A and B both read Vendor Document ... AgentIndependence\neq InformationIndependence ... extends the double-counting principle from 25N
b_rows_sample.statement: States AgentIndependence ≠ InformationIndependence: two distinct agents reading the same document are not thereby independent sources — explicitly extends the double-counting principle from Step 25N.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Counting A and B as two independent confirmations would inflate confidence. The actual independent information may be approximately 1 source
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked common-source-dependency example: two agents both reading one vendor document should count as approximately one independent information unit, not two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G_D=(V,E_D) ... E_1\leftarrow SourceDocument, E_2\leftarrow SourceDocument ... E_1\not\perp E_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a dependency graph G_D=(V,E_D) for evidence provenance, enabling detection of non-independence (E1 ⊥̸ E2) among evidence sharing a common source.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict(A,E_1,E_2) ... same entity? same time? same context? same proposition? same measurement? independently acquired? authoritative? different scopes? Only then can we resolve the conflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Conflict(A,E1,E2) and requires an eight-question diagnostic checklist (entity, time, context, proposition, measurement, independent acquisition, authority, differing scopes) before attempting resolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus=3.69 at 10:00, Nexus=3.70 at 15:00 ... Conflict=False ... identity + temporal semantics must precede conflict resolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked apparent-conflict example resolved by temporal disambiguation (different times) — Conflict=False; identity+temporal semantics must precede conflict resolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus_{production}=3.70 and Nexus_{development}=3.69 ... Conflict=False. The apparent contradiction disappears after entity/context resolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked apparent-conflict example resolved by context/entity disambiguation (production vs development) — again Conflict=False.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ProductionNexus=3.69 at t=10:00 and ProductionNexus=3.70 at the same t=10:00 ... genuine conflict. KnowledgeOS must preserve it
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked genuine-conflict example: same entity, same time, contradictory values — must be preserved, not disambiguated away.

b_rows_sample.anchor: if conflict: choose one, delete the other. That destroys epistemic history ... Conflict=FirstClassKnowledgeState
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against the anti-pattern of silently choosing and deleting one side of a conflict, destroying epistemic history — Conflict must be a FirstClassKnowledgeState.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ResolveConflict(E_1,E_2,A,C)\rightarrow Resolution ... Confirmed(E_1), Confirmed(E_2), BothValid, BothInvalid, Unresolved
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines ResolveConflict(E1,E2,A,C)->Resolution with five possible outcomes: Confirmed(E1), Confirmed(E2), BothValid, BothInvalid, Unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Temperature_1=20C and Temperature_2=21C ... may both be correct because they measure different physical locations ... Conflict may actually indicate ContextMissing
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked BothValid example: two sensors at different physical locations both correct — a reported Conflict may actually indicate ContextMissing, 'a very important diagnostic principle.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict->Identity check->Temporal check->Context check->Semantic proposition check->Dependency check->Source reliability->Authority->Independent corroboration->Resolution/Unresolved ... much safer than weighted voting
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a nine-stage conflict-resolution pipeline, explicitly 'much safer than weighted voting.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Trust(A)=0.8 and Trust(B)=0.7 ... should not calculate 0.8>0.7\Rightarrow A=True ... B may possess direct contradictory evidence. A may merely be repeating B's source ... TrustScore\neq TruthSelector
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against naive trust-score comparison to resolve conflicts: a higher-trust source may merely repeat a lower-trust source's own contradictory direct evidence — TrustScore ≠ TruthSelector.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Board approved migration [engineer] versus Architecture Board rejected migration [official record] ... official decision record has stronger authority ... B can supersede A for governance status. But A should remain historical evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked authority-resolved conflict example: an official decision record supersedes an ordinary engineer's claim for governance status, while the engineer's claim remains historical evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: System: Nexus version=3.69 versus LLM: Nexus version appears to be 3.70 ... not because System>LLM universally. It is because MeasurementMethod is better suited to that proposition
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues preferring a direct system observation over an LLM interpretation is a measurement-method-suitability judgment for that specific proposition, not a universal source-type ranking.

a_aliases: Step 19: Authority, Trust, Evidence Weighting, Source Reliability, and Knowledge Commitment
b_aliases: Multi-Agent Knowledge, Conflict Resolution, Consensus, Trust and Distributed Epistemics

Note: S0913's Step 25U: the fully worked multi-agent trust/conflict/consensus model (contextual trust, competence tables, evidence-clustered consensus, ByzantineConsensus distinction); extends B0021's authority-trust-source-reliability-knowledge-commitment (S0876/Step 19) with a formal conflict taxonomy and resolution pipeline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A relation always requires: Entity + Property Boundary + Context Boundary + Relation Mode
a_rows_sample.statement: Avacchedaka (the delimitor/scope of a property in Navya-Nyaya) is presented as 'the Missing Type System': a database-style {entity, attribute, value} triple (e.g. {System, Status, Active}) is insufficient because a bare property like 'Active' is meaningless without a bounding context (software lifecycle vs user account vs legal contract vs infrastructure context). Proposes replacing a flat {"property":"active"} JSON object with one carrying bounded_by:{domain, lifecycle, authority} and a relation field (e.g. "state-of").

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Identity = (Entity, Property, Context, Relation, Time, Authority)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'Avacchedaka becomes Context-Bounded Identity': Knowledge Identity is defined as the 6-tuple (Entity, Property, Context, Relation, Time, Authority), explicitly contrasted with a naive 'Entity + Text' identity model. The file frames this as directly connecting to 'your earlier discovery: Semantic Context is missing' (a prior finding not identified by name or source within this file).

type_signature.domain: Entity x Property x Context x Relation x Time x Authority

b_rows_sample.anchor: This document is actually more important architecturally than the previous Tarka document, because it moves from reasoning steps into the structure of reasoning itself... sambandha (relation) as ontologically primary, not merely grammatical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Asserts this Navya-Nyaya material is more architecturally important than the prior Tarka extraction because it addresses the structure of reasoning (relations) rather than reasoning steps, singling out sambandha (relation) as ontologically primary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not fundamentally a document system. It is not even fundamentally a knowledge-object system. It is a: relationship-preserving reasoning system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a deeper model Entity->Relationship->Meaning->Inference->Knowledge State, explicitly contrasted with a rejected Document->Embedding->Answer model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Relation-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL treat epistemic relationships as first-class entities and SHALL NOT reduce them into attributes of knowledge objects. This is probably one of the strongest kernel candidates discovered so far.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues existing KnowledgeOS discoveries (Evidence!=Authority, Observation!=Decision, Assessment!=Authority, Expression!=Meaning, Representation!=Identity) are all relationship constraints, not object properties, contrasting a flat 'Evidence{authority_level: high}' schema with a relational 'Evidence -supports-> Claim, Source -provides authority for-> Evidence' model, then proposes H-KOS-Relation-001.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Avacchedaka = delimiter / limiting condition... 'The system is secure.' Without delimiter: Meaning undefined. With delimiter: Security limited by Application Layer / Network Layer / Threat Model X ... H-KOS-Context-002: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the delimiting conditions under which a proposition is valid.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces avacchedaka (delimiter/limiting condition) with a security example showing the same proposition changes meaning by delimiter, concluding context is a logical boundary rather than metadata, and proposes H-KOS-Context-002.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The logical structure is visible inside the representation itself... 'self-presenting' where inferential structure is visible through the expressive system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS probably requires neither a relational-database-only nor vector-database-only model but a semantic relationship model (Knowledge Graph/Hypergraph with supported-by/bounded-by/derived-through edges), citing Navya-Nyaya's self-presenting representational structure as the architectural precedent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preserves: 1. Identity 2. Evidence 3. Authority 4. Context 5. Transformation 6. Time 7. Uncertainty 8. Knower ... Through: 9. Relations 10. Reasoning chains 11. Validation processes 12. Revision history
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the kernel formula as eight preserved dimensions realized through four relational/procedural mechanisms (relations, reasoning chains, validation processes, revision history).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Strong Candidates: Sambandha (relations first-class) — Very High; Avacchedaka (context boundary) — Very High; Reasoning structure preservation — High; Fallacy preservation — High; Debate intent classification — Medium ... Research Only: 16 categories as complete architecture; Nyaya liberation goal; Sanskrit logical terminology
b_rows_sample.statement: Final classification separating strong kernel-relevant candidates (sambandha, avacchedaka, reasoning-structure preservation, fallacy preservation, debate-intent classification) from items explicitly marked 'Research Only' (the full 16 categories as architecture, the liberation goal, Sanskrit terminology).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 16 padarthas represent the complete framework of logical inquiry... The 12 Prameyas (Objects of Knowledge): Atma, Sarira, Indriya, Artha, Buddhi, Mana, Pravrtti, Dosa, Pretyabhava, Phala, Duhkha, Apavarga
b_rows_sample.statement: Appended full reference table of all 16 padarthas with Sanskrit terms and descriptions, plus the full 12-item Prameya (objects of knowledge) enumeration, presented as background explanation rather than a KnowledgeOS-specific extraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Navya-Nyaya emerged in the 14th century in Mithila (Bihar) with Gangesa Upadhyaya's seminal work Tattvacintamani, and reached maturity in 17th-century Navadvipa (Bengal)... Daniel Ingalls famously called Navya-Nyaya 'the most precise calculus of properties produced before Frege.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Navya-Nyaya's historical development (Gangesa Upadhyaya, then Raghunatha Siromani/Mathuranatha Tarkavagisa/Jagadisa Tarkalamkara in Navadvipa), its technical vocabulary table (sambandha, avacchedaka, pratiyogin/anuyogin, vyapti, abhava, tadatmya, paryapti, visesana-visesya), a canonical example compound sentence, and its 'unbounded relational depth' (parampara-sambandha) capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not only: Knowledge Graph. It is: Knowledge Graph + Argument Graph + Debate Graph... a knowledge object should contain: Claim / Who asserted / Evidence / Counterclaims / Reasoning / Validation / Decision / Revision history
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues logic's growth from debate discipline implies KnowledgeOS must be a Knowledge Graph plus an Argument Graph plus a Debate Graph, and specifies the full field set a knowledge object should carry.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Amends the ratified Book Architecture (BA-1…BA-6, GN-34) for Edition 2 production ONLY. ... Edition 1 remains frozen under the un-amended BA.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2 amends the ratified Book Architecture BA-1..BA-6 (GN-34) for Edition 2 production only, leaving BA-1..BA-6 unmodified as documents and Edition 1 frozen under the original BA; authorized by GN-42 Decision 1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Each Edition-2 chapter opens with its Edition-1 text verbatim as a labeled abstract ('Edition 1 abstract') — traceability, not rewriting.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-01: chapter depth follows S/M/L/XL word RANGES (never fixed targets), and each chapter must open with its Edition-1 text verbatim as a labeled abstract for traceability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A definition may never exceed its source's grade (GN-14 applies with full force).
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-02: every introduced concept requires an explicit definition block (name, formal notation, semantic meaning, scope, evidence/grade, relations, example, limitation), and a definition may never exceed its source's evidential grade -- GN-14's no-epistemic-upgrade rule applies with full force.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status vocabulary is mandatory and immutable through prose: DERIVED · RECONSTRUCTABLE · ASSUMED · HYPOTHESIS · NOT ESTABLISHED · RESEARCH REQUIRED. A NOT-ESTABLISHED derivation is TAUGHT AS OPEN with its closing act named.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-03: a fixed, immutable six-value derivation-status vocabulary must be used verbatim in prose; a NOT-ESTABLISHED derivation must be taught as explicitly open with its closing act named, never invented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The example is [INTERPRETATION]/[EDITORIAL] — an illustration of ratified machinery, never evidence for it, and never product design.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-04: the book's running worked example (election-certification) threads Part III under a three-voice discipline (CONCEPTUAL MODEL / ARCHITECTURE / IMPLEMENTATION-HONESTY) and is explicitly marked interpretation/editorial -- an illustration of ratified machinery, never itself evidence for it or product design.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No upgrading of an [U]/open proposition into architectural fact — the GN-42 master constraint: Edition 2 may explain the architecture more deeply, but may not expand the architecture because deeper explanation creates theoretical gaps.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-08, called 'the master apparatus': every section opens with a status line from a closed vocabulary (fact/definition/derivation/evidence/interpretation/hypothesis/open); states the GN-42 master constraint that Edition 2 may explain the architecture more deeply but must never expand it, since deeper explanation risks silently creating theoretical gaps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I.3 is evidence-gated on the separate kernel-research commission (GN-42 Decision 3) and is never filled from inference. No historical claim may exceed its evidence; the hindsight ban continues.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-09: Part I historical evidence depth follows a governing table; chapter I.3 is gated on a separate kernel-research commission and must never be filled from inference; the corpus's existing hindsight ban (no historical claim exceeding its evidence) continues to apply.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part III → Part II → Part IV → evidence-ready Part I (I.2, I.4, I.5, I.6, I.1-light) → I.3 after kernel research. Reviews per plan §15: per-part producer + independent review... one final acceptance act.
a_rows_sample.statement: GN-42 Decision 2 sets Edition 2's production order (Part III, then II, then IV, then evidence-ready Part I chapters, then I.3 last after kernel research) and mandates a per-part producer-plus-independent-review cycle with correction gates and one final acceptance act per part.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every major formal relation taught in an Edition-2 chapter carries a table row: | Relation | Source | Ratified? | Formal status | Computable? | Tested? | Open issue | Purpose: no relation may look mathematically more complete than it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-11 (added by GN-50, 2026-08-29, additive): every major formal relation taught from chapter III.9 onward must carry a status table row (Source/Ratified?/Formal status/Computable?/Tested?/Open issue), so that no relation can look mathematically more complete than it actually is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Post-edit re-verification: any edit after a chapter's conformance check invalidates the check... CLAIM-STRENGTH INHERITANCE CHECK (GN-54): a compression may never carry stronger epistemic status than its source representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-12 (added by GN-54, 2026-08-29, binding for Parts II/IV/I): eight production controls including post-edit re-verification (any edit invalidates a prior conformance check), grep-verified negative assertions, a cross-artifact summary gate (row-by-row check of synoptic claims against the artifact summarized), a machine-checkable running-example continuity ledger, a fixed Tested? vocabulary, a phrase-strength sweep, a planned III.1-III.8 retrofit, and a claim-strength inheritance check (a compression must never carry stronger epistemic status than its source).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The artifact subjected to final verification must be the artifact delivered for review, or any transformation between them must be mechanically demonstrated lossless. ... never a re-typed/condensed rendition labeled as the artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-13 (adopted by GN-57, 2026-08-29, binding): delivery artifact integrity rule -- the verified artifact and the delivered artifact must be identical, or any transformation between them mechanically proven lossless; review deliveries must be verbatim machine-emitted content with md5/line/word counts, never a re-typed or condensed stand-in.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Citation existence is not citation substantiation. ... 1. the cited artifact exists; 2. the cited location is identifiable; 3. the cited artifact actually CONTAINS the asserted evidence; 4. the evidence supports the claim at the STATED strength...; 5. no retrospective interpretation has been silentl
a_rows_sample.statement: BA-ED2-14 (adopted by GN-61/HPA label GN-58, 2026-08-29, additive): citation-content substantiation control requiring five ordered verification steps beyond mere citation existence (artifact exists; location identifiable; artifact actually contains the asserted evidence; evidence supports the claim at the stated strength; no silently substituted retrospective interpretation), applying with particular force to 'verified'/'tested'/'independently audited'/universal-quantifier/census/byte-identical/mathematical-conformance claims; explicitly a production-integrity control, not an architectural change, and never retrofitted into a chapter's historical narrative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Origin: GN-60 audit of II.3 — the nine-control pass verified evidence-map rows existed but not that cited files contained the claims (mechanical presence checking ≠ semantic evidence checking); two silent upgrades survived until an independent audit traced claims to records.
a_rows_sample.statement: States BA-ED2-14's own governance origin: it was created because the GN-60 audit of chapter II.3 found that an existing nine-control verification pass checked only that evidence-map citation rows existed, not that the cited files actually contained the claimed evidence -- exactly the same producer-control gap this batch's audit-three-lens.md (S1398) for II.3 independently reports and proposes a rule for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Imported standing rules (binding, from the ruled record) GN-14 no-epistemic-upgrade · the D-2 verbatim rule ... GN-10 status vocabulary (never 'validated') · OQ non-resolution · DeepSeek and all external mathematics excluded pending independent establishment + intake gate
a_rows_sample.statement: Imports several pre-existing standing rules as binding for Edition 2: GN-14 (no epistemic upgrade), the D-2 verbatim-reproduction rule, GN-10 status vocabulary (banning 'validated'), non-resolution of open questions, and exclusion of DeepSeek/external mathematics pending independent establishment and an intake gate.

A component of K is necessary only if removing it causes some mandatory operation to lose required semantic information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\mathcal O_{all} = \mathcal O_{sem} \cup \mathcal O_{obs} \cup \mathcal O_{gov} \cup \mathcal O_{hist} \cup \mathcal O_{repr}$$ ... $$\boxed{\mathcal O_{all} \neq \text{one homogeneous algebra}}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the earlier O_core formulation's category error: operations belong to different mathematical categories (Assert changes state, Query observes, Compare produces a relation, Authorize evaluates governance admissibility, Serialize changes representation, Replay reconstructs history) and must not be treated as one homogeneous algebra. Defines the full operation universe as a union of five disjoint families: semantic-state, observation, governance, historical, and representation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$O_S=\{Assert,Retract,Supersede,Infer,Merge\}$$ $$O_E=\{Support,Refute,Qualify,Assess,DetectContradiction,Resolve\}$$ $$O_O=\{Query,Compare,Identity,Equal\}$$ $$O_H=\{Replay,Trace\}$$ $$O_G=\{Authorize,Validate\}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives the candidate semantic operation universe as the union of five families: semantic state operations O_S = {Assert, Retract, Supersede, Infer, Merge}; evidence/epistemic operations O_E = {Support, Refute, Qualify, Assess, DetectContradiction, Resolve}; observation/equivalence operations O_O = {Query, Compare, Identity, Equal}; historical operations O_H = {Replay, Trace}; governance operations O_G = {Authorize, Validate}. Representation/infrastructure operations (Serialize, Deserialize, Save, Load, Delete) are explicitly excluded from the semantic kernel (O_repr ∩ O_sem = ∅).

b_rows_sample.anchor: It would be incorrect to infer: $$Operation\rightarrow StateField$$ For example: $$DetectContradiction$$ does not imply: $$Conflict\in\Sigma$$ as a primitive field. Likewise: $$Supersede$$ does not imply: $$Superseded\in\Sigma.$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Names one of the step's most important conclusions: an operation existing in O_core does not imply the distinction it detects must become a primitive field of Sigma. DetectContradiction existing does not force Conflict into Sigma; Supersede existing does not force Superseded into Sigma; Replay existing does not force complete history to be embedded in K. Operations constrain K but do not dictate its decomposition — hence a genuine sufficiency/minimality proof (not operation enumeration) is still required for K and Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### F272A-1 — Missing mandatory operation ... F272A-2 — Redundant operation ... F272A-3 — Category error ... F272A-4 — Hidden dependency ... F272A-5 — Governance contamination ... F272A-6 — Historical contamination
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six falsification requirements the candidate operation universe must survive: (1) remove each candidate operation and test whether a mandatory distinction becomes impossible; (2) attempt to express each operation via the remaining operations (redundancy test); (3) test whether an operation actually belongs to another semantic layer (e.g. verify Serialize is not in O_sem); (4) determine whether an operation requires information not represented by candidate K (hidden dependency); (5) verify Authorize does not become an epistemic-status transition merely because it gates permitted transformations; (6) verify Replay does not require history to be treated as an instantaneous state component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\textbf{DERIVED — SUBSTANTIALLY ESTABLISHED}}$$ ... It does **not** yet prove: $$K_{minimal}$$ nor: $$\Sigma_{minimal}.$$

Establishes that KnowledgeOS requires a layered operation universe (State | Epistemic/Evidence | Observation | History | Governance) rather than one undifferentiated algebra, with representation/infrastructure kept outside the semantic kernel. Explicitly does not yet establish K_minimal or Sigma_minimal — those require the subsequent deletion/counterexample analysis (assigned to Step 273).

a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

a_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
a_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

a_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
a_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-2) discovers the Amendment 1 pointer correcting C-14's status was applied by a scripted first-match string replace and accidentally landed on the C-5 row instead, because both capabilities shared an identical look-alike table cell -- and it proposes extending the existing 'no automated search-and-replace on source code' rule's scope to any artifact with look-alike sites.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of a C-5-owned aggregate may disqualify a separate bounded context but must NOT be used as proof that the capability itself does not exist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refinement applied to C-5: absence of a C-5-owned authoritative aggregate/state disqualifies it from being its own bounded context but must not be read as evidence against the capability's existence -- an existence/category conflation the original analysis had committed for C-14 most clearly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not treat organizational independence as established in a single-operator environment. ... Single-operator constraint -- six separations, distinguished explicitly: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, external attestation.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-5's separation dimensions must distinguish six kinds: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, and external attestation; organizational independence must never be treated as established in a single-operator environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Material participation in producing the evidence being verified? YES, and this is decisive ... my Verification #2 findings W-1...W-6 fed the correction chain that runs into this artifact's lineage
b_rows_sample.statement: An independence gate is extended beyond mere non-authorship to material participation: a verifier whose own prior findings materially shaped a later correction chain is disqualified from verifying that chain's output, even without direct authorship of the artifact under review.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted

b_rows_sample.anchor: a unifying invariant candidate falls out of it: both control-plane capabilities are defeated by the SAME failure -- self-assertion by the gated party. C-5 is defeated by self-declared separation; C-14 by self-declared compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: organizational independence NOT_ESTABLISHED (not NOT_APPLICABLE) ... in a single-operator environment organizational independence is not among the achievable separations, and it MUST NOT be represented as established.
b_rows_sample.statement: A four-state model for separation dimensions is adopted (NOT_APPLICABLE, NOT_ESTABLISHED, ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED); organizational independence is corrected from the original 'not applicable / undefined' to NOT_ESTABLISHED, because NOT_APPLICABLE risks collapsing into PASS while NOT_ESTABLISHED correctly states a real, currently unsuppliable assurance gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: intra-platform third-party != external attestation ... A different process under the same operator, on the same filesystem -- that is evidence of process separation, not of externality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #3 adds external attestation as a sixth separation dimension at NOT_ESTABLISHED, and sharpens the distinction that a different process under the same operator establishing a fact (as Verification #3 did for SB-1) is process separation, never external attestation -- no party outside the platform has attested any separation claim in this estate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is C-5 -- separation attestation -- failing in production, on the very work item that is analysing it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding I-2, an explicit analogy: the estate's identity-attribution mechanism has produced both a false negative and a false positive on the same question within one day, on the exact work item studying separation attestation (C-5) -- framed as C-5 failing in production, recorded as evidence, with no ownership or OQ-A conclusion drawn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Producing a fresh analysis would create a second, competing C-5 model -- while the first is mid-verification (S5 ACTIVE, outstanding). That forks the subject under assurance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Search-before-modelling (ES-005.4) applied concretely: a commission to define C-5 fresh is refused because a 922-line canonical analysis already treats C-5 across four sections, and producing a competing model while the canonical one is mid-verification would fork the subject under active assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If I author this analysis I become a producer on the item I govern ... C-5 operating correctly forbids its own analysis being written by the party that governs the record it rests on. This refusal is itself C-5 evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential separation argument: Governance for the work item refuses to author a C-5 analysis because doing so would make it a producer on the item it governs -- the exact shape of defect §4 of the provenance reconciliation had just recorded -- and the refusal is offered as a third, live instance of C-5 evidence on the very work item studying C-5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLASSIFICATION: HISTORICAL VERIFICATION EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT / PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED ... ca6039a8 is neither deleted nor rewritten. Its substantive findings F-1...F-7 were separately adopted as verified findings by PO/ARB act and are not disturbed by this classification
b_rows_sample.statement: A defective-provenance classification vocabulary is introduced: an artifact can be classified HISTORICAL EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT while its substantive content (findings) remains adopted and undisturbed -- only the assurance/independence claim is refused, not the content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ca6039a8 was reclassified as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE + NOT INDEPENDENT/PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED -- not deleted, findings intact, only its ASSURANCE STATUS refused. That is exactly the shape of receipt invalidation ... invalidation is PURPOSE-SCOPED, not global.
b_rows_sample.statement: The earlier reclassification of the AMD2 verification artifact (ca6039a8) as historical-but-not-independent is offered as a real, worked instance of what 'receipt invalidation' should look like: invalidation is purpose-scoped (it removes assurance standing while leaving the content usable as evidence), not a global deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not import C-5's existence test automatically. Do not assume 'adopted invariant + performed capability' is a universal rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: The two-limb existence test derived from C-5's evidence (adopted invariant + performed capability) is explicitly declared not a universal rule to be imported automatically for other capabilities; C-10 must construct its own establishment test rather than inherit C-5's.
