a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
a_rows_sample.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q2 — which decisions does it explicitly model? ... Eight — all of one family
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight decisions are explicitly modeled, all of one family (the flow of knowledge and artifacts through governed work), grouped by question: 'Where does it belong?' (DetermineConcern, DeterminePlacement - mechanized by doc-placement.php); 'What is it/does it live?' (DetermineArtifactLifecycle - deletion litmus, DetermineArtifactType); 'Is it worth keeping/raising?' (DetermineReusePotential - Harvest, DeterminePromotionPath - ladder entry); 'What governs/verifies it?' (DetermineApplicableStandards, DetermineQualificationMethod). Deliberately excluded: ADR-making, capability approval, authority acts, promotion rulings — 'promotion is a human governance act and is never automated'; 'the AI evaluates and recommends — authority remains with governance.' The absence of governance decisions from the catalog is design, not gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q3 — which discovered decisions are not represented? ... FREEZE and RETIRE extend nothing in the catalog
a_rows_sample.statement: Answered in a prior Discovery pass and carried forward unchanged: FREEZE (n>=3, undeclared authority) and RETIRE (PM-6) extend nothing in the catalog, submitted as insufficiency evidence per the model's own stopping rule. Implicit but exercised: the challenge-commissioning trigger and terminology adoption. Nothing further found in this pass, which per the stopping rule is the correct amount.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q4 — does it govern the full ladder, or only architecture decisions? ... NEITHER — and the answer is the INVERSE of the commission's suspicion
a_rows_sample.statement: The model governs zero architecture decisions (no DetermineArchitectureDecision exists; ADRs are governance acts, outside the catalog by design). What it governs on the ladder Observation->Hypothesis->Evidence->Principle->Architecture is the entry points, not the rungs: DetermineReusePotential opens the ladder (observation->candidate); DeterminePromotionPath routes onto it (candidate->pilot->qualification->ARB decides). The rungs belong to ES-006.1, and the model correctly refuses to own them since it is an index, never a second rulebook.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q5 — Knowledge Governance or only Engineering Governance? ... Engineering Governance NOW; Knowledge Governance ANTICIPATED
a_rows_sample.statement: The model's own Decision Catalogs table states Engineering Standards answer the catalog's Engineering Decisions, while Project-Knowledge-class Knowledge Decisions (DetermineKnowledgeNeed, Source, Representation, Qualification, Promotion) are 'pilot-gated candidates — arrive only with pilot evidence; same pattern, different domain.' Engineering Governance is present now; Knowledge Governance is anticipated with the arrival condition already stated, and the entire ontology/meta-model corpus of this programme is exactly the kind of pilot evidence the anticipated catalog says it is waiting for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
a_rows_sample.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q7 — would a second decision model violate ubiquitous language? ... YES — three times over
a_rows_sample.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-EDV-1 | Does the DA intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog (§5) to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-EDV-1: does the Decision Authority intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced — waits on the ARB, natural companion to D-8.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-EDV-2 | The model's adoption test (one real cycle of conscious use) — unevenly met (U-DM-4, carried)
a_rows_sample.statement: U-EDV-2: the model's adoption test (one real cycle of conscious use) is unevenly met (U-DM-4, carried forward), waiting on EP-02 of the next real cycle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DP-n as a distinct layer between principle and capability ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — needs operational proof
a_rows_sample.statement: DP-n as a distinct architectural layer between principle and capability has no direct external counterpart found (policy-as-code practice is only adjacent); it remains a unique hypothesis requiring operational proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
a_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RESULT: THE MODEL DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT. One claim FALSIFIED · two WEAKENED · two SURVIVED · two unchanged
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall falsification result: of the domain model's claims, one is falsified, two weakened, two survived, two unchanged; the strongest claim in the model (D-2) was among those weakened, by evidence the model itself had cited. Method: every test executed against artifacts, not reasoned from the model, using the repository's own instruments (Round47-OP's nine admissible justifications, the R16 Workbook Strong/Medium/Weak scale); four falsifiers were sought, three landed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: W-1 · D-2's "own decision series" is a shared authority — two of four grounds fall
a_rows_sample.statement: D-2's claim of 'its own decision series, ADR-M distinct from ADR-AIP' is weakened: Round39-D6's header states decision authority for all ADRs is 'sponsor + ARB' and amendment requires sponsor+ARB approval, so ADR-M is a scoping device under a shared authority, not a separate authority. Its claim of 'independent evolution' is falsified: Round39-D6 states the ADRs 'were authored together on 2026-06-25' — a series written in one sitting evidences independent subject, never independent evolution over time. This matches the ARB Chair's named falsifier 'ADR separation is historical rather than semantic' — half true: separation is real in subject, absent in time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S-3 · D-1 survives every falsifier
a_rows_sample.statement: D-1 survives every falsifier sought: no multiple owners of the same concept found (DA/ARB throughout), no changes that fail to co-occur (ES set moves under STANDARDS_INDEX), no forced co-evolution with a product (ratification and freeze are product-independent), no absent invariants (append-only rulings, R-46).

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-1 | Was Round39-MC adopted by sponsor authority BECAUSE D-2 is independent, or DESPITE it being part of D-1?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-1: was Round39-MC adopted because D-2 is independent, or despite it being part of D-1 — the artifacts record the act but never the reason; only the sponsor and ARB know, and the model's validity turns on it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-4 | Is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced, or was it stated once?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-4: is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced or was it stated once — stated 2026-06-25, no subsequent enforcement event found.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-6 | Does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-6: does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers — carried forward, now sharper: shared ARB suggests peers-under-one-authority, not hierarchy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation — per domain ... The model as a whole | REVISE, then re-test ... NOT canonical
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain recommendations: D-1 ACCEPT; D-2 REVISE (restate the boundary on the one surviving ground, Round39-D6's scope exclusion; delete 'own decision series' and 'independent evolution' as grounds); D-3 DEFER (untestable at n=1, revisit when a second runtime adapter exists); D-6a DEFER, D-6b ACCEPT; D-5 ACCEPT the demotion (do not promote until ARB overturns H-CAT-1 on evidence); D-4 ACCEPT the rejection; D-7 REVISE (restate as an observation of one instance, record PKS-as-projection as falsified). Overall the model as a whole: REVISE then re-test, NOT canonical — 2 of 8 accept, 3 revise, 2 defer, 1 accept-as-rejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the real ownership map is the space map
b_rows_sample.statement: Where ownership DOES change, the boundary is a SPACE, not a viewpoint: platform (DA) -> EKP (nab.raj.sharma) -> product (the producing track). This claim is downgraded from finding to hypothesis in REV 2 because it was observed on one platform instance only; generalizing it as an architectural property requires KnowledgeOS applied elsewhere (the second-adopter gate).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-VO-4 | Whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's REAL context map
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknown U-VO-4: whether space-ownership (platform/EKP/product) is the platform's real context map — the strongest candidate reading of Finding 1 — deliberately left as a strategic-DDD question for humans, not answered by the author.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Space —generates→ Projection —attested→ authoritative | HIGH
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-4: Space generates Projection, attested to become authoritative. External support: CQRS (read models rebuildable, non-authoritative) plus audit/signature practice and data-product certification. No challenge — the corrected form IS the standard model. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-9: a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary and spaces nest (deployment = nested space). External support: bounded contexts (CANONICAL), data-mesh domains (boundary+owner). Challenge: nesting is less standardized than bounding. b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Space as declared boundary + owner + constitution is supported by bounded contexts (Evans), data-mesh domain ownership, and SKOS concept schemes. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — review 2026-08-03 (1420), three amendments annotated, none rewritten
b_rows_sample.statement: Three amendments: (1) the 'nine kinds' are held as candidate archetypes, not frozen primitives, until MM-1 resolves whether KIND is itself a dimension; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE, since its distinguishing edge ('generates Projections') is observed in only one space (the EKP) and nesting is unevidenced (H-3); (3) PURPOSE is flagged for its own investigation (U-MM-4, waits on D-5).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kinds the candidates missed but the passes repeatedly found: PURPOSE · CONTAINER · PROJECTION
b_rows_sample.statement: Three additional kinds were repeatedly found by the passes but missing from the A-G candidate list: PURPOSE (mission/vision, found twice in the Relationship Ontology), CONTAINER (Knowledge Space — declared boundary, nesting), and PROJECTION (derived, operating in production).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Classification — every gap from the projection ... G-1..G-5
b_rows_sample.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. G-3 (external authority/CONSTRAINS) is BEHAVIORAL, a missing relationship (obligation != ownership), belongs to GOVERNANCE. G-4 (PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT/INSTANTIATES) is STRUCTURAL but dissolves: a deployment is a nested Knowledge Space, so it belongs to ONTOLOGY as resolved, no new concept. G-5 (Runtime Adapter disappeared in both new domains) is STRUCTURAL but is a confirmation of Hexagonal behaving correctly, not a failure.

b_rows_sample.statement: H-3 (the nesting question) is answered by G-4: Knowledge Spaces nest, and a deployment is the nested case. No new concept was introduced; the ontology already explained the evidence, which is the test the commission set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
b_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. The chain in section 2 is completed by naming DP-n (DESIGN POLICY) as the anchor stopping capabilities from floating, observable in the Capability Catalog's 1:1 CAP->DP binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE — admitted, and the evidence is a boundary, not a folder ... A Knowledge Space is not a folder. It is a DECLARED SCOPE with an owner and a governing constitution
b_rows_sample.statement: KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted, evidenced by: knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include; three registered documentation roots (knowledgeos, pks, publicdigit); ES-005.1's three concerns (Product, Platform, Runtime mount); the EKP having its own constitution and owner. A Knowledge Space is a declared scope with an owner and a governing constitution, not a folder — which is why the '13% coverage' question was a scope decision, not a bug.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
b_rows_sample.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RO-2 | Are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent?
b_rows_sample.statement: RO-2: are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent (H-3) — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three challenges — accepted, and one is settled by my own evidence rules ... CONTAINER demoted CONFIRMED → CANDIDATE ... my own admission rule decides it, not deference
b_rows_sample.statement: Three reviewer challenges: (1) 'Archetype' replaces 'nine kinds' until MM-1, since 'archetype' already exists in the corpus (RQ-002) so the rename mints nothing — a ubiquitous-language decision, decided with governance (MM-1), not unilaterally; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE by the author's own admission rule: 'Containers generate Projections' is observed in exactly one space (the EKP's knowledge-graph.php), n=1, and nesting is unevidenced (H-3) — the settling test is a second generating space (confirms) or a capability-plus-scope reduction (refutes); (3) PURPOSE, possibly more fundamental than Container, is flagged not resolved, since the mission is enacted and unratified (D-5 pending), and deepening PURPOSE before ratification would model ahead of the domain expert — recorded as hypothesis U-ONT-2, n=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is a Knowledge State that is sufficiently complete, coherent, and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Q23 definition: a decision-ready state is a Knowledge State sufficiently complete, coherent and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence. Boxed: Decision-Ready ≠ Complete; Decision-Ready = Sufficient for Purpose; Stop Condition = f(Sufficiency, Cost, Urgency, Risk, Policy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ShouldStop(S_t, P_t, C_t, Policy_t) \in \{\text{True}, \text{False}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: The Stop Condition Framework: ShouldStop(S_t,P_t,C_t,Policy_t) is a boolean function of six criteria (Sufficiency S_u, Diminishing Returns D_r, Time/Cost T_c, Urgency U_r, Risk R_i, Policy P_o), combined as ShouldStop = Sufficient(S_t,P_t) ∨ BudgetExhausted(S_t,T_c) ∨ UrgencyThreshold(S_t,U_r) ∨ PolicyStop(S_t,P_o).

type_signature.domain: system state x purpose x context x policy

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(S_t, P_t) = \text{KnowledgeSufficient}(K_t, I^K_t) \land \text{UnderstandingSufficient}(U_t, I^U_t) \land \text{DomainSufficient}(X_t, I^D_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Sufficiency is decomposed into Knowledge, Understanding and Domain sufficiency: Knowledge sufficient requires all ideal dimensions represented (D_I ⊆ D_Kt), all critical values known, all critical epistemic states meeting a threshold Σ_I, all critical relationships represented, and coherence maintained. Understanding sufficient requires conceptual understanding, implications understanding, uncertainty and conflict-resolution each meeting thresholds. Domain sufficient requires reality meeting constraints (X_t ⊨ C_I) and performance meeting a threshold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{DiminishingReturns}(S_t) = \text{ExpectedValue}(\text{NextInvestigation}) < \text{Cost}(\text{NextInvestigation})
a_rows_sample.statement: Diminishing returns occur when the expected value of the next investigation step is less than its cost; ExpectedValue(d) = Impact(d) x Probability(d is actionable) x Severity(d); Cost(d) = Time(d) + Effort(d) + Resources(d).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Readiness = w_K \cdot K_c + w_U \cdot U_d + w_C \cdot C_r + w_{U_l} \cdot (1 - U_l) + w_D \cdot D_i + w_R \cdot R_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Readiness function: a weighted scalar in [0,1] over six factors (Knowledge Completeness K_c, Understanding Depth U_d, Conflict Resolution C_r, Uncertainty Level U_l, Decision Impact D_i, Risk Tolerance R_t); DecisionReady(S_t,P_t) iff Readiness(S_t,P_t) >= Threshold(P_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 8. The Arjuna Example: Stop Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Walkthrough of Arjuna's decision states S0 (insufficient knowledge/understanding/domain, continue), S1 (partially sufficient after observation, continue), S2 (sufficient after moral resolution, STOP and present decision-ready state); stop criteria table shows sufficiency, diminishing returns, urgency and risk all favoring Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady \neq ShouldStop
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction to Q23: the original equation ShouldStop = Sufficient ∨ BudgetExhausted ∨ UrgencyThreshold ∨ PolicyStop is 'too permissive' because it implies exhausting budget or reaching urgency can make a state decision-ready, which is not epistemically correct. Fundamental distinction established: DecisionReady ≠ ShouldStop, and a forced stop does not mean the system is decision-ready (Stop ⇏ DecisionReady). Three outcomes of investigation identified: Decision-Ready→STOP, Not Ready→Continue, Not Ready→Forced Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown \neq Not\ Decision\ Ready
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction: the requirement that all critical dimension values be 'known' is too strong — some values can remain unknown while the decision is still valid if the uncertainty is decision-irrelevant (example: not knowing whether a probability is 17% or 18% when both lead to the same decision). Replaces with DecisionRelevantUncertainty(S_t,D) ≤ T_D, a policy-defined tolerance T_D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Case C — Decision-critical unresolved conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'conflicts resolved or accepted' into three ConflictStatus cases: (A) Resolved; (B) Accepted as unresolved (Knower explicitly accepts the uncertainty/conflict); (C) Active and decision-critical unresolved conflict, in which case DecisionReady = False. 'Accepted' therefore cannot automatically mean readiness.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Knowledge = 95%
Understanding = 95%
Conflict Resolution = 95%
Critical unresolved safety conflict = YES
a_rows_sample.statement: The weighted-average Readiness score assumes all dimensions are compensable: a hypothetical case with 95% knowledge/understanding/conflict-resolution but an unresolved critical safety conflict could still average to Readiness=0.9 and incorrectly declare the state decision-ready. Presented as the counterexample motivating replacement of the scalar formula.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady = \bigwedge_i G_i \land SoftCriteriaSatisfied
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the compensable weighted scalar with a hard-gates-plus-soft-indicators architecture: non-negotiable hard constraints G_1..G_n (e.g. G1=Coherent(K_t), G2=NoDecisionCriticalConflict, G3=CriticalEvidenceSatisfied, G4=CriticalDimensionsSatisfied) must all hold, DecisionReady = (⋀_i G_i) ∧ SoftCriteriaSatisfied. Readiness is redefined as a structured triple (HardGates, SoftIndicators, RemainingDeficiencies) rather than a scalar in [0,1]; a scalar R_score=f(SoftIndicators) may still be derived for UI purposes but must never override hard constraints. States the principle: 'Structured state is fundamental; scalar measurements are derived,' attributed as following from Q19/Q22.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI = Expected\ Value\ of\ Information
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the diminishing-returns formula to account for decision impact via the Expected Value of Sample/Information (EVSI): EVSI(a) = E[decision quality after information] − decision quality now; continue investigation when expected decision benefit exceeds cost/risk. Flagged as an optional decision-theoretic mechanism, not a universal mathematical truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status = ForcedStopNotReady
a_rows_sample.statement: Urgency must not produce false readiness: 'Not sufficient + Urgent = STOP' is operationally fine but must produce Status = ForcedStopNotReady, not DecisionReady = True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discrepancy \rightarrow Findings \rightarrow Resolution Opportunities \rightarrow Prioritization \rightarrow Investigation \rightarrow Decision Sufficiency \rightarrow Decision Posture
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall assessment gives the original Q23 scores Conceptual 8/10, Mathematical 6.5/10, DDD 7.5/10, expecting 9.5/9/9.5 after corrections. States the central architectural insight: KnowledgeOS does not decide when 'enough knowledge' exists in the abstract, but whether enough decision-relevant knowledge exists for this Knower, this purpose, this context, and this decision — giving a progression chain from Discrepancy through Findings, Resolution Opportunities, Prioritization, Investigation, Decision Sufficiency, to Decision Posture (Q19→Q22→Q23).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution \neq \Delta=\emptyset
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the previous Arjuna example's claim 'After Moral Resolution -> Δ=∅' as a very important correction: even after normative resolution, uncertainty/risk/incomplete domain knowledge/emotional difficulty/consequences may remain, so Resolution ≠ Δ=∅; DecisionReady(Δ,P) may hold even though Δ≠∅. Generalized to abandon 'Δ=∅ ⇒ Success' entirely: DecisionReady=CriteriaSatisfied, not DecisionReady=NoRemainingGaps, so CompleteKnowledge is unnecessary for action — 'a very important property for a real engineering system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady(S,C) \iff DecisionCriteria(S,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that 'DecisionReady does not require Δ=∅' remains architecturally correct but is the theory's own engineering inference, not a theorem Chapter 3 itself establishes: DecisionReady(S,C) ⟺ DecisionCriteria(S,C), not DecisionReady ⟺ Δ=∅ — a design principle derived from the case, not a claim about the text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 20 — What is the complete system state, and how does it evolve?
a_rows_sample.statement: Fragment listing question prompts without worked answers: Q16 'How do observation, evidence, inference, contradiction, uncertainty and resolution change epistemic status?'; Q17/Q19 (duplicated) 'How do we mathematically measure the difference between K_t and the relevant Ideal State without reducing fundamentally different deficiencies to an arbitrary scalar?'; a differently-numbered 'Question 17 — How do Zero, Lord, and Sārathi interact with the transition system?'; Question 20 'What is the complete system state, and how does it evolve?'; Question 21 'How do we prioritize which deficiencies to address first?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DSB(P,D,C)
b_rows_sample.statement: A revised, decision-relative definition: DecisionReady(S_t,P) ⟺ MeetsDecisionCriteria(S_t,P). Sufficiency is not intrinsic to knowledge — Sufficient(K_t,P_1) ≠ Sufficient(K_t,P_2) in general — so sufficiency should be made explicit in a decision D: Sufficient(S_t,P,D). The Ideal State (I^K_t, I^U_t, I^D_t) should define a minimum, not perfection; otherwise investigation becomes potentially infinite. Introduces a Decision Sufficiency Boundary DSB(P,D,C): the minimum conditions under which a decision may responsibly be made, giving DecisionReady ⟺ K_t ⊨ DSB(P,D,C).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ready(S_t,D_1) \not\Rightarrow Ready(S_t,D_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Arjuna example is corrected: readiness must be asked 'sufficient for which decision?' Decision A ('Who is on the opposing side?') can become ready quickly; Decision B ('Should I fight?') requires much richer understanding; Decision C ('What is the morally correct action?') requires another Ideal Knowledge/Understanding model. Establishes Ready(S_t,D_1) ⇏ Ready(S_t,D_2) as a fundamental property of the theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would replace the current definition with
b_rows_sample.statement: Final recommended definition: 'A decision-ready state is a KnowledgeOS state in which the knowledge and understanding relevant to a specific decision satisfy the decision's mandatory epistemic, coherence, contextual, and domain constraints, while all remaining deficiencies are either decision-irrelevant or explicitly acceptable under the governing policy.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) ⟺ HardGates(S_t,D,P,C) ∧ AcceptableRemainingUncertainty(S_t,D,P,C). Also states StopInvestigation ≠ DecisionReady as a separate operational decision.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'decision-sufficiency-boundary' POSSIBLY relates to 'decision-readiness-stop-condition-model' (batch B0020). Note: The minimum conditions under which a decision may responsibly be made, introduced to correct Q23's over-strong 'all critical values known' sufficiency requirement; DecisionReady ⟺ K_t ⊨ DSB(P,D,C).

a_rows_sample.anchor: most probable outcome\Rightarrow best action ... mathematically wrong in general ... Knowledge\rightarrow Prediction\rightarrow Consequences\rightarrow Utility/Risk\rightarrow Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the implicit assumption 'most probable outcome => best action' as mathematically wrong in general, establishing the correct chain Knowledge->Prediction->Consequences->Utility/Risk->Decision, plus a Decision<->ValueOfInformation relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision is not inference ... S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\} ... A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\} ... decision theory evaluates a\in A under uncertainty about s\in S
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference ('what do we believe?') from decision ('what should we do?'), formalizing state space S and action space A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(a,s) ... EU(a\mid E)=\sum_s P(s\mid E)U(a,s) ... a^*=\arg\max_a EU(a\mid E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines utility U(a,s), expected utility EU(a|E)=sum_s P(s|E)U(a,s), and the rational-choice rule a*=argmax_a EU(a|E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(Outage\mid Upgrade)=0.05 ... tells us almost nothing ... U(Upgrade,Outage) and U(DoNothing,Outage) ... the decision emerges from the whole consequence structure
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example/table showing a bare 5% outage probability tells almost nothing about whether to upgrade absent the full action/outcome/consequence structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Risk=Probability ... ExpectedLoss=\sum_s P(s\mid E)L(a,s) ... real risk can involve multiple outcomes; uncertainty intervals; catastrophic tails; irreversibility; regulatory consequences; opportunity costs
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects reducing Risk to Probability, defining ExpectedLoss=sum_s P(s|E)L(a,s) and listing six additional real-risk dimensions beyond a single probability number.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action A: P(Loss=10000)=0.10 ... Action B: P(Loss=1000000)=0.001 ... same expected loss ... TailRisk is dramatically larger ... ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked tail-risk example: two actions with identical expected loss (1000) but vastly different catastrophic-tail severity may be rationally treated differently — 'ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient'; risk policy must specify how severe/irreversible outcomes are treated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(\euro x)=\sqrt{x} ... UtilityFunction is a normative choice. KnowledgeOS should not secretly invent one
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes utility functions (e.g. sqrt(x)) can encode risk aversion but are a normative organizational choice that KnowledgeOS must not secretly invent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionContract=(Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) ... a very important DDD concept
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-field DecisionContract (Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) as an important DDD concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a_1)>EU(a_2) but Authorized(a_1)=False ... a^*=\arg\max_{a\in A_{admissible}}EU(a) ... Optimization occurs within admissible actions
a_rows_sample.statement: States optimization occurs within admissible actions only: an unauthorized highest-utility action must not execute — a*=argmax over A_admissible, not all of A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalRiskTooHigh or GovernanceAuthorizationMissing or EvidenceInsufficient ... DecisionStatus: blocked, Reason: governance_authorization_missing
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires Sarathi to distinguish blocking-failure reasons (technical risk, governance authorization missing, evidence insufficient) via a structured DecisionStatus=blocked+Reason record, rather than a bare 'decision=no.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: a^*=Upgrade [recommendation] ... does not necessarily mean Decision=Approved ... Recommendation\neq Decision\neq Authorization
a_rows_sample.statement: States Recommendation ≠ Decision ≠ Authorization: an AI-computed optimum is only a Recommendation until an authorized human/body decides.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi as a decision-support/decision-orchestration intelligence, not as an autonomous source of authority ... Sarathi:(K,Models,Constraints)\rightarrow DecisionCandidate ... Authorize(DecisionCandidate)
a_rows_sample.statement: Characterizes Sarathi as decision-support/orchestration intelligence producing a DecisionCandidate, with governance separately determining Authorize(DecisionCandidate).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord may choose between Action and InformationAcquisition ... Option 1 make decision now ... Option 4 ask human expert ... the system therefore performs meta-decision-making
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord's role as choosing between Action and InformationAcquisition, worked with a four-option example (decide now, collect observation, run simulation, ask human expert) — 'the system performs meta-decision-making.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: VOI=EU(\text{best decision after information})-EU(\text{best decision now}) ... VOI(E)=E_e[\max_a EU(a\mid E,e)]-\max_a EU(a\mid E) ... one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Value of Information via two equivalent expressions, called 'one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(Upgrade)=100, EU(DoNothing)=95 ... VOI(Inspection)=20, Cost(Inspection)=5 ... NetVOI=20-5=15>0 ... AcquireInformation is itself the rational action ... gives Zero a mathematical foundation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: given EU(Upgrade)=100 vs EU(DoNothing)=95, a candidate inspection with VOI=20 and Cost=5 yields NetVOI=15>0, making AcquireInformation itself rational — 'gives Zero a mathematical foundation.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{epistemic} from Zero_{decision} ... a missing fact matters only if resolving it could change something important ... DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero into Zero_epistemic vs Zero_decision: a knowledge gap matters only if resolving it could change something important — DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap is more important than arbitrary missing information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which Linux kernel version is installed on a test server? ... VOI\approx0 ... Lord should do nothing ... prevents KnowledgeOS from endlessly trying to make itself complete
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a genuine knowledge gap with VOI≈0 for the current decision means Lord should take no action — prevents pursuing exhaustive completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: should not optimize for CompleteKnowledge. We should optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision ... much more realistic
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision, not CompleteKnowledge — 'both computationally and operationally much more realistic.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\} ... ReadConfiguration, AskHumanExpert, RunTest, QueryAPI, RunSimulation ... i^*=\arg\max_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] ... a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes information-gathering actions as a candidate set I with per-action Cost and VOI, giving i*=argmax_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] as 'a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Restart production server to verify configuration ... Risk(Restart)>0 ... NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) ... Lord cannot blindly maximize information
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing an information-gathering action (production restart) can itself carry risk, extending net value to NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) — 'Lord cannot blindly maximize information.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference asks what can we conclude from what we know. Step 34 asks What should we learn next? ... a fundamentally different problem
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference from information-acquisition selection as fundamentally different problems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10^6 uncertain assertions ... impossible and unnecessary to validate all of them immediately ... Choose the information acquisition action that produces the greatest useful improvement relative to its cost
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS should not investigate everything, requiring a cost-relative optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: QueryCMDB, InspectRuntime, AskDomainExpert, RunTest, PerformExperiment, RetrieveDocument, CompareIndependentSource ... produces an observation Y_I
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the information-gathering action set with seven worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cost(I) ... Time, Money, Compute, HumanAttention, OperationalRisk ... information is not free
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Cost(I) across five components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI=L_0-L_{PI} ... an upper bound on the value of information
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as an upper bound.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=L_0-E_Y[\min_d E[L(d,\theta)\mid K,Y]] ... NVOI(I)=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) ... the core mathematical idea
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Sample Information and net value of information as the step's core idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^*=\arg\max_{I\in\mathcal I}NVOI(I) ... our first formal definition of NextBestEpistemicAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first formal Next-Best-Epistemic-Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: InformationValue\neq UncertaintyReduction ... A has no influence on any important decision ... UncertaintyReduction(A) may have almost zero practical value
b_rows_sample.statement: States the subtle principle that information value is not the same as uncertainty reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionSensitivity(A,D) ... Information about A is valuable if learning A can change d^*
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines DecisionSensitivity as the criterion for information value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus has 31 GB RAM ... migration architecture does not depend on RAM beyond a very large safety margin ... almost no decision value
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of low-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (RAM precision beyond safety margin).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Production database backup is restorable ... DecisionSensitivity(B,D) is very high ... validating B may have extremely high VOI
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting example of high-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (backup restorability).

b_rows_sample.anchor: d^*=f(K) ... If perturbing A does not change f(K), then A has low local decision sensitivity
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a decision-relevance partition via perturbation of the decision function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(A) ... A\rightarrow B\rightarrow D ... DependencyClosure+DecisionCriticality=EpistemicPrioritization
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines Step 32's dependency closure with decision dependency, giving a prioritization formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(D) ... Low, Medium, High, Critical ... should be domain-owned. KnowledgeOS can consume it but should not invent the business meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a domain-owned Criticality classification, not invented by KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL(d)=E[L(d,\theta)\mid K] ... d^*=\arg\min_d EL(d) ... d_1 expected loss 10, d_2 expected loss 12 ... investigation may reveal a high-risk state in which d_2 becomes preferable
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected loss and current-optimal decision, worked with a two-decision expected-loss-reversal example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk<5\%\Rightarrow AutomaticApproval ... Risk\in[3\%,8\%] ... DecisionBoundaryUncertainty. Uncertainty far from a decision boundary may be harmless. Uncertainty near a boundary can be critical
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DecisionBoundaryUncertainty, worked with a threshold-straddling risk-interval example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk\in[1\%,2\%] ... no urgent investigation ... Risk\in[4\%,7\%] crosses the decision boundary ... additional evidence is valuable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting examples of harmless-far and critical-boundary-straddling risk intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(A)\propto DecisionImpact(A)\times Uncertainty(A) ... conceptual, not yet a universal formula
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual, not-yet-universal epistemic-triage priority formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=10, Cost(I)=2, NVOI(I)=8 ... EVSI=12, Cost=20, NVOI=-8 ... should not be prioritized merely because it provides more information
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked arithmetic example showing higher-EVSI investigations can have lower net value once cost is subtracted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanAttention is an epistemic resource ... 2 hours of a senior architect's time may be more expensive than a machine-readable check
b_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is itself a costed epistemic resource, worked with a comparison example.
