a_rows_sample.anchor: Take P which is epistemically well-supported but administratively rejected. ... Epistemic and Governance status must be tested as orthogonal dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes testing (not yet establishing) that EpistemicStatus and GovernanceStatus are orthogonal dimensions, illustrated by a proposition that is epistemically Supported yet administratively Rejected, and by an Epistemically-Unknown proposition coexisting with GovernanceStatus=AcceptedForInvestigation; if such states are meaningful, one scalar status cannot represent both dimensions without information loss.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A single status enum must encode the cross-product of every fact any decision reads. ... A one-dimensional Sigma is provably inadequate: it would need {n} values. The distinctions are NOT one axis. They are at least FIVE orthogonal facts.
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-21/22 define ten constructed situations (never-asked, asked-nothing-found, one-supporting-item, meets-policy-bar, support+accepted, support+rejected, refuting-evidence, both-directions, replaced-by-newer, was-valid-now-expired) and nine theory-required downstream decisions as functions of each situation, computing a 'decision signature' per situation; groups situations by identical signatures to find how many distinct situations must be distinguishable, then maps each decision to the underlying facts it reads (asked, evidence, authority, supersession, validity), showing the worst-case cross-product of these five facts' arities (2x4x3x2x2=96) would be needed by any single-dimensional status enum, proving a one-dimensional Sigma is provably inadequate and the distinctions form at least five orthogonal facts, not one axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every axis whose removal produces a HARMFUL collision is IRREDUCIBLE ... This is the necessity demonstration the mandate asks for, and it is produced WITHOUT choosing any vocabulary. ... Putting these nine words in ONE enum conflates four independent axes.
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-23 tests each of the five candidate axes (asked, evidence, authority, supersession, validity) for irreducibility by dropping it and checking whether any two situations that a required decision must separate become identical (a 'harmful collision'); finds each axis is irreducible; concludes the corpus's nine status words (Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted reading the evidence axis; Accepted/Rejected reading the authority axis; Superseded reading the supersession axis; Invalidated/Stale reading the validity axis) conflate four independent axes when placed in a single enum, and identifies Contested as reading a sixth, entirely unmodeled fact (an open process) -- concluding the vocabulary question is downstream of this axis-count finding and does not itself require a human decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ten situations were modelled from corpus material ... 10 situations -> 10 distinct decision signatures (no two situations produce the same set of decisions). ... any Sigma carrying fewer than ten distinguishable states cannot support the decisions the corpus already requires. This immediately rules out the three-value ladders ... as a COMPLETE Sigma. They are adequate as ONE AXIS, not as Sigma.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding SG-1: all ten corpus-derived situations produce mutually distinct decision signatures under the nine required decisions, so no situation is redundant and any Sigma with fewer than ten distinguishable states cannot support the corpus's own required decisions, ruling out the corpus's running three-value ladder (Candidate<Supported<Accepted, verified running in ladder_dc_reference.py) as a complete Sigma -- it is adequate only as one axis among several.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A one-dimensional Sigma would need 96 values. The distinctions the corpus requires are FIVE orthogonal facts, not one enum. ... Putting these nine words in one enum conflates four independent axes. ... This subsumes the corpus's EpistemicStatus != GovernanceStatus result (ARC D). That result is correct but insufficient: it separates two axes where five are needed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding SG-2: maps each of nine required decisions to the underlying fact(s) it reads (asked, evidence, authority, supersession, validity), computes the worst-case cross-product (96 states) that a single-dimensional enum would need, and concludes Sigma requires five orthogonal axes, not one; assigns each corpus status word to its actual axis (Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted->evidence; Accepted/Rejected->authority; Superseded->supersession; Invalidated/Stale->validity; Contested->a process fact; Candidate->ambiguous across two axes), showing nine words in one enum conflate four independent axes; states this subsumes but strictly refines the corpus's own EpistemicStatus!=GovernanceStatus separation (ARC D) as correct-but-insufficient (2 axes separated where 5 are needed).

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'sigma-necessity-decomposition' POSSIBLY relates to 'epistemic-vs-governance-status-orthogonality' (batch B0041). Note: A vocabulary-independent necessity test: ten constructed situations are checked against nine theory-required downstream decisions to derive how many distinct status values and axes are mathematically necessary, finding at least five orthogonal irreducible facts (asked, evidence, authority, supersession, validity) plus a sixth unmodeled fact (an open contest process) -- refuting any single-axis or naive single-enum Sigma.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a person may have insufficient evidence to establish a proposition, yet still need to act as if one hypothesis were true for practical or theoretical purposes. ... Claim: 'Hypothesis A is true' / Epistemic status: NOT_PROVEN / Decision: 'Proceed using A temporarily.' There is no contradiction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cook Wilson's epistemic-vs-practical-decision distinction, worked as an example: acting on a NOT_PROVEN hypothesis is not contradictory, strengthening the justification for keeping a Decision Boundary strictly outside the Knowledge Core (NOT_PROVEN does not imply DO_NOT_ACT; VALIDATED does not imply MUST_ACT).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS preserves the governed relationships among questions, beliefs, claims, evidence, inquiry, assessment, epistemic standing, authority, revision and action without collapsing epistemic status into practical decision or representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the previous KnowledgeOS definition to explicitly include questions/beliefs/inquiry/action and the non-collapse of epistemic status into practical decision or representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Higher stakes demand greater assurance for rational action. ... Epistemic status != decision threshold. Outside Kernel: Risk policy, Decision threshold, Safety policy, Regulatory assurance, Business impact. ... Moral considerations ... should influence decision/governance policies, not redefine the meaning of epistemic truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Pragmatic encroachment (higher stakes demand more evidence) and moral encroachment are both explicitly kept outside the Kernel as decision/governance policy rather than redefinitions of epistemic truth: Epistemic status != decision threshold.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should therefore never model governance simply as: allowed = true/false. We need at least the semantic distinction: Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown and potentially: Recommended, Discouraged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a deontic-modal governance vocabulary (Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown, and potentially Recommended/Discouraged) as necessary to replace a naive boolean allowed=true/false governance model, since 'positive permission' Permitted(a), 'obligation' Required(a), and 'prohibition' Forbidden(a) are argued to be distinct semantic categories, closer to a policy/dharma model than an IF-condition-THEN-execute command system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Wisdom is not merely storing knowledge. It is continuously asking: What should I do? but equally: What should I refrain from doing? This gives us a second dimension to KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Wisdom is a second architectural dimension distinct from Knowledge->Determination->Decision->Action: Chapter 4 suggests Knowledge->Wisdom->Action Guidance, where Wisdom evaluates both action and non-action (DO/ACT vs DO NOT ACT) before the Decision/Action stage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A workflow should not assume: Decision => Action. Instead: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}. ... Insufficient Evidence => Do Not Determine and perhaps => SeekMoreEvidence. That is epistemic restraint.
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Do nothing' (and deferral/escalation/seeking more evidence) must be first-class Decision outcomes rather than an implicit fallback: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}; when evidence is insufficient a KnowledgeOS-governed agent should conclude 'Do Not Determine' / 'SeekMoreEvidence' rather than force an answer -- termed 'epistemic restraint'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have already established that: Evidence not=> Truth. Now Chapter 4 gives us another principle: Knowledge not=> Action. There must be an intermediate judgment: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.
b_rows_sample.statement: By analogy to the already-established 'Evidence does not imply Truth' principle, Chapter 4 is read as supplying a parallel principle 'Knowledge does not imply Action', requiring an intermediate Judgment stage: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint: A governed system must be capable of determining both what should be done and what should not be done. Therefore: Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and records 'Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint': a governed system must be able to determine both what should be done and what should not be done, formalized as Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The actor must know the limits of its own knowledge. This is perhaps the most important principle for AI. An agent should be able to say: I know this. I do not know this. I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it. ... That is epistemically mature architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a third principle, considered possibly the most important for AI: 'the actor must know the limits of its own knowledge', illustrated by a required repertoire of self-report statements (I know this / I do not know this / I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it / the system has historical evidence for this / the evidence is insufficient for action / the action is prohibited / the action requires authority), termed 'epistemically mature architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> (SHOULD DO / SHOULD NOT DO) -> DECISION -> (ACT/DEFER/REFRAIN) -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, and above all of it: PROVENANCE + LINEAGE
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the KnowledgeOS pipeline diagram (previously Knowledge->Inquiry->Evidence->Determination->Decision->Action) into a richer chain: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> {SHOULD DO, SHOULD NOT DO} -> DECISION -> {ACT, DEFER, REFRAIN} -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, with PROVENANCE + LINEAGE positioned as an overarching background layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would actually say Chapter 4 strengthens our architecture rather than forcing us to redesign it. Especially these existing decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly claims Chapter 4's material strengthens/validates (rather than forces redesign of) ten prior architecture decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should investigate whether Wisdom is a cross-cutting domain function: Wisdom: (Knowledge, Context, Evidence, Rules, Authority) -> (ActionGuidance) where ActionGuidance in {DO, DON'T, WAIT, ASK, ESCALATE, INVESTIGATE}. I don't necessarily mean creating a class called Wisdom. That would be premature.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the open question of whether Wisdom should be modeled as a cross-cutting domain function Wisdom: (Knowledge, Context, Evidence, Rules, Authority) -> ActionGuidance with ActionGuidance in {DO, DON'T, WAIT, ASK, ESCALATE, INVESTIGATE}, while explicitly warning against prematurely reifying it as a literal `Wisdom` class; frames this as the key question to examine before 'Step 158', concluding Chapter 4 may reveal a missing architectural layer: a governed mechanism converting knowledge into action or restraint, not another knowledge repository.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3C. Missing concepts ... Look for concepts that the reasoning requires but which were never explicitly modeled. Examples discovered during later reasoning may include: wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, epistemic restraint. Do not automatically accept these. Evaluate them against the complete corpus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly names wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, and epistemic restraint as candidate 'missing concepts' example categories to evaluate for Phase 3C -- directly referencing (and thereby corroborating the significance of) the Chapter-4-derived wisdom-action-guidance-function and historical-continuity-vs-accessible-memory material found elsewhere in this same batch (S1067), while cautioning these candidates must not be automatically accepted.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'wisdom-action-guidance-function' POSSIBLY relates to 'epistemic-vs-practical-decision-separation' (batch B0026). Note: Gita-Chapter-4-derived proposal that Wisdom is a cross-cutting domain function mapping Knowledge/Context/Evidence/Rules/Authority to an ActionGuidance value drawn from a deontic vocabulary (Required/Permitted/Forbidden/Unknown, Do/Refrain/Defer/Escalate/Investigate), explicitly not to be reified as a literal Wisdom class; parallels but is not identical to the prior epistemic-vs-practical-decision-separation object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: equiv <-> approx <-> congruence ... Flagged in the corpus as the N-1 conflict. ... An SCC on the critical path cannot be resolved by ordering the work. It is broken either by O fixing the quantifier (approx is for-all O in O_K) or by a stipulation. This is a further reason the root is O.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 6: identifies a strongly-connected cycle equiv<->approx<->congruence on the critical path (the corpus's own N-1 conflict, built from four separately-cited directional edges), arguing an SCC cannot be resolved by reordering work -- it must be broken either by O_core fixing the universal quantifier inside approx (defined as for-all o in O_K) or by an explicit stipulation -- offered as a further reason to treat O_core as the analytical root.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x equiv_sem y iff same semantic object under the specified identity semantics. x approx_{Q,Gamma} y iff indistinguishable w.r.t. inquiry Q. x ~_O y iff for all o in O: o(x) equiv_sem o(y). ... The cycle is an artifact of untyped reuse of one symbol, not a genuine circularity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 8: restores a typed hierarchy among the three previously conflated relation symbols: x≡_sem y (semantic identity under specified semantics), x≈_{Q,Gamma} y (inquiry/context-relative indistinguishability), x~_O y (congruence: agreement under every operation in O), with ≡_sem⇒≈_{Q,Gamma} and ≡_sem+O⇒congruence_O valid but not the reverse (≈_{Q,Gamma}⇏≡_sem); claims this matches the corpus's own prior finding (CR-4) that the executable tester is ≈_{Q,Gamma,O} not ≡_sem, plus a representation-adequacy result about answering the same questions while differing elsewhere; concludes the apparent ≡⇄≈⇄congruence cycle is an artifact of untyped symbol reuse, broken by stipulating the typing (itself a recorded act).

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'equiv-approx-congruence-cycle-root-reason' POSSIBLY relates to 'equiv-approx-congruence-typed-hierarchy' (batch B0067). Note: The strongly-connected equiv/approx/congruence cycle used as a further argument for O_core being the analytical root; related to the typed-hierarchy resolution proposed later in S2788.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Until now we have used Zero intuitively as 'the gap between where we are and where we need to be.' We now need to make that statement mathematically precise. The decisive test is: Can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState? If yes, Zero becomes a genuine computational primitive of Knowledg
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25D's decisive test: can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState, making Zero a genuine computational primitive rather than an AI metaphor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A conventional system might define Delta=Target-Current. That is insufficient for KnowledgeOS. ... Nexus version known/3.69 known, Rollback verified/unknown, Firewall permitted/conflicting, Architecture approval/missing. There are four fundamentally different situations. Therefore Zero != simple sub
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the naive Delta=Target-Current model of Zero using a four-requirement worked example (known/unknown/conflicting/missing), establishing Zero≠simple subtraction — it must compare requirements against epistemic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Let the goal be G. The goal induces a set of required knowledge conditions: R_G={r_1,r_2,...,r_n}. For Nexus migration ... r_1=CurrentVersionKnown ... r_7=GovernanceApprovalObtained. This is crucial: Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone. We need the Epistemic Contract that tells us what must
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge Requirement set R_G induced by a goal G (worked with seven Nexus-migration requirements r1-r7), establishing that Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone and requires an Epistemic Contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define EC_G=(R_G,Gamma_G) where R_G = required conditions; Gamma_G = rules determining sufficiency. So EC_G = what must be established + how sufficiency is judged. This gives Zero a formal input.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Epistemic Contract EC_G=(R_G,Γ_G) — required conditions plus sufficiency rules — as Zero's formal input.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For each requirement r_i, we evaluate its status against K_t. Define Sat(K_t,r_i). Initially I propose the following state set: S={Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable}. This is already much richer than Boolean logic.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a nine-value requirement-satisfaction status set (Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable), explicitly richer than Boolean logic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Sat(K,r)=False. That could mean: we know it is false; we don't know; evidence conflicts; evidence is stale; evidence was invalidated; governance prohibits the action. These are operationally very different. Therefore Sat != Boolean.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues Sat≠Boolean: a bare False collapses six operationally distinct situations (known-false, unknown, conflicting, stale, invalidated, prohibited) into one indistinguishable value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We can define Z_i=Status(K_t,r_i,EC_G). Then Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i) | r_i in R_G}. This gives us a Zero vector. For example Z(K)=[Satisfied,Satisfied,Unknown,Insufficient,Conflicted,Satisfied,Missing]. Now Zero is computationally representable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i)} as a computationally representable 'Zero vector' of per-requirement statuses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Case A: No evidence exists: Evidence(r)=empty. Status: Unknown. Case B: Governance requires approval, and no approval exists. That is Missing. These are different. So I recommend Missing as a separate status where the requirement itself is an expected governed artifact/action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (no evidence exists at all) from Missing (an expected governed artifact/action, such as an approval, that does not exist) as two different status values.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose current KnowledgeState contains A_1: NexusVersion=3.69, A_2: RepositoryCount=43, but nothing about rollback. Then Status(r_1)=Satisfied but Status(r_3)=Unknown. If Architecture Board approval is explicitly required and has not been issued: Status(r_7)=Missing. Therefore Zero(K)={r_3:Unknown,
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked Nexus example computing a concrete Zero(K)={r3:Unknown, r7:Missing} from partial knowledge state evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We can therefore define Zero(K,G,EC)=R_G \ Satisfied(K,R_G) but this is only a shorthand. The real result must retain why each requirement is not satisfied. So Zero={Requirement, Status, Evidence, Reason, Dependencies}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a shorthand set-difference definition of Zero (R_G minus satisfied requirements) into the fuller structured form Zero={Requirement,Status,Evidence,Reason,Dependencies}, retaining why each requirement is unsatisfied.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero item should look conceptually like: Requirement: RollbackVerified; Status: Unknown; SupportingEvidence: none; BlockingReason: no successful restore test; RequiredAction: perform restore test; DecisionCriticality: high. This is already implementable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a concrete implementable structured-Zero-item template with six fields (Requirement, Status, SupportingEvidence, BlockingReason, RequiredAction, DecisionCriticality).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 supports RollbackVerified=True. Is that enough? Not necessarily. The epistemic contract may require 2 independent tests. Or 1 test witnessed by a designated authority. Or Probability(success)>=0.99. Therefore Satisfied = ContractSpecific.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that satisfaction of a requirement is ContractSpecific — the same supporting evidence may or may not count as satisfied depending on the epistemic contract's own sufficiency rule (independent-test count, witness authority, or probability threshold).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need Satisfied(K,r,EC) which may invoke the appropriate reasoning model. For example Satisfied(K,r,EC)=RuleEngine(K,r,EC) or =StatisticalCriterion(K,r,EC) or =HumanAuthorization(K,r). This is another reason Zero must not contain one universal inference mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the satisfaction predicate Satisfied(K,r,EC) as potentially delegating to RuleEngine, StatisticalCriterion, or HumanAuthorization — reinforcing that Zero must not embed one universal inference mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should not calculate everything itself. Instead: Zero -> RequirementEvaluation -> AppropriateReasoningModel. ... Zero aggregates the results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Zero as an orchestrator that dispatches requirement evaluation to the appropriate reasoning model (Rules/Statistics/Authority) and aggregates results, rather than being an inference engine itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Operational Zero: Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) where W* is the target world state. Epistemic Zero: Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC) where K*_EC is the knowledge required by the epistemic contract. These are fundamentally different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally splits Operational Zero Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) from Epistemic Zero Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC), reaffirming the two are fundamentally different quantities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Target: Nexus Pro running in target environment. Current world: Nexus OSS 3.69 running. Operational gap: Z_W>0. But suppose Target architecture known, Current version known, Backup status unknown, Firewall status unknown, Approval missing. Then Z_K>0. Even if an engineer knows exactly how to perform
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing Z_K (epistemic gap) can independently block execution even when the operational how-to is fully known, illustrating Z_W and Z_K as genuinely separate blocking gaps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend Zero=(Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision) at the conceptual level. Z_world: What differs in reality? Z_knowledge: What required facts are unknown/uncertain? Z_governance: What required approvals/rules are missing? Z_decision: What prevents a defensible decision? This is much
a_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes Zero into four conceptual dimensions (Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision), each answering a distinct question, stronger than a single scalar distance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Z_knowledge=5 and Z_governance=1. Can we say Zero=6? No. The six missing items are not necessarily comparable. One missing governance approval could be more blocking than five low-priority informational gaps. Therefore Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample against summing dimension counts into a scalar Zero=6: a single governance gap can outweigh five informational gaps in blocking severity, so Zero must remain primarily a structured object, not a scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Once the structured Zero exists, we may calculate: GapCount. Or CriticalGapCount. Or WeightedGapScore. Or ContractCoverage. For example Coverage(K) = satisfied required conditions / total required conditions. But these are projections of Zero, not Zero itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four derivable scalar projections of the structured Zero object (GapCount, CriticalGapCount, WeightedGapScore, ContractCoverage), explicitly distinguished as projections, not Zero itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Each requirement can have Criticality(r) such as {Critical,High,Medium,Low}. But again, we should be careful with arbitrary scores. A critical requirement might be RollbackVerified. If Status=Unknown, then migration could be blocked regardless of all other results. This gives us BlockingCondition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces per-requirement Criticality with a caution against arbitrary scoring, deriving the concept of a BlockingCondition — a single unresolved critical requirement that blocks regardless of all other results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameText\neq SameMeaning ... one of the most important principles for KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: States SameText ≠ SameMeaning, worked with an identical 'Approved' string across two contexts with differing meaning — 'one of the most important principles for KnowledgeOS.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Syntax: What was written? Identity: What entity does it refer to? Semantics: What does the statement mean? ... Syntax\neq Identity\neq Semantics
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines three distinct layers (Syntax, Identity, Semantics) — Syntax ≠ Identity ≠ Semantics, worked with an 'Approved Nexus' example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameMeaning(P_A,P_B\mid C_A,C_B) ... \{Equivalent,Compatible,Related,Different,Unknown\} ... Unknown must be a first-class result
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines SameMeaning(PA,PB|CA,CB) with a five-value result set, requiring Unknown to be a first-class result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Meaning belongs to a BoundedContext ... Architecture Context Approved = board accepted ... Change Management ... Security ... These are related concepts. They are not necessarily identical
b_rows_sample.statement: States 'Meaning belongs to a BoundedContext,' worked with three differing 'Approved' definitions across Architecture/Change Management/Security contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Approved=true and reuse it everywhere. That is dangerous ... Approved_{Architecture}, Approved_{Change}, Approved_{Security} remain distinct concepts. They may be mapped explicitly
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a naive universal 'Approved=true' ontology entry, requiring distinct per-context concepts with explicit mappings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded context defines Vocabulary+Meaning+Rules+Invariants ... Meaning(term,C) is context-dependent ... Meaning(Approval,C_1)\neq Meaning(Approval,C_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines a bounded context's semantic content as Vocabulary+Meaning+Rules+Invariants, giving context-dependent Meaning(term,C).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Term\rightarrow Concept ... ArchitectureDecision, ArchitectureReview, ArchitectureApproval, ArchitectureException ... the language must correspond to DomainModel
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires Ubiquitous Language (Term->Concept) to correspond to the DomainModel, not merely serve as a dictionary, worked with four Architecture BC terms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology as Concepts+Relations+Constraints+Semantics ... Ontology\neq DomainModel
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Ontology as Concepts+Relations+Constraints+Semantics, distinct from the DomainModel (Behavior+Invariants+BusinessRules) — Ontology ≠ DomainModel, both supported without one replacing the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticRelation\in\{Equivalent,Subsumes,Specializes,Overlaps,Related,MapsTo,Incompatible,Unknown\} ... much richer semantic interoperability
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value SemanticRelation taxonomy, giving much richer semantic interoperability than a bare same/different check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_A\equiv Client_B only if the domain mapping explicitly establishes it ... We should not assume this merely because humans often use the words similarly
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires Equivalent relations to be explicitly established by domain mapping, never assumed from casual similar word usage (Customer/Client example).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ProductionSystem\subset System ... ProductionSystem\sqsubseteq System ... matters for inheritance of knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines subsumption ProductionSystem ⊑ System, mattering for knowledge inheritance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Repository\rightarrow requiresBackup ... Nexus repository may inherit requiresBackup ... Repository\rightarrow supportsFeatureX does not necessarily imply every specialized repository supports X ... Subsumption does not imply unrestricted property inheritance
b_rows_sample.statement: States a specialized concept may inherit some but not all parent properties, giving the explicit invariant that subsumption does not imply unrestricted property inheritance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_A\cap C_B\neq\emptyset without C_A=C_B ... Architecture Change / Software Change ... semantic mapping can be Overlap
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines partial overlap between two concepts as a distinct semantic relation, worked with an Architecture-Change/Software-Change example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: technically reviewed versus legally authorized [Approved] ... Treating them as equivalent could cause serious governance failure ... SemanticIncompatibility must be representable explicitly
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked incompatible-meaning example under a shared term ('Approved' meaning technically-reviewed vs legally-authorized), warning conflation risks serious governance failure — SemanticIncompatibility must be explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContextA\leftrightarrow ContextB ... ArchitectureApproval_A\rightarrow ArchitectureGatePassed_B. But this mapping should be explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires DDD-style explicit context mapping between concepts across bounded contexts, worked with an ArchitectureApproval->ArchitectureGatePassed example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Translate(C_A)=C_B does not necessarily mean C_A\equiv C_B ... transformation; aggregation; decomposition; enrichment; loss of information ... Translation\neq Equivalence
b_rows_sample.statement: States Translation ≠ Equivalence: a translation mapping does not imply equivalence, since translation may involve transformation, aggregation, decomposition, enrichment, or information loss.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Legacy System->Anti-Corruption Layer->KnowledgeOS Domain Model ... precisely what KnowledgeOS needs when integrating Jira; GitLab; CMDB; architecture repositories; monitoring systems; documents; external APIs
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the DDD Anti-Corruption Layer pattern to protect KnowledgeOS from directly importing foreign semantics when integrating Jira, GitLab, CMDB, architecture repositories, monitoring systems, documents, and external APIs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: status=Done ... Done=Approved. That may be completely wrong ... ExternalStatus\neq DomainState unless an explicit mapping establishes it
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked danger example: naively mapping Jira's status=Done to domain 'Approved' can be completely wrong — ExternalStatus ≠ DomainState absent explicit mapping.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticMapping=(SourceContext,SourceConcept,TargetContext,TargetConcept,Transformation,Conditions,Loss,Validity) ... extremely valuable
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-field SemanticMapping contract, worked with a Jira/Status=Done -> ChangeManagement/ImplementationCompleted example explicitly noting non-equivalence to ArchitectureApproved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_A contains five pieces of information but C_B contains only three ... InformationLoss ... otherwise the receiving system may assume equivalence when there is only partial correspondence
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicit InformationLoss representation when a translation target holds less information than its source.

a_rows_sample.statement: H-K06 (Action ≠ Result): `o ≠ δ(K,o)` and `δ(K,o₁)=δ(K,o₂) ⇏ o₁=o₂` are required properties: an action/operation is not identical to its transformation result, and two different actions can produce the same state transformation

a_rows_sample.anchor: `δ(K,o₁) =_semantic δ(K,o₂) ⇏ o₁ = o₂`. **The equality must be named or the property is vacuous**
a_rows_sample.statement: H-K06 (Action ≠ Result) formal consequence: δ(K,o1) semantically equal to δ(K,o2) does not imply o1=o2, but the equality relation used must be explicitly named or the property is vacuous. DDD: operations are commands, results are domain events, state is neither — Command ≠ Transformation, already boxed at an earlier step (§256.21). Architecture: an operation registry must key on operation identity, not resulting state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⚠️ **WITHDRAWN 2026-08-31:** I previously wrote that this *strengthens* the case for typing `humanActRef`. **It does not**
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-retraction: an earlier claim that H-K06's Command≠Transformation consequence strengthens the case for typing the humanActRef field is withdrawn — that is judged a different identity layer (referred to as E6), and the humanActRef question stands on its own implementation evidence, independent of this Gita research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Trivially required and not interesting on its own:** `o` is an element of an operation set, `δ(K,o)` an element of `𝕂`. **Different types.** ... The corpus already enforces it `CORPUS`: `Command ≠ Transformation` (§256.21–22, boxed).
a_rows_sample.statement: Property 1 (o ≠ δ(K,o)) is trivially required by typing alone — o is an element of the operation set, δ(K,o) an element of the state space K — and is already independently enforced by the corpus as Command ≠ Transformation (§256.21-22, boxed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: o1 = (Assert, a2, origin:scan, actor:tool) / o2 = (Assert, a2, origin:vendor, actor:human) / delta(K0,o1) = ['a1','a2'] delta(K0,o2) = ['a1','a2'] / states equal? True operations equal? False
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes exec/t285_reconcile.py T-E with two concrete operations o1 (Assert a2, origin:scan, actor:tool) and o2 (Assert a2, origin:vendor, actor:human) starting from state K0=['a1']: both produce resulting state ['a1','a2'] (states equal) while the operations themselves differ (operations equal=False). Confirmed and required: collapsing the two operations would make 'who asserted this, on whose authority' unrecoverable from the state — an outcome the estate has already suffered once (two authority acts sharing one grantId, a silent loss of an authority act, per implementation evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Under the verification lane's own identity rule `id = H(P, e, c, t, Π)`, **`Π` is inside the hash.** So `o₁` and `o₂` produce assertions with *different ids*, hence **structurally different states**, and the antecedent `δ(K,o₁) = δ(K,o₂)` is **false** — the property never fires. **It fires only under semantic equality**
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows the property is equality-relative: under structural equality (id=H(P,e,c,t,Π), which includes provenance Π) o1 and o2 produce different ids, so the antecedent is false and the property never fires — vacuously true and useless under structural equality, required and load-bearing under semantic equality, and required under observational equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Typed result:** `δ(K,o₁) =_semantic δ(K,o₂) ⇏ o₁ = o₂`. **Stating the property without naming the equality makes it vacuous.** ... the Gītā framing — *"do not define the action by its fruit"* — does not by itself supply the qualification. **Philosophy asked the question; the equality typing answered it.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final typed result: delta(K,o1)=semantic delta(K,o2) does not imply o1=o2, and stating it without naming the equality relation makes it vacuous; the Gita's framing ('do not define the action by its fruit') does not by itself supply this qualification — philosophy asked the question, the equality typing methodology answered it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Verdict: the Gītā CORROBORATES a property KnowledgeOS derives on its own.** Per Step 286's own methodology that is *"a stronger scientific result than claiming KnowledgeOS was derived from the Gītā."* **Classified `R5` on the mathematics, `R2` on the philosophical contribution.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs the independence test: the property (Action≠Result) is reached both via the Gita (2.47-2.48, duty distinguished from its fruits) and independently by KnowledgeOS (Command≠Transformation derived from typing alone, plus the grantId collision as an implementation failure demanding it); concludes the Gita corroborates a property KnowledgeOS derives on its own — judged, per the project's own methodology, a stronger scientific result than claiming KnowledgeOS was derived from the Gita. Classified R5 on the mathematics, R2 on the philosophical contribution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Mapping:** ``` Karma ≠ Karma-phala → o ≠ K' ``` ... This is the source of our **Action ≠ Result hypothesis**
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Karma≠Karma-phala (action is not its fruit) as the textual source of the KnowledgeOS Action≠Result hypothesis, mapping Karma to operation o and Karma-phala to resulting state K'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **`I-C` is the most dependency-loaded:** it is substantive under `≡`-with-`Π`-excluded and **vacuous** under `≅_λ`. **Decision 3 does not merely refine it — it decides whether it says anything.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies I-C (Command≠Transformation) as the most dependency-loaded candidate in the register: it is substantive under semantic equality with provenance excluded, but becomes VACUOUS under provenance-sensitive equality -- meaning Step 254 Decision 3 does not merely refine I-C, it decides whether I-C says anything at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Command != Transformation != Result, which we already independently derived ... Karma = operation is useful only as a conceptual correspondence ... K_t --O--> K_{t+1} while Phala = consequence is separate ... operation and outcome must not be conflated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reiterates Command != Transformation != Result (said to already be independently derived): Karma=operation is useful only as a conceptual correspondence, formalized as K_t --O--> K_{t+1} while Phala=consequence remains separate, preserving 'operation and outcome must not be conflated' as architecturally valuable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The previous proposal: Non-Attachment → EC=FALSE is rejected. Why? Because EC is an empirical closure classification, whereas attachment in the Gītā concerns the relation to the fruits/results of action. They are categorically different. A more defensible hypothesis is: Action validity ≢ Result desirability ... Operation validity ≢ Outcome success.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the specific mapping 'Non-Attachment implies EC=FALSE is acceptable' on the grounds of a category error (EC is an empirical-closure classification; Gita attachment concerns the actor's relation to result), replacing it with the defensible, weaker hypothesis that action/operation validity is not equivalent to result desirability/outcome success — noting a failed outcome does not retrospectively invalidate a valid operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The strongest principle emerging from this research is not EC=FALSE. It is: Result Status ≠ Action Validity ... Guidance ≠ Decision ... Decision ≠ Execution ... Execution ≠ State Transition. These distinctions are mathematically, architecturally and philosophically coherent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the four-part Result-Status≠Action-Validity / Guidance≠Decision / Decision≠Execution / Execution≠State-Transition chain as the single strongest principle to emerge from this research pass, explicitly displacing the earlier (rejected) EC=FALSE claim as the headline finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vairāgya / non-attachment → outcome independence ... Can the validity of an operation be separated from whether the desired outcome occurred? Potentially: Valid(o,K) ⇏ Desired(K'). This must remain a research hypothesis.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the operation-validity-independent-of-outcome-desirability hypothesis found elsewhere in the batch (S2058) in the specific symbolic form Valid(o,K) does not imply Desired(K'), again explicitly hedged as a research hypothesis rather than an established result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-K11 non-attachment: 'A valid action/process may retain epistemic or normative validity even when its intended outcome is not achieved.' Then test Valid(o,K) against Outcome(o)=success and Outcome(o)=failure. ... H-K04 equanimity: Epistemic impartiality is not epistemic equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Narrows the non-attachment hypothesis to a precise, testable claim (validity independent of outcome achievement, tested against both success and failure cases) and separately proposes 'epistemic impartiality is not epistemic equality' as a candidate principle distinguishing actor-blind evaluation from treating all evidence identically -- both explicitly marked as unproven until independently demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.statement: Records E-03 and E-04 as the specific textual loci (verses 2.47 and 2.48) underlying, respectively, the action/result-separability hypothesis and the outcome-valence-versus-validity distinction used throughout this batch's Step 285 documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The material world is an inverted tree. Its roots are above (the Supreme Source), and its branches extend below
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the Gita's inverted-Ashvattha-tree image onto a KnowledgeOS component hierarchy: roots-above = Knowledge Atma (source), branches = Assertions, leaves = Propositions, twigs = Evidence, roots-below = Karma/History, and 'the axe of detachment' = non-attachment (EC=FALSE acceptable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Purushottama > Akshara > Kshar … Purushottama = source of all knowledge … Akshara = established knowledge (EC=TRUE) … Kshar = provisional knowledge (EC=FALSE)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-level ontology mapping the Gita's Purushottama/Akshara/Kshar hierarchy directly onto Knowledge-Atma/established-knowledge/provisional-knowledge, offered as completing 'the complete Gita-KnowledgeOS framework.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across successive knowledge states, while its knowledge, understanding, observations, and forms may change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Ātma A_K as the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across a sequence of knowledge states K_0,K_1,...,K_t, satisfying A_K(t1)=A_K(t2) while K_t1≠K_t2 in general — 'the Ātma remains invariant while the knowledge state evolves'. Explicitly NOT defined as 'all knowledge' or as the Ideal State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Knowledge Ātma}\neq K_t\neq I_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three distinct concepts that must not collapse: Knowledge Ātma (who/what persists through knowledge-state changes), Knowledge State K_t (what is currently known/represented), Ideal State I_t (what should be known/understood/achieved for the current purpose) — Knowledge Ātma ≠ K_t ≠ I_t, called 'a very strong architectural separation'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq\mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a potentially unbounded Knowledge Space 𝒦 of which the current Knowledge State is only a finite/partial representation, K_t⊆𝒦; Knowledge Ātma is not 𝒦 itself but the persistent identity undertaking an 'epistemic journey' A_K --epistemic journey--> K_t⊆𝒦 across K_0->K_1->K_2->... indefinitely. Layered architecture diagram: Ātma=persistence/identity, Knowledge State=current manifestation, Zero=reveals the boundary of what is currently known, Lord=expands the possible knowledge horizon, Sārathi=navigates the transition, Knower=experiences/evaluates/decides.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural and mathematical abstraction inspired by the philosophical concept of Ātman. It is not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman described in the Bhagavad Gītā.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit disclaimer required before using the term in formal theory: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural/mathematical abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman — protecting the model from a category error. Notes that introducing Knowledge Ātma changes the ontology of the complete KnowledgeOS model, requiring formal distinction of identity, state, knowledge, understanding, ideal, and evolution, and recommends exploring this before Question 20.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is the persistent Knower whose identity remains invariant while its knowledge, understanding, observations, experiences, and represented states change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles 'Ātma = invariant identity underlying changing states' with 'Ātma = the Knower' into one definition: Ātma = the persistent Knower, invariant (A_t1=A_t2) while its knowledge state K_t changes (K_t1≠K_t2). 'Knower' names its role, 'invariant/persistent' names its mathematical property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \underbrace{\text{Ātma}}_{\text{Who knows}} \quad \underbrace{K_t}_{\text{What is known}} \quad \underbrace{I_t}_{\text{What should be known}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a clean three-way separation Ātma ('who knows') / K_t ('what is known') / I_t ('what should be known'), judged much cleaner than identifying Ātma with the Knowledge State itself; repeats the caution that this is a KnowledgeOS mathematical/architectural abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a claim of having mathematically captured the metaphysical Ātman of the Gītā.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that KnowledgeOS Ātma is literally a second Ātman
b_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating KnowledgeOS Ātma as literally a second metaphysical Ātman — that would move from architectural analogy to metaphysical claim. Defines 𝒜_H := Human Knower abstraction and 𝒜_K := KnowledgeOS persistent system identity; the shared word 'Ātma' expresses the analogy of persistence/invariant identity, not metaphysical identity between the two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A_H \neq \mathcal A_K \neq K_t \subseteq \mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the four-way separation Knower Ātma ≠ Knowledge Ātma, Knowledge Ātma ≠ Knowledge State, Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Space, giving 𝒜_H ≠ 𝒜_K ≠ K_t ⊆ 𝒦. Models the Arjuna-Sārathi interaction as 𝒜_H --Intent--> 𝒜_K --Investigation--> K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> next inquiry, worked through 'show me whom I have to fight' discovering new dimensions {Kinship, Teacher, Elder,...} via parsing/semantic reconstruction rather than the Knower pre-specifying them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the architecture as Human Knower <-> KnowledgeOS Ātma <-> Knowledge Space, with Zero/Lord/Sārathi operating between the current state and the expanding knowledge horizon, and proposes that the next formal question should be 'what is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?' rather than continuing with an isolated mathematical object — called 'a significant conceptual milestone'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \widehat K_t = \text{best available reconstruction from }O_{\le t}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'we try our best but never reach the best' as K̂_t = best available reconstruction from O_≤t, with K̂_t ≠ K_t possibly persisting even as observations accumulate (O_≤t1 ⊆ O_≤t2 may give a better but still imperfect K̂_t2). Draws a careful analogy to least-squares/Gaussian estimation (x̂=argmin_x‖Ax-b‖²): 'best approximation under a criterion' does not guarantee x̂=x_true, giving 'Best reconstruction under regime R ≠ complete underlying Knowledge'. Places measure/probability theory specifically at the Observations->probabilistic reconstruction step (P(K_t|F_t), E[X_t|F_t]), with K_t itself 'conceptually prior' to the probabilistic extraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātman should not be modeled as an "Ideal State" itself. It is better modeled as the invariant identity underlying changing states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed equation of Ātman with the Ideal State, offering instead 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' ℐ with ℐ_{t+1}=ℐ_t while K_{t+1}≠K_t and I_{t+1}≠I_t in general, giving Identity ≠ Current State ≠ Ideal State — 'a very important refinement'. K_t = State(ℐ,t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_0 \subseteq? K_1 \subseteq? K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution K_0->K_1->K_2->... within K_t⊆𝒦 is NOT necessarily monotonic — an assertion can be accepted, then questioned, then rejected, so K_{t+1} may contain less information than K_t in one sense while being epistemically better, reinforcing the earlier distinction between knowledge quantity and knowledge quality/coherence. Also cautions against assuming lim_{t->∞} K_t = 𝒦 as a mathematical fact rather than an assumption.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Ātman doctrine} \rightarrow \text{philosophical inspiration} \rightarrow \text{Invariant Identity abstraction}
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit philosophy/mathematics firewall: 'The Gītā teaches that Ātman is not destroyed' does NOT mathematically imply 'our model proves an invariant identity exists' — Ātman doctrine -> philosophical inspiration -> Invariant Identity abstraction, never Ātman doctrine ⇒ mathematical theorem. Recommends adding 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' as a new theoretical concept (not folding Ātman into Ideal State), with a suggested documentation sentence: 'The concept of Ātman provides a philosophical analogue for the architectural concept of persistent identity... KnowledgeOS may use this as a conceptual inspiration, but does not claim to computationally model Ātman or establish its metaphysical truth.'

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-inverted-tree-purushottama-akshara-kshar' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledge-atma-identity-concept' (batch B0049). Note: Gita chapter 15 (Purushottama Yoga) read as providing 'the complete theory of knowledge identity' and directly answering 'what exactly makes two knowledge objects the same knowledge': a three-level ontology (Purushottama/Supreme = K_atma, Akshara/Imperishable = established knowledge EC=TRUE, Kshar/Perishable = provisional knowledge EC=FALSE) via the inverted-tree image (roots above = source, branches below = assertions/propositions/evidence/karma-history), with boxed 'identity criterion' K_atma(A1)=K_atma(A2) iff Source(A1)=Source(A2) and Identity(A1)=Identity(A2), and a 'persistence criterion' K_atma(K_t)=K_atma(T(K_t)) for all T. Proposed as directly touching the existing knowledge-atma-identity-concept object with a specific (unratified, scripture-derived) identity criterion the earlier object left open.
