a_rows_sample.anchor: In Chapter 4, Krishna tells Arjuna that both have had many births, but Krishna remembers them while Arjuna does not. ... It introduces a distinction between: Continuity and: Accessible memory. Those are not the same thing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses Krishna's remembered-vs-Arjuna's-unremembered past births as an example motivating a distinction between Continuity (that a lineage of states exists) and Accessible memory (what a given state can currently retrieve of that lineage) -- these are argued to not be the same thing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Layer 1 -- Current state: S_t. Layer 2 -- Historical lineage: H={S_0,S_1,...,S_t}. Layer 3 -- Authorized historical knowledge: K(H). These are different. Therefore: State != History != Accessible Memory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a three-layer memory model: Layer 1 current state S_t; Layer 2 historical lineage H = {S_0,...,S_t} (what actually happened); Layer 3 authorized/accessible historical knowledge K(H) (what some actor/system is permitted or capable of knowing about H). States the invariant State != History != Accessible Memory, i.e. 'History exists' does not imply 'Current agent knows history'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agent_{t+1} != Agent_t in terms of accessible memory. But KnowledgeOS can preserve: History(Agent) outside the ephemeral agent state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the three-layer memory model to an AI agent session example: a later session's agent (Agent t+1) need not remember an earlier session's agent (Agent t) state, but KnowledgeOS can preserve History(Agent) outside the ephemeral per-session agent memory, so the agent does not have to carry its entire history itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory. This strongly validates the architecture decision we previously made that: .claude/ and .codex/ should not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory. The agent harness may contain operational memory. KnowledgeOS contains governed historical knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the principle Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory and explicitly claims this validates a prior architecture decision that agent-harness directories (.claude/, .codex/) must not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory -- the agent harness holds operational memory, while KnowledgeOS holds governed historical knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We need to distinguish: Actor identity, State, Memory, Role, Authority, Experience, Knowledge. ... ActorIdentity = A ... State(A,t1) != State(A,t2). And: Memory(A,t2) may not contain: Memory(A,t1). Yet: History(A) can still exist.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues identity should not be shallowly answered with 'the user ID'; instead distinguishes seven separate notions -- Actor identity, State, Memory, Role, Authority, Experience, Knowledge -- and formalizes that a stable ActorIdentity A can have State(A,t1) != State(A,t2), Memory(A,t2) not necessarily containing Memory(A,t1), while History(A) still exists as a distinct object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D1 [with] actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp, provenance. Otherwise the determination becomes: 'Something the AI once said.' That is not governed knowledge. Instead it becomes: Historical epistemic artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that a determination D1 must retain its actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp and provenance even after the originating session disappears, because without this it degrades from governed knowledge into a mere unattributed 'historical epistemic artifact' ('something the AI once said'); this is offered as the reason provenance must be external to transient agent state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not model Krishna simply as "the administrator who has all memory." A better abstraction is: Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity. ... A trusted epistemic authority that can establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modeling Krishna as 'an administrator who has all memory' (an omniscient-database analogy) and instead re-characterizes his architectural role as Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity -- a trusted epistemic authority able to establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance asks: Where did this knowledge come from? Provenance(x). Lineage asks: What states/instances are connected through continuity? Lineage(x). They overlap but are not identical. So: Provenance != Lineage.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Provenance(x) (where knowledge came from) from Lineage(x) (what states/instances are connected through continuity): the two overlap but are argued to not be identical, proposed as an addition to the architecture vocabulary. A governed 'Historical Continuity' mechanism is proposed to maintain Lineage(x) even when Memory(x,t) is incomplete.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Principle IV-B -- Continuity exceeds accessible memory: Historical continuity must not depend on the current actor's accessible memory. Therefore: CurrentMemory subseteq HistoricalKnowledge may be true. But: CurrentMemory = HistoricalKnowledge must not be assumed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names and records 'Principle IV-B -- Continuity exceeds accessible memory': historical continuity must not depend on the current actor's accessible memory; CurrentMemory subseteq HistoricalKnowledge may hold, but CurrentMemory = HistoricalKnowledge must never be assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The actor must know the limits of its own knowledge. This is perhaps the most important principle for AI. An agent should be able to say: I know this. I do not know this. I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it. ... That is epistemically mature architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a third principle, considered possibly the most important for AI: 'the actor must know the limits of its own knowledge', illustrated by a required repertoire of self-report statements (I know this / I do not know this / I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it / the system has historical evidence for this / the evidence is insufficient for action / the action is prohibited / the action requires authority), termed 'epistemically mature architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> (SHOULD DO / SHOULD NOT DO) -> DECISION -> (ACT/DEFER/REFRAIN) -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, and above all of it: PROVENANCE + LINEAGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the KnowledgeOS pipeline diagram (previously Knowledge->Inquiry->Evidence->Determination->Decision->Action) into a richer chain: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> {SHOULD DO, SHOULD NOT DO} -> DECISION -> {ACT, DEFER, REFRAIN} -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, with PROVENANCE + LINEAGE positioned as an overarching background layer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would actually say Chapter 4 strengthens our architecture rather than forcing us to redesign it. Especially these existing decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly claims Chapter 4's material strengthens/validates (rather than forces redesign of) ten prior architecture decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3C. Missing concepts ... Look for concepts that the reasoning requires but which were never explicitly modeled. Examples discovered during later reasoning may include: wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, epistemic restraint. Do not automatically accept these. Evaluate them against the complete corpus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly names wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, and epistemic restraint as candidate 'missing concepts' example categories to evaluate for Phase 3C -- directly referencing (and thereby corroborating the significance of) the Chapter-4-derived wisdom-action-guidance-function and historical-continuity-vs-accessible-memory material found elsewhere in this same batch (S1067), while cautioning these candidates must not be automatically accepted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 8. DO NOT CONFUSE MEMORY WITH KNOWLEDGE ... Apply the same discipline to this synthesis project. The current Claude context is NOT the authoritative memory of the project. The corpus is the historical source. The synthesis artifacts become the structured working model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the same memory-vs-knowledge discipline the corpus develops about KnowledgeOS reflexively to the synthesis process itself: the synthesizing agent's own (Claude) context is explicitly declared NOT the authoritative memory of the project -- the brainstorming corpus is the historical source and the synthesis artifacts (files under docs/knowledgeos/reviews/synthesis/) become the structured working model. This mirrors the Ephemeral-Agent-Memory != Authoritative-Knowledge-Memory principle found in S1067.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā text ↓ Philosophical principle ↓ Abstract structural pattern ↓ KnowledgeOS question ↓ Mathematical / architectural test ↓ Possible hypothesis ... Never: Gītā character → KnowledgeOS object ... and never: philosophical idea → equation → architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: The Bhagavad Gita research track is classified as external research, not an architecture source. Correct method: Gita text -> philosophical principle -> abstract structural pattern -> KnowledgeOS question -> mathematical/architectural test -> possible hypothesis; forbidden shortcuts are 'Gita character -> KnowledgeOS object' and 'philosophical idea -> equation -> architecture'. Current research covers Chapters 1-4, with candidate hypotheses including Continuity != Memory != Observation and Knowledge != Wisdom != Action ('Wisdom is active discernment concerning what should be done and what should not be done'), explicitly framed as research hypotheses only. DeepSeek's Gita document is separately classified EXTERNAL RESEARCH / NON-AUTHORITATIVE / CONCEPTUAL LENSES / HYPOTHESES, and its unsupported quantitative equations are not accepted as KnowledgeOS derivations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source ≠ History ≠ AccessibleMemory. ... For an object x, we want Lineage(x)={x0,x1,…,xt}. But an actor at time t may have only Memory_t(x) ⊂ Lineage(x). KnowledgeOS should preserve enough information to reconstruct the relevant lineage independently of the actor's current memory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Gita-Chapter-4-derived principle Source != History != AccessibleMemory as three new audit questions (What is the authoritative source? What happened during transmission -- Lineage? What does the current actor actually remember -- AccessibleMemory?). Formalizes Lineage(x)={x_0,...,x_t} versus an actor's Memory_t(x) which is only a subset of Lineage(x) at time t, and states KnowledgeOS should preserve enough information to reconstruct relevant lineage independently of an actor's current memory -- termed a major architecture capability (historical continuity audit).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We must never confuse: Archive with: Lineage. An archive answers: 'Do we still have the old information?' Lineage answers: 'How did the current state arise from the previous state?' KnowledgeOS requires the second. ... TransactionTime from ValidTime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Archive ('do we still have the old information?') from Lineage ('how did the current state arise from the previous state?'), arguing KnowledgeOS requires the latter; historical continuity evidence (session logs, change logs, repository history, saved conversations) is judged PARTIAL because these are not yet a unified historical model. Also distinguishes TransactionTime from ValidTime as an explicit audit requirement, since createdAt/updatedAt fields are not automatically sufficient to reconstruct semantic validity at a point in time (State(x,t)).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_t be the total relevant historical lineage at time t. ... M_t be what an agent currently remembers. Then generally: M_t ⊆ H_t. A new agent/session may have M_{t+1}∩M_t that is much smaller than the complete historical lineage. Yet the system can preserve H_t. ... Continuity must belong to the governed system, not depend solely on the memory of the current actor.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Chapter-4 continuity insight: H_t = total relevant historical lineage at time t, M_t = what an agent currently remembers, with M_t subseteq H_t generally holding; a new agent/session's overlap with the prior agent's memory (M_{t+1} intersect M_t) may be much smaller than the full lineage H_t, yet the system can still preserve H_t independently. Yields the principle 'continuity must belong to the governed system, not depend solely on the memory of the current actor' -- described as highly relevant to AI engineering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system preserves the lineage necessary to reconstruct relevant prior states. ... GlobalHistoricalContext may be available to the system of record while LocalActorContext is intentionally incomplete. Therefore: SystemContext ⊇ ActorContext can be a design principle. ... Projection(H,C) → Context_C. The agent receives a context projection appropriate to its task. ... Context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state. Otherwise the actor may incorrectly assume: 'What I was given is everything that exists.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the Gita continuity insight architecturally: not 'the system remembers everything' but 'the system preserves the lineage necessary to reconstruct relevant prior states'; models GlobalHistoricalContext (system of record) vs intentionally incomplete LocalActorContext under the design principle SystemContext ⊇ ActorContext, formalized as a context-projection function Projection(H,C) -> Context_C giving an agent only a task-relevant slice of history. Adds a new invariant: context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state, else the actor may wrongly assume it was given everything that exists. Argues a complete-memory-for-every-agent design would be expensive, hard to govern, potentially unsafe, and hard to invalidate/reason about, so Agent -> RelevantContext is preferred over Agent -> Everything.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(t) ⊉ History(0..t) in general. ... K.current is not equivalent to: KnowledgeHistory. ... AgentMemory ≠ SystemHistory. The system's authoritative lineage must live outside ephemeral agent context. ... Memory ≠ Knowledge ≠ Evidence ≠ History.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the general formal principle State(t) does not superset History(0..t): the current aggregate state (e.g. K.v7) need not contain its full reasoning history (K.v1->...->K.v7), so K.current != KnowledgeHistory; an agent's session sees only CurrentState, not PreviousReasoning, so AgentMemory != SystemHistory and the authoritative lineage must live outside ephemeral agent context -- reinforcing the chained non-identity Memory != Knowledge != Evidence != History.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should therefore never model governance simply as: allowed = true/false. We need at least the semantic distinction: Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown and potentially: Recommended, Discouraged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a deontic-modal governance vocabulary (Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown, and potentially Recommended/Discouraged) as necessary to replace a naive boolean allowed=true/false governance model, since 'positive permission' Permitted(a), 'obligation' Required(a), and 'prohibition' Forbidden(a) are argued to be distinct semantic categories, closer to a policy/dharma model than an IF-condition-THEN-execute command system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Wisdom is not merely storing knowledge. It is continuously asking: What should I do? but equally: What should I refrain from doing? This gives us a second dimension to KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Wisdom is a second architectural dimension distinct from Knowledge->Determination->Decision->Action: Chapter 4 suggests Knowledge->Wisdom->Action Guidance, where Wisdom evaluates both action and non-action (DO/ACT vs DO NOT ACT) before the Decision/Action stage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A workflow should not assume: Decision => Action. Instead: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}. ... Insufficient Evidence => Do Not Determine and perhaps => SeekMoreEvidence. That is epistemic restraint.
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Do nothing' (and deferral/escalation/seeking more evidence) must be first-class Decision outcomes rather than an implicit fallback: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}; when evidence is insufficient a KnowledgeOS-governed agent should conclude 'Do Not Determine' / 'SeekMoreEvidence' rather than force an answer -- termed 'epistemic restraint'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have already established that: Evidence not=> Truth. Now Chapter 4 gives us another principle: Knowledge not=> Action. There must be an intermediate judgment: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.
b_rows_sample.statement: By analogy to the already-established 'Evidence does not imply Truth' principle, Chapter 4 is read as supplying a parallel principle 'Knowledge does not imply Action', requiring an intermediate Judgment stage: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint: A governed system must be capable of determining both what should be done and what should not be done. Therefore: Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and records 'Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint': a governed system must be able to determine both what should be done and what should not be done, formalized as Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The actor must know the limits of its own knowledge. This is perhaps the most important principle for AI. An agent should be able to say: I know this. I do not know this. I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it. ... That is epistemically mature architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a third principle, considered possibly the most important for AI: 'the actor must know the limits of its own knowledge', illustrated by a required repertoire of self-report statements (I know this / I do not know this / I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it / the system has historical evidence for this / the evidence is insufficient for action / the action is prohibited / the action requires authority), termed 'epistemically mature architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> (SHOULD DO / SHOULD NOT DO) -> DECISION -> (ACT/DEFER/REFRAIN) -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, and above all of it: PROVENANCE + LINEAGE
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the KnowledgeOS pipeline diagram (previously Knowledge->Inquiry->Evidence->Determination->Decision->Action) into a richer chain: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> {SHOULD DO, SHOULD NOT DO} -> DECISION -> {ACT, DEFER, REFRAIN} -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, with PROVENANCE + LINEAGE positioned as an overarching background layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would actually say Chapter 4 strengthens our architecture rather than forcing us to redesign it. Especially these existing decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly claims Chapter 4's material strengthens/validates (rather than forces redesign of) ten prior architecture decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should investigate whether Wisdom is a cross-cutting domain function: Wisdom: (Knowledge, Context, Evidence, Rules, Authority) -> (ActionGuidance) where ActionGuidance in {DO, DON'T, WAIT, ASK, ESCALATE, INVESTIGATE}. I don't necessarily mean creating a class called Wisdom. That would be premature.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the open question of whether Wisdom should be modeled as a cross-cutting domain function Wisdom: (Knowledge, Context, Evidence, Rules, Authority) -> ActionGuidance with ActionGuidance in {DO, DON'T, WAIT, ASK, ESCALATE, INVESTIGATE}, while explicitly warning against prematurely reifying it as a literal `Wisdom` class; frames this as the key question to examine before 'Step 158', concluding Chapter 4 may reveal a missing architectural layer: a governed mechanism converting knowledge into action or restraint, not another knowledge repository.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3C. Missing concepts ... Look for concepts that the reasoning requires but which were never explicitly modeled. Examples discovered during later reasoning may include: wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, epistemic restraint. Do not automatically accept these. Evaluate them against the complete corpus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly names wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, and epistemic restraint as candidate 'missing concepts' example categories to evaluate for Phase 3C -- directly referencing (and thereby corroborating the significance of) the Chapter-4-derived wisdom-action-guidance-function and historical-continuity-vs-accessible-memory material found elsewhere in this same batch (S1067), while cautioning these candidates must not be automatically accepted.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega = \text{epistemic horizon} ... Not: \Omega=\text{God} ... and not: \Omega=\mathcal K
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Omega = epistemic horizon, representing the horizon against which the finite knowledge state is situated -- explicitly refusing the identities Omega=God and Omega=K (Knowledge Space), calling both unjustified architectural identities. Gives K_t != K even if |K|=infinity, protecting the theory from defining Moksha merely as 'infinite knowledge'. Extends the Chapter-13 Kshetra!=Kshetrajna separation with a four-way conceptual separation N != K_t != K != Omega (Knower, current state, whole knowledge space, horizon), explicitly conditioned on subsequent research confirming these distinctions are genuinely useful and non-redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Perspective(K_t) \rightarrow Perspective(K_{t+1}) ... Knowledge growth \neq fact accumulation
a_rows_sample.statement: Beyond ordinary growth K_t subset K_{t+1}, Chapter 11 suggests Perspective(K_t) -> Perspective(K_{t+1}): the system may restructure its relationship to existing facts (e.g. discovering relationships among A, B, C previously poorly understood) rather than merely acquire more facts. Hence Knowledge growth != fact accumulation, and epistemic transformation != simple state enlargement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: epistemic limitation = f(K_t,G_t) ... epistemic expansion = f(K_t,\Omega)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a tension between two directions: Chapter 11's expansion (perspective toward the whole, epistemic expansion = f(K_t,Omega)) versus Chapter 14's conditioning (knowing conditioned by G_t, epistemic limitation = f(K_t,G_t)). Proposes the kernel continuously works between its current bounded state and an epistemic horizon that exceeds that state, closer to KnowledgeOS as a continuously active system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M\neq K_{\max} ... M\neq |\mathcal K|\rightarrow\infty ... M\sim\text{transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon}
a_rows_sample.statement: With Chapters 11-14 combined, refuses modeling Moksha as the final Knowledge State: M != K_max and M != |K|->infinity. Proposes instead M ~ transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon, combined with Chapter 14's transcendence of ordinary conditioning; the theoretical transition is not simply K_0->K_1->K_2->... but (N,K_t,rho_t,G_t,Omega) -> different epistemic regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq Knowledge State ... Kernel \neq Knowledge Space ... The Knower is a philosophical abstraction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reasserts the kernel must not be confused with the Knower: Kernel != Knowledge State and Kernel != Knowledge Space. Full research-model vocabulary listed: K=Knowledge Space, K_t=Knowledge State, N=Knower, Omega=Epistemic Horizon, rho_t=Epistemic Orientation, B_t=Discrimination/Buddhi, G_t=Operating Condition, delta=Knowledge-State Transformation, combined as (K_t,O_t,rho_t,G_t,Omega) --B_t--> d_t --delta--> K_{t+1}. Explicit correspondence-strength classification: strong correspondence (Kshetra/Kshetrajna<->Field/Knower); strong conceptual candidate (Buddhi<->Discrimination); interesting research hypotheses (Guna<->Operating condition; Chapter12<->Epistemic orientation); new research hypothesis (Chapter11<->Epistemic horizon); explicitly NOT established: Omega/rho/G/B are KnowledgeOS primitives; Omega=K; Moksha=K_max.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is "Moksha" mathematically a fixed point, boundary, quotient, or **change of state space altogether**?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'can a KnowledgeOS kernel be formally modeled as a discriminating dynamical system?' with X_{t+1}=F(X_t,O_t), X_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,rho_t), F=delta o B, and 14 concrete research questions: what are the primitive kernel operations; what is the algebra of Buddhi/discrimination; which operations are idempotent/commutative/monotonic; which create vs only transform information; which reduce vs introduce uncertainty; what exactly constitutes purification; can purification be an order on Sigma; is there a fixed point; is there a limit; is Moksha mathematically a fixed point, boundary, quotient, or a change of state space altogether. Flags the last as particularly interesting: Moksha might not be a state in the existing algebra but a transition to a different epistemic regime -- if that survives mathematical/DDD testing it would be a genuine theoretical contribution, not merely a Gita analogy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,H_t) = \text{the detectable discrepancy between represented knowledge and the current epistemic horizon}
a_rows_sample.statement: Upgrades the Zero hypothesis from Zero(K_t)=what is missing to Zero(K_t,H_t) = the detectable discrepancy between represented knowledge and the current epistemic horizon H_t: Z_t = H_t minus K_t (only if horizon and state are sets over the same typed universe) or more safely Z_t=Delta(K_t,H_t). Motivated by the tree metaphor's point that what is visible is not the whole structure; also connects verse 15.17 (Supreme Person entering/supporting the three worlds) to a Knowledge Horizon concept where the kernel need not contain all knowledge, K_t subset K with a reachable horizon H_t, so Zero(K_t,H_t) can report 'outside the current epistemic horizon' rather than 'does not exist'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t=(K_t,G_t,R_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Three chapters answer three different questions: Chapter 12 (Bhakti Yoga) -- how does the knower orient itself (epistemic orientation/relationship R_t); Chapter 13 (Kshetra-Kshetrajna) -- what is known and who knows (Knowledge Field K_t + Knower N); Chapter 14 (Guna-traya) -- under what condition does knowing occur (epistemic operating condition G_t). Combined into X_t=(K_t,G_t,R_t), explicitly a research model, not canonical. The Knower is not another item inside the Knowledge Field merely because it operates upon it (Kshetra != Kshetrajna as an architectural boundary), and the field is enumerated over the eight primitives {Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not say Buddhi=\delta ... B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) \rightarrow d_t ... \delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: Careful mathematical separation: Buddhi != delta. B_t is Evaluation/Discrimination, delta is State Transition. Formalized as B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) -> d_t, followed by delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}. Candidate (non-canonical) Buddhi decision codomain d_t in {Accept, Reject, Qualify, Defer, Transform, Escalate}; notes the philosophical lens does not solve the unresolved Qualify problem but may explain why qualification is a distinct act of discrimination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: decision correctness \neq decision outcome ... corroborate an existing architectural property rather than create a new primitive
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 12's outcome-independence (a disciplined actor performs an action without making the desired result the criterion) suggests decision correctness != decision outcome, close to the existing Command != Transformation and Guidance != Authority distinctions -- explicitly framed as Chapter 12 corroborating an existing architectural property rather than creating a new primitive, consistent with the Step 286 corroboration!=derivation methodology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Delta\text{Knowledge} = \Delta\text{Dimension} + \Delta\text{Quality} ... Knowledge Growth requires Discrimination
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes dimension from value: a statement could add a new dimension but have poor epistemic quality, or add no new dimension yet dramatically improve reliability/consistency/provenance/resolution/confidence/contextual understanding -- decomposed (as a research decomposition only) as Delta Knowledge = Delta Dimension + Delta Quality. Argues K_{t+1}>K_t in quantity does not imply K_{t+1} succ K_t epistemically, because more information != better knowledge; the kernel therefore requires Buddhi to discriminate: Knowledge Growth requires Discrimination, not merely ingestion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observe \rightarrow Represent \rightarrow Discriminate \rightarrow Qualify \rightarrow Decide \rightarrow Act \rightarrow Observe
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a closed kernel feedback loop Observe -> Represent -> Discriminate -> Qualify -> Decide -> Act -> Observe, with Buddhi as the discrimination mechanism, G_t as the condition of processing, and R_t as the orientation. Reformulates the dynamic system as X_t=(K_t,G_t,R_t), X_{t+1}=F(X_t,O_t) with F = delta o B, i.e. (K_t,G_t,R_t) --Buddhi--> decision --delta--> (K_{t+1},G_{t+1},R_{t+1}) -- assessed as potentially the first point where the Gita research approaches a mathematical model of the kernel rather than merely vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G_t is independent of \Sigma_t | OPEN ... Buddhi requires its own formal algebra | OPEN
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit status classification to avoid premature canonicalization: Field!=Knower and Knowledge State changes with time are already independently established; Buddhi~discrimination is a strong candidate correspondence; Guna~operating condition, Bhakti~epistemic orientation, Purification~trajectory improvement, and Moksha~regime transcendence are research hypotheses; while whether G_t is independent of Sigma_t, whether R_t is a KnowledgeOS state variable, whether Buddhi is a kernel operator, and whether Buddhi requires its own formal algebra are all marked fully OPEN. Revises Moksha again: Moksha != 'almost infinite knowledge'; Moksha ~ a transformation/transcendence of the ordinary conditioned epistemic regime, posing whether a limiting regime exists in which the system is no longer governed by ordinary G_t conditioning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can epistemic discrimination itself be formalized as an algebra?
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the deepest emerging question from Chapters 12-14 as: what is the minimum formal structure required for a system that continuously discriminates, transforms, and purifies a changing knowledge state? Proposes investigating B:(K_t,O_t,G_t,R_t)->D_t as the formal candidate for Buddhi, decomposable into operators {compare, distinguish, validate, qualify, prioritize, reject, accept, defer}, and determining whether these form an algebra -- framed as a legitimate research programme motivated by an exposed structural question, not because the Gita mandates implementing these operators. Culminating question: can epistemic discrimination itself be formalized as an algebra?

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapters11-14-horizon-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapters12-13-14-triple-model-field-condition-orientation' (batch B0054). Note: Extends the Chapter 12-13-14 (Field/Condition/Orientation) model by adding Chapter 11 as the source of a fourth research concept, Omega = epistemic horizon (explicitly not God, not identical to the Knowledge Space K), giving a four-term separation N != K_t != K != Omega and a five-fold kernel responsibility model (Perceive, Represent, Discriminate, Transform, Orient). Reformulates purification as progressive improvement of the epistemic state relative to its horizon, and poses 14 concrete mathematical research questions culminating in whether Moksha is a fixed point, boundary, quotient, or a change of state space altogether -- explicitly not established as any of these, framed as the strongest emerging research direction if it survives mathematical/DDD testing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: jnana-vijnana-trptatma ... the purport explicitly says that mere book knowledge without realization is insufficient. ... Representation of knowledge ≠ realization of knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws from Gita 6.8 (jnana-vijnana-trptatma) the distinction between represented/acquired knowledge and realized knowledge, classified as R6 corroboration of the corpus's already-independently-motivated Jnana!=Knowledge-primitive correction rather than a new derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi = discriminative power. Its essential function is to distinguish one thing from another. ... we cannot yet claim Buddhi = Qualify. The legitimate research statement is: Buddhi provides a philosophical lens for investigating whether KnowledgeOS requires an explicit discriminative capability, and whether Qualify is the technical manifestation of such a capability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the working definition of Buddhi from a loose 'intelligence/decision-making' gloss to specifically 'discriminative power' (the capacity to distinguish one thing from another), and connects this precisely to the corpus's unresolved Qualify gap, while explicitly refusing to assert Buddhi=Qualify as an identity - stating only that Buddhi is a lens for investigating whether Qualify is the technical manifestation of a general discriminative capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: many of our existing theoretical problems are precisely discrimination problems. For example, Step 287 had to distinguish `= ≠ ≡ ≠ ≈ ≠ ≅_λ`. The research itself had to discriminate between four relations that were previously at risk of being conflated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that KnowledgeOS's recurring need to carefully distinguish near-identical relations and categories (e.g. the four-way equality register split in Step 287) is itself independent evidence for a cross-cutting discrimination capability being architecturally necessary, offered as a stronger form of corroboration than a bare terminological correspondence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify(x, 𝒩, K_t, C, t, Π) where qualification depends upon: what is being asserted, who/what is asserting, current knowledge state, context, time, provenance, evidence. This is a hypothesis — not a proposed canonical signature yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reframing the unresolved Qualify gap from a single-argument boolean test Qualify(x) to a multi-parameter function Qualify(x, Knower, K_t, Context, time, Provenance), explicitly marked as an unadopted hypothesis rather than a canonical signature, motivated by the Jnana/Vijnana distinction's implication that qualification is a richer epistemic process than a single test.

type_signature.domain: assertion x, knower N, state K_t, context C, time t, provenance Pi

a_rows_sample.anchor: If Chapter 7 is right, GK-13 splits: Jñāna ~ represented, Vijñāna ~ qualified — and the pair straddles Qualify, not δ. ... it supplies NO body for Qualify
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally challenges the existing register mapping GK-13 (Jnana ~ delta) as potentially needing to split into Jnana (represented) and Vijnana (qualified/validated), locating the split at the Qualify boundary rather than at the transformation operator delta; explicitly records that this sharpens the question at Qualify without supplying any predicate, policy semantics, or evidence criterion that would actually narrow the G1 gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sharpening a question is not narrowing a gap. No philosophical source may fill Qualify, and Chapter 7 does not. ... this is precisely the hazard REFINED-STEP-286 §6 already opened for Cavell ... H-G7-1 is a THIRD such motivation and must not be merged with either.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a load-bearing methodological principle: sharpening/re-motivating an existing irreducible gap (Qualify, G1) from a new philosophical angle is not the same as narrowing it; explicitly refuses to merge the new Jnana/Vijnana motivation with a separately pre-existing Cavell-motivated Qualify hypothesis, treating three independent philosophical sources gesturing at the same one gap as one piece of evidence, not three.

a_rows_sample.anchor: represented knowledge ≠ realized/validated knowledge ... J_t = epistemically represented knowledge; V_t = realized/grounded knowledge. Not necessarily as two new primitives — that would be premature.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and reinforces the Jnana(J_t)/Vijnana(V_t) represented-vs-realized-knowledge distinction from Gita 9.1, explicitly flagged as a theory-level distinction rather than a proposal for two new KnowledgeOS primitives.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify: Evidence × Proposition × Context × Provenance × Discrimination → Epistemic Status. Potential statuses could eventually include: Observed, Reported, Supported, Qualified, Ratified, Rejected, Unresolved. But do not canonicalize these yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate multi-argument signature for Qualify (Evidence x Proposition x Context x Provenance x Discrimination -> Epistemic Status) together with a candidate seven-value epistemic-status enumeration, explicitly marked as not to be canonicalized, motivated by the claim that qualification is unlikely to be a binary yes/no function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jñāna → Knowledge is the wrong mapping. Jñāna → Knowing, i.e. the transformation, not the state. Jñātā → the Knower (already ratified as Kṣetrajña). Jñeya → the known, i.e. Proposition/Assertion content. Jñāna → the transformation δ / the act of knowing — not K. ... Verdict R4 — falsifiable, useful, and it reinforces the ratified decision rather than challenging it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the register's Jnana->Knowledge mapping using the traditional Sanskrit Tripuṭī triad (knower/knowing/known), relocating Jnana to the transformation delta rather than the state K, on the grounds that KnowledgeOS deliberately excludes 'Knowledge' from its 8 ratified primitives and from its Steps 100-158 vocabulary -- so mapping a Priority-1 Gita term onto a deliberately-absent primitive would have silently reintroduced it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jñātā → Knower. Jñeya → Known/Proposition. Jñāna → Knowing/Transformation. Thus Jñāna ~ δ, as a research correspondence, not an identity claim. ... The Gītā mapping changed KnowledgeOS by causing a candidate mapping to be tested and rejected. That is scientifically more valuable than finding another analogy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strongly endorses the Jnana correction as the program's most valuable negative result, explicitly reframing Jnana~delta as a research correspondence rather than an identity, and generalizing the underlying methodological point: causing a candidate mapping to be tested and rejected is scientifically more valuable than accumulating another surviving analogy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `[S]` `Jñāna` — knowing (Ch. 4, 7, 13). The revised prompt maps it to **`Knowledge`**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the H-K13 correction: 'Knowledge' is absent from the 8 ratified primitives and from the Steps 100-158 vocabulary; the corpus's Sanskrit reading situates Jñāna inside the Tripuṭī (Jñātā·Jñāna·Jñeya = knower·knowing·known); corrected mapping is Jñātā→Knower (ratified Kṣetrajña), Jñeya→the known (Proposition/assertion content), Jñāna→the transformation δ, not K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Jñāna` maps to **knowing/transformation**, not to `Knowledge`. ... **Formal consequence:** `Jñātā → Knower`, `Jñeya → Proposition`, `Jñāna → δ`.
b_rows_sample.statement: H-K13 restated as a correction rather than an addition: Jñāna maps to knowing/transformation, not to Knowledge (deliberately absent from the 8 ratified primitives); Jñātā→Knower, Jñeya→Proposition, Jñāna→δ. Architecture and governance consequence: none — reinforces an existing ratified decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Jñāna ∼ δ` rather than `Jñāna = δ`. That follows the new promotion rule: **Correspondence ⇏ Type ⇏ Primitive ⇏ Canonical Architecture**
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Jnana's mapping further: Jnana is correspondence-related to (∼) delta, not equal to (=) delta, following a new stated promotion rule 'Correspondence does not imply Type does not imply Primitive does not imply Canonical Architecture' — intended to prevent the project from gradually converting philosophical analogies into architectural claims.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Area | Current verdict |
b_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a 15-row status table as the current evidence state: W/Omega referent layer recovered/promoted; Observation closed as discovery gap; Sanjaya corpus-native six-valued structure; Jnana mapping corrected (Jnana~delta, not Knowledge); Knowledge primitive deliberately absent/corroborated; Kshetra/Kshetrajna ratified as genuine contribution; Karma/Phala corroborated but weakened to quotient-relative; Vairagya/outcome-independence independently supported; Sarathi/guidance-authority boundary independently implemented; K_atma destroyed; Theta_total rejected (does not type-check); Equality graded G1 (under-specified, not absent); =_semantic in D285-5 confirmed a methodological defect; history⊊structural⊊semantic is a verification-lane construct not corpus fact; Qualify still G1 and still the πK blocker.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **`Knowledge` is absent from the 8 primitives while `Observation` and `Proposition` are present.** The ratified model deliberately does **not** name `Knowledge` a primitive. `K_t` is therefore **not** "the knowledge state" in the verification lane's sense — it is a **state over a knowledge-bearing vocabulary**. **Two different objects wearing one letter.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms Knowledge is absent from the 8 ratified primitives (while Observation and Proposition are present) and draws a sharper distinction: K_t is not 'the knowledge state' in the verification lane's sense, it is a state over a knowledge-bearing vocabulary — two different objects sharing one letter (K).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### 21.1 No `Knowledge` primitive ... ### 21.2 No universal Knower inside KnowledgeOS ... ### 21.3 No `Θ_total` ... ### 21.4 No `𝒦_ātma` ... ### 21.5 No repaired Θ operators
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates an explicit five-item exclusion list stating what the reconstructed ontology does NOT contain: no Knowledge primitive (Jnana does not justify adding it), no universal Knower inside KnowledgeOS (the theological proposition is outside the formal falsification domain; the KnowledgeOS result is only that a universal Knower is not derivable as an architectural requirement), no Theta_total (rejected by typing), no K_atma (rejected, persistence already represented by existing provenance/lineage structures), and no repaired Theta operators (the R4 type-check failure is evidence against the construction, not a missing implementation feature).

a_aliases: Jnana-Vijnana split onto Qualify not delta

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-jnana-vijnana-realization-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'jnana-to-knowing-not-knowledge-correction' (batch B0053). Note: Gita Chapters 6, 7 and 9 (jnanam ... sa-vijnanam, 6.8, 7.2, 9.1) distinguish Jnana (acquired/represented knowledge) from Vijnana (realized/grounded/integrated knowing), with the purport explicitly saying book knowledge without realization is insufficient. The hypothesis (H-G7-1) proposes this maps to KnowledgeOS's unresolved Qualify gap (Observation x Policy -> Evidence, classified G1 irreducible) rather than to the transformation operator delta - i.e. represented-knowledge != qualified/validated-knowledge. The corpus's own synthesis (source 16-GAP-UPDATE) records this as challenging the EXISTING register mapping GK-13 Jnana ~ delta (opening open item GK-Q2: should GK-13 split into Jnana/Vijnana straddling Qualify instead), while ruling that the hypothesis supplies no predicate/body for Qualify and must not be merged with the pre-existing Cavell-motivated Qualify reclassification hypothesis (a second source gesturing at the same one gap, not two-fold evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human first has/conceives an Ideal State ... IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE. That is a substantially different model from the one I was using before.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major reorientation: humans do not build up an ideal state from arbitrary observations; instead a human first has/conceives an Ideal State and then evaluates reality against it, giving the pipeline IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE, substantially reversing the previously-used observation-first model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal state ... The complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for the thing at that point in time. ... all applicable rules; all required participants; ... I_t = Ideal Knowledge State at t ... O_t -- comparison with I_t --> K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal state I_t broadly as the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for a thing at time t; for an election system this would include all applicable rules, required participants, required conditions, valid relationships, required evidence, expected states, constraints, applicable laws, and known principles; every new piece of observed information O_t is evaluated against I_t, giving the extraction problem O_t --comparison with I_t--> K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge. ... K_t subset I_t ... The ideal state itself may be unknown to us. ... I_t -- the theoretical ideal state, and hat-I_t -- our current extracted/estimated representation of it. Then: hat-I_t != I_t in general. That may actually explain your earlier statement: "We try our best but never achieve the best."
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'information on the ideal state is knowledge' to 'information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge', giving K_t subset-or-equal I_t as the established/identified portion of the ideal state -- but the ideal state I_t itself may be unknown to us, so we must distinguish the theoretical ideal state I_t from our current extracted/estimated representation hat-I_t, with hat-I_t != I_t in general, explaining 'we try our best but never achieve the best'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known) ... Probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations. Not: Knowledge=Probability. Instead: Probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Locates probability's role: for an ideal-state element x, given incomplete and overlapping observations O_1..O_n we estimate P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known); probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations, not in defining Knowledge -- probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state, not Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System must have backup capability ... backup configuration exists ... If the applicable reasoning rules determine that the observation satisfies the criterion, we establish: F_t: "System has backup capability." ... the fact is not produced merely from the observation. It is produced by: Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of fact production: ideal state I_t requires 'system must have backup capability', observation O_t is 'backup configuration exists'; comparing O_t against I_t via applicable reasoning rules establishes fact F_t='System has backup capability' -- a fact is produced not merely from observation but from Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logic = mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state. ... I_t: A and B and C. Observed: O_t: A,B,not-C. Logic gives: O_t does not entail I_t. Therefore the determination might be: F_t: "Current state does not satisfy the ideal state."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines logic's role as the mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state: given ideal state I_t=(A and B and C) and observed O_t=(A,B,not-C), logic determines O_t does not entail I_t, yielding determination F_t='Current state does not satisfy the ideal state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(A)=1, P(B)=0.9, P(C)=0.6, P(D)=0.2. Then our extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain. The probability is therefore attached to the extraction/determination, not necessarily to the underlying ideal state itself. That gives: I_t -> hat-I_t where hat-I_t is probabilistically estimated from available information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the origin of graded 0-to-1 values: if the ideal state requires A,B,C,D but observations only partially resolve them (P(A)=1,P(B)=0.9,P(C)=0.6,P(D)=0.2), the extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain -- this probability attaches to the extraction/determination I_t -> hat-I_t, not to the underlying ideal state itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where does the Ideal State come from? ... A. Given by reality I_t=Reality_t B. Given by human knowledge I_t=HumanModel_t C. Given by rules/laws/principles I_t=NormativeModel_t D. Given by the domain model I_t=DomainModel_t E. An ideal mathematical state I_t=I* F. Some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge). We should not assume which one it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'Where does the Ideal State come from?' as, in the author's opinion, the most important unresolved problem, with six unassumed candidate sources: given by reality (I_t=Reality_t), given by human knowledge (I_t=HumanModel_t), given by rules/laws/principles (I_t=NormativeModel_t), given by the domain model (I_t=DomainModel_t), an ideal mathematical state (I_t=I*), or some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge) -- explicitly: we should not assume which one it is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state. And the current Knowledge state is K_t while the ideal state is I_t. The goal of knowledge extraction could therefore be: K_t -> I_t or more realistically: K_t approx I_t with the difference I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves 'is Knowledge a collection of facts?' into a richer formulation: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state; with current knowledge state K_t and ideal state I_t, knowledge extraction aims at K_t -> I_t or more realistically K_t approx I_t, with the residual I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge." I would change "every information" to "every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state". ... "I believe the ideal state contains X." That is information about someone's belief, not necessarily Knowledge about the ideal state. ... "The document says X." ... Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the overbroad claim 'every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge', proposing instead 'every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state'; example: 'I believe the ideal state contains X' is information about someone's belief, not Knowledge about the ideal state, and 'the document says X' is knowledge that the document says X, not knowledge that X is true. Preserves the distinction: Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IDEAL STATE -> (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION -> (evidence/uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal <-> observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time. ... Probability primarily helps with the extraction from imperfect information, while Logic helps determine consequences and relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full revised pipeline diagram: IDEAL STATE (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION (branching into evidence and uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal<->observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time; probability primarily helps with extraction from imperfect information, logic helps determine consequences and relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before determination, we now need to investigate: What is the Ideal State? Because determination is: D_t = Compare(Observed_t, Ideal_t) and if we don't understand Ideal_t, we don't fully understand D_t. ... IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the research direction: before determination can be understood, 'What is the Ideal State?' must be investigated, since determination is formalized as D_t=Compare(Observed_t,Ideal_t) and understanding D_t requires understanding Ideal_t; sets the research sequence as IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE, with Probability->uncertain extraction and Logic->comparison and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the fundamental question for KnowledgeOS is not "How do we store Knowledge?" and not even "How do we extract Knowledge?" It may be: "How is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?" ... Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between them. I would now research Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before we touch the Kernel again.
a_rows_sample.statement: States what may be 'the biggest discovery so far': the fundamental KnowledgeOS question may be neither 'how do we store Knowledge' nor 'how do we extract Knowledge' but 'how is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?'; Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between Ideal State and Observed State. Proposes researching Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before returning to Kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information" you mean all possible information about the thing, not merely "some information." So your proposition is: I_t = the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t. And I_t may be infinite.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'every information' as meaning ALL possible information about a thing, not merely some information: I_t is redefined as the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t, and I_t may be infinite -- a much stronger interpretation than given previously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_t subset I_t or, more realistically, imperfect projections of I_t. The extraction process is therefore: I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, with the extraction being imperfect because the underlying elements can overlap and the observation process cannot completely distinguish them.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human/system cannot access all of the (possibly infinite) I_t, only observations O_t subset I_t or imperfect projections of it; extraction is I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, imperfect because underlying elements can overlap and observation cannot completely distinguish them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = the space of all possible information/knowledge elements ... I_t subset K is the complete/ideal information state relevant at that time. Then an observer A has only an extracted state: K_t^A subset I_t ... K_t^A != I_t in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens 'Knowledge is a state and subset of elements of the infinite Knowledge Space' into: K-script (the space of all possible information/knowledge elements), with I_t subset K-script being the complete/ideal information state relevant at time t; an observer A has only an extracted state K_t^A subset I_t (or a representation/projection of it), and because extraction is imperfect, K_t^A != I_t in general.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A). So probability describes the extraction uncertainty. ... Knowledge itself is not probability. Rather: Probability can describe the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.
a_rows_sample.statement: For an ideal-state element x in I_t that an observer cannot directly verify, the observer estimates P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A) given its observations -- probability describes extraction uncertainty, consistent with 'the elements overlap and only probability can extract them as separately as possible' (still to be tested as the right mathematical mechanism, but a coherent hypothesis). Knowledge itself is not probability; probability describes the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I_t means all possible information, then we need to distinguish: possible information from true information and knowable information. ... whether your I_t means: 1. all logically possible information, or 2. all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or 3. all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t. I think this distinction is now the next critical question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Raises the next critical question: since not every possible description of a system is true, I_t must be disambiguated among three readings -- (1) all logically possible information, (2) all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or (3) all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t; this distinction will determine the meaning of the 'infinite Knowledge Space' and what KnowledgeOS is trying to extract from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at time t ... K_t (script) = Infinite Knowledge Space at t and I_t subset K_t (script) could represent an ideal state/configuration of the domain. But even I_t may itself be infinite. ... K_t = Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the extraction/projection available to the observer.
a_rows_sample.statement: If I_t can be infinite, it should not be modeled as a finite list of facts but as the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at t; introduces K-script_t (infinite Knowledge Space at t) with I_t subset K-script_t as an ideal state/configuration of the domain (itself possibly infinite), and the observer's actual accessible/extracted knowledge as K_t subset I_t or, more generally, K_t=Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the observer's extraction/projection function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t={x_1,x_2,x_3,...}. We cannot observe all of them. ... construct an estimate hat-I_t from the observations. For an element x: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) can express our uncertainty ... probability is increasingly looking like a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, rather than a definition of Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: With an infinite ideal state I_t={x_1,x_2,...} that cannot be fully observed, an estimate hat-I_t is constructed from observations O_{<=t}, and for an element x, P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) expresses uncertainty about membership; probability is increasingly a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, not a definition of Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \neq A Single Assertion ... K_t \neq A Set of Assertions ... K_t = A Structured Collection of Assertions + Their Relationships + Their Epistemic Status + Their History ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge State K_t as a 6-component structure: Assertions A_t, Relationships R_t, Evidence E_t, History H_t (all previous Knowledge States), Zero findings Z_t, and Lord candidates L_t; forms a Knowledge Graph G_t=(A_t,R_t) with Assertions as nodes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identical, Equivalent, Consistent, Contradictory, Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction ... R_j = (A_i, A_k, Type, Strength, Evidence)
a_rows_sample.statement: Types the Relationship edges of the knowledge graph with eight relation kinds spanning both the earlier Compare vocabulary (Identical/Equivalent/Consistent/Contradictory) and the newer conflict taxonomy (Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction), each carrying Strength and supporting Evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State_t = (K_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) ... I_t = (D_I, V_I, R_I, C_I) ... Compare(K_t, I_t) -> G_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the complete System State as (KnowledgeState,IdealState,Question/Intent,Context), formalizes the Ideal State I_t=(IdealDimensions,IdealValues,IdealRelationships,Constraints), and defines Compare(K_t,I_t)->G_t as the set of gaps between current knowledge and the ideal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Detection: Normative conflict between A_2 and A_3 ... Z_1 = (Normative Conflict, {A_2, A_3}, 'Family duty vs. war duty') ... Resolution... Zero Resolved: Z_1 is resolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the full Arjuna example through five knowledge states K_0..K_4, showing a Zero-detected NormativeConflict finding created when the opposing-side assertion is added and resolved once the moral-conflict assertion clarifies the relation between the grandfather and opponent assertions as Compatible rather than contradictory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Knowledge State should probably not be defined as 'everything KnowledgeOS has.' It should be defined as the epistemically structured state relevant to a particular observer, purpose, context and time... K_t = K(X,P,N,C,tau)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modelling K_t as an absolute, single global object; since the Observation model already parameterizes on Purpose/Observer/Context/Time, the Knowledge State must be similarly parameterized: K_t=K(X,Purpose,Knower,Context,tau), since two Knowers (Arjuna vs Dhrtarastra) observing the same reality do not share an identical Knowledge State.

type_signature.domain: Reality x Purpose x Knower x Context x Time

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \supset Z_t but Z_t=Zero(K_t) which means the state contains the output of an operation that operates on the state itself... I would therefore define: K_t = CurrentKnowledgeState and separately H_{0:t}=KnowledgeHistory
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags a definitional circularity in the S0783 Knowledge State: embedding Z_t=Zero(K_t) and H_t={K_0,...,K_t} as components of K_t itself makes K_t contain the output of an operation applied to K_t, and makes each historical K_i recursively contain its own history; proposes separating CurrentKnowledgeState K_t from KnowledgeHistory H_{0:t} and computing Zero(K_t)/Lord(K_t) as derived views rather than stored fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion does not simply exist. It applies somewhere... Scope = (Context, Time, Subject, Boundary, ...) This is essential for avoiding false contradictions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Scope as a missing concept an assertion needs (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 applies to production but not test; a policy applies to one organization but not another), motivated as necessary to avoid false apparent contradictions between assertions that actually hold in different scopes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Conflict Free State ... Coherence = all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints ... A Knowledge State may contain unknowns, conflicts, competing interpretations, unresolved questions, normative tensions and still be coherent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Coherence away from 'no contradictions' toward 'all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints', explicitly allowing a coherent Knowledge State to contain unknowns, unresolved normative tensions and competing interpretations without being incoherent -- Knowledge State != Conflict-Free State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 13: What is the formal structure of the Knowledge State? ... Is Knowledge State a set, graph, typed graph, labelled graph, relational structure, lattice, or some composite algebraic structure?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 13 as the prerequisite to formalizing distance: K_t must be given an exact formal structure (set/graph/typed-graph/relational-structure/lattice/composite) before any distance/measurement function over it can be mathematically meaningful.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is the formal, typed, structured representation ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t, T_t, G_t, C_t, M_t) ... Knowledge State = A Structured Typed Graph with Epistemic Metadata
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-component Knowledge State (Assertions, Relationships, Evidence, History, ZeroFindings, LordCandidates, Temporal structure, Knowledge Graph, Context, Metadata/provenance) formalized as a typed, directed, labelled graph, with immutability of History (new states appended, never overwritten) as a core invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K contains things that are not knowledge ... Zero findings: No. Zero findings are observations about the Knowledge State. Lord candidates: Definitely no. History: Probably not part of the instantaneous Knowledge State. Knowledge Graph: probably a representation of the Knowledge State, not another independent component inside it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the ten-component K_t as a category error: Zero findings and Lord candidates are derived observations/hypotheses about the state, not the state itself; History is a temporal model over states, not a field within one state; the typed graph is a representation/projection of the state, not an ontologically independent component. Proposes a smaller canonical K_t=(Propositions,Assertions,Relationships,Evidence,EpistemicState,Context,Temporal,Provenance) with Z_t=Zero(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), L_t=Lord(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), and H_t=History(K_0,...,K_t) all computed externally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Contained in' is not the right mathematical relation. Entity not-subset Proposition ... use Participates In / Referenced By / Forms instead.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the typed-universe diagram's 'contained in' arrows (Entity/Dimension/Value -> Propositions) which are not subset relations: an entity participates in a proposition, a dimension is referenced by it; recommends participates-in/referenced-by/forms relations instead, consistent with the earlier containment-vs-set-inclusion correction from Question 7.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SystemState_t = (K_t, U_t, X_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, Z_t, L_t, H_t) ... K_t = Knowledge State only
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the complete runtime SystemState as wrapping the (now smaller) Knowledge State K_t together with Understanding U_t, Domain X_t, Ideal I_t, Intent/Question Q_t, Context C_t, Knower N_t, and the derived Z_t/L_t/H_t, cleanly separating what KnowledgeOS knows from what it also tracks about the Knower and the epistemic journey.

Is a Relationship a proposition? Is an Epistemic State part of an assertion or external? Is a Gap part of knowledge or a finding about knowledge?
