a_rows_sample.anchor: the word is an expression generated from an underlying semantic structure, rather than being identical to the meaning itself. ... EXPRESSION != MEANING. ... Is the definition describing the concept or merely its current wording?

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic identity must not be altered merely by representational transformation. ... database representation / JSON representation / event representation / replay representation / audit representation / human-readable report. a_rows_sample.anchor: sandhi as boundary transformation: when two elements meet, they do not merely concatenate; governed transformation rules determine the resulting expression. ... Evidence + Evaluation must not silently become Evidence-with-interpretation ... Composition must not silently transfer semantic ownership.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sandhi-derived 'semantic sandhi' concept: composing two bounded contexts (e.g. Evidence + Evaluation) at their boundary must not silently collapse into one merged concept that transfers ownership; a governed relationship must remain explicit at the boundary. Candidate principles: 'Composition must not silently transfer semantic ownership'; 'Transformation must not silently change semantic identity'; 'Expression changes are not evidence of identity changes' -- all explicitly marked as candidate principles pending Shani's promotion decision, not yet constitutional invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Root/intrinsic meaning -> Contextual/domain meaning -> Conventional/operational usage ... Term != Concept != Usage. ... TERM -> general concept -> constitutional Evidence -> implementation object -> database table. We must not assume these are equivalent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Vocabulary-layer stack (Term -> Concept -> Domain meaning -> Operational realization) formalizing Term!=Concept!=Usage, illustrated with 'evidence' passing through general concept, constitutional Evidence, implementation object, and database table -- raising the question of where architectural meaning actually becomes normative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: grammatical tense/mood can encode distinctions beyond simple past/present/future ... event time versus knowledge-state time. ... EVENT TIME / CAPTURE TIME / EVALUATION TIME / PUBLICATION TIME / KNOWLEDGE TIME. This is much more precise than simply having created_at.
a_rows_sample.statement: Five-way temporal distinction for Evidence derived from Sanskrit tense/mood grammar: event time (when it happened), capture time (when observed), evaluation time (when interpreted), publication time (when frozen/published), knowledge time (when the system knew it) -- more precise than a single created_at timestamp.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Panini and Topology are not competing lenses. They look at different aspects of transformation. ... How is transformation governed? -> What structural properties survive transformation?
a_rows_sample.statement: Pairs Paninian (governs how transformation happens) with Topology (identifies what structural properties survive it) as complementary, not competing, diagnostic lenses, producing a six-lens review sequence: Ganesha (what is it?) -> Leonardo (what else could it be?) -> Krishna (why should it exist?) -> Panini (how can it transform?) -> Topology (what survives transformation?) -> Shani (what must never break?).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Panini becomes a hypothesis/model to test, rather than an unquestioned ontology. ... Where does the observed data violate or extend our assumed rule system?
a_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens-driven reframing: Paninian grammatical rules should be tested against independently observed transformation structure (how much do they explain, where do they fail) rather than assumed as an unquestioned ontology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Model B executed -- K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda) with policy as an argument to T ... If pi in K, then revoking or amending a policy changes every stored state, while nothing that is known has changed. ... VERDICT: pi is EXTERNAL. MATHEMATICALLY VERIFIED by counterexample.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes Model B (policy external to K, passed as an argument to T) successfully, and gives a counterexample against Model A (policy internal): if pi were in K, revoking/amending a policy would change every stored state despite no change in what is known, and two states holding identical knowledge under different policies would be unequal -- policy governs the transition, not what is known. Verdict: pi is external to K, mathematically verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 and K2 with identical content, status, temporality and policy -- differing only in history ... structural: False, semantic: True, provenance-sensitive: False, historical identity: False. ... History(K) != K is fundamental. lambda belongs OUTSIDE K, as History: K -> Histories.
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs two states K1/K2 identical in content/status/temporality/policy but differing in history, computing all four equality relations from the earlier stress test (structural=False, semantic=True, provenance-sensitive=False, historical identity=False), demonstrating semantic equality can be TRUE while historical identity is FALSE -- proving a single tuple containing lambda cannot express both relations at once, and that including lambda in K makes structural equality history-sensitive, breaking deduplication and merge. Verdict: History(K)!=K is fundamental; lambda belongs outside K as History:K->Histories, mathematically verified, and aligned with the real implementation (a separate lineage graph, no KnowledgeState).

a_rows_sample.anchor: same proposition, different evidence: Observed vs Supported ... same proposition+evidence, different policy: Observed vs Unknown ... Model 1 REFUTED ... Model 2 REFUTED (insufficient) ... Model 3 SURVIVES ... sigma is not a primitive of the Knowledge State. It is derived from an Assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests all three S1602-mandated sigma models by execution: Model 1 (sigma:Proposition->Status) is refuted because one proposition yields three distinct status values depending on context; Model 2 (adding Evidence,Context) is refuted as insufficient because policy also changes the outcome and is not an argument; Model 3 (a full Assessment function over Proposition,Evidence,Context,Policy, with Status derived) survives. Concludes epistemic status is a derived Assessment output, not a Knowledge-State primitive -- noted as exactly Step 232.4's Validation:K x X->Assessment shape, extended to status, which Step 245 had re-internalized as a primitive.

a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a direct counterexample refuting theta as a function of Proposition alone: the same proposition can carry two overlapping-but-distinct assertion instances with different validity intervals, which a single-valued function theta:Proposition->Interval cannot represent. Verdict: temporal validity belongs to the assertion instance, mathematically verified; also notes the four bitemporal dimensions (valid/known/record/decision time) are not collapsible to one timestamp, yet the real implementation does collapse them to a single decidedAt field -- flagged as an IMPLEMENTATION GAP.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_0's own content has edges = empty set. A set suffices for the constructed example. The graph is required only when relations between propositions must be expressed. a_rows_sample.statement: Notes that Step 245's own concrete K0 instance uses zero edges, so a plain set would have sufficed; concludes C=(V,E)'s graph structure is a representation choice justified only when inter-proposition relations must be expressed, not an ontological fact or implementation necessity -- downgrading Step 245's unstated graph assumption to PROPOSED rather than CORPUS ESTABLISHES; this is the one component of K0 that survives the attack (in reduced form).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = a set of Assertions, where Assertion=(Proposition,Interval,Context) [with Evidence, Assessment, History, Policy, Authority, T, Validation all listed as external] ... a_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Subtractive-structural, statistical-residual, and absence-typology are **three different operations under one name.**
a_rows_sample.statement: X-005: the corpus itself records two incompatible definitions of 'the Zero lens' 90 minutes apart, neither citing the other -- 'remove prior structure, ask what can be recovered from the source alone' (subtractive/structural, 20260824-152415, S1-F034) versus 'what statistically persists after explaining away non-knowledge' (statistical residual, 20260824-154254). Neither matches the absence typology (not mentioned != absent; absent from enumeration != excluded; not represented != zero; unknown != false; classes: zero/absence/unrepresented/unknown/not-applicable/excluded/not-tested) the reviewer has been applying in every review in this register, supplied by its own standing instructions. Three different operations share one name; this does not invalidate any finding (the reviewer's own usage is well-specified and consistent) but is a naming defect. Update (S2-R-F034.2): the lens was additionally used undefined for ~17 hours before any written definition existed (S1-F013, S1-F016, S1-F021 reached Zero-derived conclusions first), so the full picture is: used undefined, then defined twice incompatibly within 90 minutes, then a third sense applied by this reviewer -- meaning 'the Zero lens shows...' is not a single claim anywhere in the corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the corpus's most-used instrument was **used undefined for ~17 hours**, then **defined twice incompatibly within 90 minutes**
a_rows_sample.statement: The Zero lens was defined on 2026-08-24 at 15:24 while in continuous use since 2026-08-23 -- a ~17 hour lag -- meaning every Zero-lens conclusion recorded before that timestamp (S1-F013, S1-F016, S1-F021) used an undefined instrument; recorded by Session 1 as a caveat, not invalidation, and the reviewer concurs. Combined with a separately recovered miss (S1-F024), the full picture is worse than either finding alone: used undefined for ~17 hours, then defined twice incompatibly within 90 minutes (subtractive-structural at 15:24:15; statistical-residual at 15:42:54), and this review's own session applies a third sense (absence typology, per X-005).

a_rows_sample.anchor: `revok` scoring zero in v1.1 does **not** establish that revocation is absent from KnowledgeOS. ... Concluding `IMPLEMENT` from a grep would be exactly the *not mentioned → absent* conversion I have charged others with.
a_rows_sample.statement: The reviewer applies the Zero lens to its own result: a zero grep-count for 'revok*' in v1.1 does not establish that revocation is absent from KnowledgeOS, because Authority is 'held by the Authority context' -- a supporting context whose internals v1.1 describes but does not specify -- and temporal validity of a grant may legitimately live there. What is established is narrower: the core model cannot express revocation-aware temporal validity, and nothing verifiable says the supporting context does either. Concluding IMPLEMENT from the grep alone would repeat the 'not mentioned -> absent' error charged against other findings in this register. Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION, not IMPLEMENT.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: *Absence must not silently become an epistemic state*. ⟦L⟧ ⟨Z-1⟩ says exactly this. **CONSISTENT**, reached independently; ninth angle on the absence family.
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F038's claim 'absence must not silently become an epistemic state' is confirmed as already stated by existing law (<Z-1>), reached independently -- classified CONSISTENT rather than corroborating, per the register's own standing rule about not treating instruction-derived matches as corroboration. Called the ninth angle on the corpus's recurring absence family of findings. Verdict: DO NOT IMPLEMENT (already protected). Separately, the corpus's explicit refusal to store epistemic state as possible worlds (following Gardenfors) is confirmed as converging with a separate resolution of a 'Fagin thread' elsewhere in the corpus -- a matter of placement (where the refusal belongs), not of ontology (what possible worlds are).

Elaborates the earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Transition division with explicit role definitions: Zero detects gaps/conflicts/boundaries; Lord expands the possibility space; Sarathi navigates/guides; Transition actually changes state. The earlier Sarathi formalization is given a full function signature: Sarathi(K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) -> a_t, where a_t is the next epistemic action -- described as remarkably close to what is now called action selection/guidance, though the modern formal model deliberately avoids promoting the old lens vocabulary into architectural objects. Confirms the earlier KnowledgeOS-as-Epistemic-Sarathi formulation (rather than an answer engine) and its See != Guide != Decide principle, noting it later became compatible with the modern formal chain Evidence != Determination != Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action.

type_signature.domain: K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, confirmation theory, decision theory, and justification.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's culminating 'complete formal system for KnowledgeOS': Sigma_t = {cr_t(P): P in L} as the epistemic state; Sigma_{t+1} = Sigma_t(.|E_t) (or Jeffrey Conditionalization for uncertain evidence) as the transition; confirmation as E confirms H iff Sigma_t(H|E) > Sigma_t(H); decision as a_t = argmax_A sum_i u(A&S_i)*Sigma_t(S_i|A) (EDT) or the CDT analogue; and the Three Lenses re-stated as Zero (regularity/confirmation-measures/Scott Axiom), Lord (Bayes's theorem/likelihood ratios), Sarathi (decision theory/Conditionalization). Final claim: 'These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS' -- asserted without independent derivation or proof of fit to the prior KnowledgeOS kernel formalizations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Lens examines the boundary between what a KnowledgeOS knowledge state represents and what it does not represent. ... What is absent, undefined, unobserved, undiscovered, unresolved, unmodelled, assumed away, or otherwise outside the current representation? ... Not represented ⇒ Does not exist ... That inference is generally invalid. ... a discipline of non-collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Zero Lens's purpose: examine the boundary of what a knowledge state represents vs does not, explicitly to block the invalid inference 'not represented ⇒ does not exist'; names it a 'discipline of non-collapse' that protects distinctions ordinary information systems routinely destroy.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Zero 
eq KnowledgeElement ... Zero 
eq Dimension ... Zero 
eq Value ... Zero is a constraint on interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: First architectural principle: Zero must not be modelled as a domain object/knowledge element/dimension/value sitting alongside Knowledge/Dimension/Statement/Value in a hierarchy; it is a lens applied to the knowledge state (Z(K_t)) and a constraint on interpretation, not a data field.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency(X)=Present / Absent / Unknown ... A conventional database often collapses B and C into: NULL. KnowledgeOS must not. ... these are different epistemic axes ... Zero is pushing us toward orthogonal semantic properties, rather than a single status field.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues a dimension's epistemic state needs several orthogonal axes (Dimension, Assessment, Value, Evidence), not one enum collapsing 'investigated-and-absent' and 'never-established' into a single NULL — giving worked contrasting examples of the same dimension under different Assessment/Value/Evidence combinations.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
NO_EVIDENCE 
eq INVALID_EVIDENCE ... NOT_ASSESSED 
eq LOW_CONFIDENCE ... coverage gap ... epistemic uncertainty ... NOT_APPLICABLE 
eq UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three further non-collapse distinctions with worked examples: no-evidence vs invalid/unreliable evidence; not-assessed (a coverage gap) vs low-confidence (an epistemic uncertainty after assessment); and not-applicable (evaluated and outside domain) vs unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero tells us not to resolve the contradiction merely by selecting one value. ... Claims(Version)={c_1,c_2} with Conflict(c_1,c_2)=True ... KnowledgeOS should present both information and warn the owner rather than silently deciding which information is correct. ... Conflict \neq Unknown ... Conflict \neq Invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: When two trusted sources conflict (e.g. Version=2.69 vs 3.85), Zero requires preserving the conflict as a first-class claim set with an explicit Conflict flag rather than silently picking a winner; a conflict is itself information about the current epistemic state, distinct from both Unknown and Invalid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The derived statement is not directly observed. It is logically produced. ... Observed -> Evidence ... Derived -> Rule + premises ... The fact that a derived value is absent does not mean the underlying condition is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Using a worked compliance-rule example (Version=2.69, RequiredVersion=3.85, Rule ⇒ Compliance=False), shows Zero must preserve the distinction between an observed statement (backed by Evidence) and a derived statement (backed by Rule+premises); absence of a derived value does not mean the underlying condition is absent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What semantic relationships might this sentence fail to express? ... Not expressed \neq False ... Semantically unresolved \neq Semantically absent ... one of the strongest intersections between the Sanskrit lens and Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies Zero to semantic/Pāṇinian parsing: a parsed sentence (e.g. 'Nexus runs version 2.69 on RHEL 9.8') expresses only certain relationships; the parser must not manufacture unexpressed implications (e.g. a specific kernel version); states Not expressed ≠ False and Semantically unresolved ≠ Semantically absent, called one of the strongest intersections between the Sanskrit/semantic lens and Zero.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "secure" may conceal many dimensions ... Which dimensions have been compressed into the word "secure"? ... Abstraction \neq Completeness ... Compression \neq Losslessness ... documents, embeddings, summaries and AI responses are all forms of compression.
b_rows_sample.statement: A high-level word like 'secure' can legitimately compress many sub-dimensions (authentication, authorization, network exposure, vulnerabilities, encryption, dependencies, patch status, configuration) without falsifying them; states the general rules Abstraction ≠ Completeness and Compression ≠ Losslessness, explicitly warning that documents, embeddings, summaries and AI responses are all forms of compression subject to this rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I found no evidence of an undocumented dependency. ... NoEvidence \Rightarrow NoDependency ... Zero rejects that inference. ... AI must be evaluated not only on: What did it extract? but also: What did it fail to discover?
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies Zero to AI evaluation specifically: an AI's 'no evidence found' must not be interpreted as 'no dependency exists'; argues AI systems must be evaluated on what they failed to discover, not only on what they extracted, calling this a fundamentally different evaluation problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dimension discovery / Value determination / Relationship discovery / Derivation / Contradiction detection / Assumption detection / Coverage analysis / Lens variation ... TryBest = Maximize justified knowledge expansion while preserving unresolved boundaries
b_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the instruction 'try your best' into eight concrete sub-disciplines (dimension discovery, value determination, relationship discovery, derivation, contradiction detection, assumption detection, coverage analysis, lens variation), summarized as TryBest = Maximize justified knowledge expansion while preserving unresolved boundaries — explicitly contrasted with just telling an LLM to 'be comprehensive'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every lens must be accompanied by an explicit examination of its blind spots. ... Normal lens: L_i(O) -> D_i ... Zero: Z(L_i,O) -> Boundary(L_i) ... Are there dimensions outside security that affect the security determination?
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Zero as a meta-lens applied to every other lens: a normal lens L_i(O) -> D_i must be paired with Z(L_i,O) -> Boundary(L_i), i.e. every lens must be examined for what it systematically fails to see, what assumptions it makes, and what dimensions lie outside its scope — guarding against e.g. '100 security dimensions found' being mistaken for 'security is comprehensively understood'.

type_signature.domain: a lens L_i applied to observation O

b_rows_sample.anchor: Known gap: d \in D^*\setminus D_t ... Unknown gap: D^*\setminus D_t is itself partially unknown. That is the deepest form of Zero. ... Zero(K_t) may itself contain unresolved structure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a 'known gap' (a specific missing dimension d ∈ D*\D_t is identified) from an 'unknown gap' (D*\D_t is itself partially unknown, i.e. we don't know which dimensions are missing), and generalizes this to recursive uncertainty about unknown dimensions, unknown relationships, and unknown interpretations — concluding Zero(K_t) may itself contain unresolved structure and therefore should not be an ordinary database field.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Mithya 
eq Asat ... Appearing/not independently concrete ≠ nonexistent. ... Representation 
eq Reality ... Model insufficiency 
eq Reality insufficiency ... a powerful Zero safeguard against reification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Translates the philosophical Mithya≠Asat distinction into a Zero safeguard against reification: Representation ≠ Reality, Model insufficiency ≠ Reality insufficiency — a missing dimension in the model does not mean the corresponding aspect of the observed object does not exist, nor does difficulty establishing a statement mean the underlying phenomenon is unreal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Dimension,Value,Context,Time) at minimum. ... NotCurrentlyTrue \Rightarrow WasNeverTrue ... PreviouslyUnknown \Rightarrow PreviouslyNonexistent ... essential for knowledge history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero to temporal knowledge: a Claim must minimally carry (Dimension, Value, Context, Time); Zero must block both 'not currently true ⇒ was never true' and 'previously unknown ⇒ previously nonexistent', framed as essential for knowledge history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not create a `Zero` aggregate. Instead, Zero should influence the ubiquitous language and invariants around knowledge. ... An unassessed dimension must not be interpreted as absent. ... A representation must not be treated as the observed reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: From a DDD standpoint, explicitly rules out a 'Zero' aggregate/entity; instead Zero should shape the ubiquitous language and invariants across Observation/Dimension/Statement/Claim/Value/Evidence/Source/Assessment/Derivation/Conflict/Uncertainty/Coverage/Assumption/Context/Validity/TemporalValidity, listing five example invariants (unassessed≠absent, absence-of-evidence≠evidence-of-absence, unresolved≠false, derived statements retain derivation basis, representation≠observed reality).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZI-01 — Non-collapse of absence: Unknown ≠ Absent ... ZI-06 — Non-collapse of dimension/value: UnknownDimension ≠ UnknownValue ... ZI-10 — Non-collapse of completeness: NoKnownGap ≠ Complete
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a formal ten-item invariant catalog ZI-01..ZI-10 (Non-collapse of: absence Unknown≠Absent; assessment NotAssessed≠LowConfidence; applicability NotApplicable≠Unknown; evidence NoEvidence≠InvalidEvidence; interpretation Unresolved≠False; dimension/value UnknownDimension≠UnknownValue; representation/reality Model≠Reality; state/time PreviouslyUnknown≠PreviouslyAbsent; conflict Conflict≠Invalidity; completeness NoKnownGap≠Complete), flagging ZI-10 as especially important.

b_rows_sample.anchor: |D_t|/|D^*| is not a useful completeness measure. ... Coverage(K,U) = |D_{assessed}|/|D_U| ... provided D_U is explicitly defined. ... Completeness requires a defined universe of discourse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects |D_t|/|D*| as a completeness measure when |D*|=∞ (e.g. 'KnowledgeOS knows 95%' is meaningless globally), and instead proposes a bounded-domain Coverage(K,U) = |D_assessed|/|D_U| valid only when D_U (the universe of discourse) is explicitly defined; states 'completeness requires a defined universe of discourse' as a mathematically important restriction.

type_signature.domain: knowledge state K, bounded domain U

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not: "We don't know anything." Nor: "Knowledge is impossible." It is: "Do not claim more than the represented epistemic state justifies." ... Zero actually enables more aggressive knowledge discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly distinguishes Zero from epistemic pessimism: Zero does not claim knowledge is impossible or that nothing is known; it only forbids claiming more than the represented state justifies — and argues this actually enables MORE aggressive knowledge discovery, since the system can safely mark a dimension unknown and keep searching rather than prematurely declaring non-existence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CURRENT KNOWLEDGE -> ZERO EXAMINATION -> Missing values/Missing dimensions/Hidden assumptions -> More evidence/New lenses/Model challenge -> RE-EVALUATE -> NEW KNOWLEDGE -> Zero again ... Zero is recursive. It does not run once during ingestion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an operational, recursive 'Zero cycle': current knowledge -> Zero examination (missing values / missing dimensions / hidden assumptions) -> remediation (more evidence / new lenses / model challenge) -> re-evaluate -> new knowledge -> Zero again; explicitly states Zero is continuously applicable, not a one-time ingestion-time check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Zero Lens is an epistemic and architectural discipline that examines the boundary of a knowledge state ... while explicitly preventing those conditions from being interpreted as non-existence, falsity, invalidity, irrelevance or completeness. ... Zero is the lens that prevents the domain model from turning epistemic absence into a domain fact. ... ZERO PRINCIPLE: What is not represented is not thereby nonexistent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the document's final formal definition of the Zero Lens, a one-line DDD formulation ('Zero is the lens that prevents the domain model from turning epistemic absence into a domain fact'), and a capstone 'ZERO PRINCIPLE' ('What is not represented is not thereby nonexistent') with a restated set of seven boxed non-collapse rules, concluding Zero is 'not a model of nothingness, but a rigorous discipline for preserving the boundary between what the system knows, what it has not established, and what it has not even yet learned to ask.'

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'zero-lens-non-collapse-discipline' POSSIBLY relates to 'zero-lens-bayesian-gaps' (batch B0018). Note: A general, non-Bayesian-specific formalization of the Zero Lens as an epistemic/architectural discipline (not a domain object) with a ten-item invariant catalog ZI-01..ZI-10, a formal definition, a DDD one-liner, and an operational recursive Zero cycle; distinguished from the indexed zero-lens-bayesian-gaps object, which is specifically the 12 gaps (ZERO-01..12) found by applying Zero to Bayesian cognitive modelling — this document instead states Zero as a general foundational lens for the whole KnowledgeOS model.
